intro:
"Best Cultural Tour in the World 2016" - TourRadar Tour of the Year Awards.

Your Award-Winning adventure, should you choose to accept, is five days of castle-storming, whisky-drinking, ceilidh-dancing and monster-hunting.
Rambling across the Highlands our guides will take you through the very best of what Scotland has to offer, ensuring an unforgettable experience.
Overnight stops include Inverness, the Isle of Skye for two nights and Oban (April - October) or Fort William (November - March)

days.title: Edinburgh to Inverness
optional: Paid attraction tickets at visited sites (Culloden, Clava Cairns, or others) - availability and popularity dependent
days.start_point: 15 Johnston Terrace, Edinburgh, EH1 2PW (Please check in at Castle Rock Hostel from 8.30 for a 9am departure, 09:00)
days.description: Spend the whole day on the Isle of Skye with your guide sharing local folklore and stories. You'll spend far more time hiking than sitting on the bus, climbing up to one of the island's distinctive rock formations where the views stretch out in all directions.

days.title: Inverness to Isle of Skye
included: Cross to Isle of Skye via ferry
days.description: Start by crossing the iconic Forth Bridges, then head out into the Highlands for a forest walk. Along the way, you'll hear stories about clan rebellions and get a feel for what Highland life is really like. Later, there's a swim in Loch Ness if you're up for it, where you can keep an eye out for Nessie while you're in the water. By evening, you'll arrive in Inverness.

days.title: Isle of Skye
included: Hike to distinctive rock formation on Skye
Guided tour of Skye with local folklore
optional: Visit The Old Man of Storr
days.description: Take the ferry off Skye and head toward Fort William, stopping at the Glenfinnan Viaduct (the Harry Potter bridge) and the Bonnie Prince Charlie monument. Then you'll drive through Glen Coe's dramatic landscape before reaching Oban for the night.

days.title: Isle of Skye to Oban
days.description: Head west through beautiful scenery, walking across the Corrieshalloch Gorge and seeing the ancient Torridon mountains. After that, you'll cross the water to reach the Isle of Skye, which becomes your base for the next two nights.

days.title: Argyll - Trossachs National Park - Edinburgh
included: Travel through Argyll and Trossachs National Park
Learn about William Wallace country and Scotland's fight for independence
optional: Visit Kilchurn Castle (Summer months only - entrance fee applies)
See Hairy Coos along the way
days.description: Your last day takes you through Argyll and into the Trossachs National Park, traveling through William Wallace country to learn about Scotland's fight for independence. You'll stop at St. Conan's Kirk, and if you're visiting during summer months, you can see Kilchurn Castle. After that, pick one of three options: Doune Castle, the Wallace Monument, or Bannockburn Battlefield. Then it's time to head back to Edinburgh for your final goodbye. Your guide will adjust things based on weather to get the most out of your experience.

name: Explore Croatia

attributes.name: Group Tour
attributes.tip: Join a group and forge lifelong friendships

attributes.name: Fully Guided
attributes.tip: An experienced guide will be with you for the entire tour

intro:
Discover the true heart and soul of Croatia with an eight-day seaside exploration of some of the Dalmatian Coast’s finest locations. Walk the walls of the Old Town of Dubrovnik, island hop between Vis and Hvar and wander the harbour of Split. Sampling regional specialties and local wine along the way, your Croatian discovery is full of nature and relaxation. See the white stone villages that dot the coast, sample local produce and learn about local history – all on the turquoise waters of the Adriatic. Get ready to explore Croatia’s sparkling highlights and live like the locals.

Please keep your luggage as small and light as possible. You'll be travelling on public transport where storage space is limited. You'll need to be able to lift your luggage into storage racks, walk across cobblestone streets with it and carry it up and down stairs., Don’t let the heat keep you from exploring the world! Summer temperatures can be very high in this region (over 40°C), which can make things uncomfortable. It’s important to use sun protection, wear layers to combat the heat, and drink plenty of water., Hotels in Europe often don't have double beds, but rather two single beds that can be pushed together., On Hvar Island, you’ll stay in private apartments that locals rent out during the summer months. These are in various buildings spread across town, but all are within a 15-minute walk of the main square. The apartments are not hotels, which means there's no reception, room service or daily cleaning service, no televisions or washing machines, but plenty of charm. They differ in layout and facilities, can vary in size, and most don't have air-conditioning or wi-fi. The individual rooms are allocated on a same-gender, twin-share basis. However, the apartments are allocated on a mixed-gender basis, so you’ll be sharing a two or three-room apartment with the other group members. We try to use apartments with rooms that include private facilities. On rare occasions, apartments may only have one bathroom to be shared between the group members staying in the same apartment. In this case, if you've booked a single supplement, you'll be allocated a single room, but you'll share the bathroom with the group., Please be aware that the Croatian coast is very hilly and mountainous, which means lots of steps are an inherent feature of the landscape. Also, stone streets become very slippery when wet. Some people may find Croatia's topography very demanding.

days.title: Dubrovnik
optional: Visit Elafiti Islands (Lopud) - hiking and clean beaches
Dubrovnik Card (1 day local transport and entry to sites) - HRK180
Discover Game of Thrones Filming Locations Urban Adventure - EUR69
Mt Srd Museum of Croatian War of Independence - EUR4
days.description: You'll arrive in Dubrovnik and have a welcome meeting at 6 pm. If your flight gets in early, the Elafiti Islands are right there for some hiking and beach time, or you could do scenic walks around Kolocep. Dinner tonight is when you'll meet the rest of your group.

days.title: Dubrovnik to Hvar
optional: Free exploration of Dubrovnik Old Town
days.description: A morning boat takes you to Vis island in the Adriatic. You'll stop at Green Cave for a swim and snorkel at Blue Cave, then head to Stiniva Beach, a secluded cove with dramatic cliffs and a narrow entrance. Back on Vis by afternoon, you'll have time to lounge on the beaches or check out the island's bars and restaurants in the evening.

days.title: Hvar
optional: Visit UNESCO World Heritage site Stari Grad
Visit local restaurants for traditional dishes
days.description: This morning you'll explore Vis Island's military history with a guide, visiting former military facilities like a rocket launcher base, cannon base, and submarine tunnel from when the island was a restricted zone during Yugoslavia. Later there's a local wine and food tasting at a family property in Komiza. The afternoon is yours to wander through lavender fields, visit St Stephen's Cathedral, or relax on the beach.

days.title: Hvar to Vis
days.description: Get an early start walking the medieval city walls and soaking in views of the Adriatic. Wander through the Old Town at your own pace, checking out Big Onofrio's Fountain and the Franciscan monastery that has a 13th-century pharmacy. Later in the afternoon you'll board a catamaran headed to Hvar and settle in for the evening.

days.title: Vis
included: Military & History Tour of the island
days.description: A local leader takes you on an orientation walk through Hvar this morning. You can spend the rest of the day hitting beaches, visiting the Franciscan Monastery, checking out the UNESCO site at Stari Grad, or wandering through the fishing town of Vrboska. If you're up for a hike, Spanjola Fortress has panoramic views, or just relax on the beach and try local dishes like pasticada with fresh vegetables and cheeses.

days.title: Vis to Split
optional: Grab a drink at a cafe on Riva Promenade
Highlights of Split Urban Adventure - EUR64
St Domnius Cathedral and Tower - EUR10
days.meals: Breakfast, Dinner (Atmospheric dinner at secluded bay)
days.description: Nothing's scheduled today, so you can leave whenever you want. Split and the area around it has lots to explore, like Salona, Trogir, and Sibenik if you feel like day trips. You could also extend your stay here if you want, just reach out to your booking agent beforehand.

days.title: Split
days.description: A morning boat takes you to Split, Croatia's second largest city. A local guide walks you through the town's history, taking you down into the basements under the city, through the Cathedral in Diocletian's Palace, and past Jupiter's Temple. The 1700-year-old ruins of Diocletian's Palace are really something to see. After, you'll relax at a cafe on the Riva Promenade and maybe have dinner by the harbor with your group.

name: Famous 5 - 5 day Tour of Tasmania

attributes.name: Nature & Wildlife
attributes.tip: Explore untamed landscapes teeming with wildlife

attributes.name: Group Tour
attributes.tip: Join a group and forge lifelong friendships

attributes.name: Fully Guided
attributes.tip: An experienced guide will be with you for the entire tour

attributes.name: Medium Intensity
attributes.tip: Travelers should be comfortable with somewhat-demanding activities

intro:
The Famous Tour of Tasmania’s Wild Places, Wildlife and Wild Fun! 

Escape into Tasmania’s pristine wilderness as we travel coast to coast and experience the best of the island over five days. The five day tour of Tasmania starts by heading to the wild West Coast for waterfalls, rainforests, and wildlife. You’ll discover the startling changes of scenery in the alpine wilderness of Cradle Mountain, and the pristine sands of Tasmania’s East Coast, at the Bay of Fires, Wineglass Bay, and Freycinet National Park. Eco-certified and active, this small group tour of Tasmania offers a diversity of outstanding short walks in National Parks to suit your fitness level.

­ 

Starts: Hobart 7.00am

Finishes: Hobart 5.30pm

­

days.title: Hobart to Strahan
included: Visit Russell Falls at Mount Field National Park
Walk amongst world's tallest trees at Mount Field
Stop at Lake St Clair, Cradle Mountain–Lake St Clair National Park
Explore Franklin-Gordon Wild Rivers National Park
landmarks: Cradle Mountain–Lake St Clair National Park
days.start_point: 9 Argyle Street, Hobart Tasmania 7000, Australia (YHA Hobart Central , 07:00 - 07:15)
days.description: Head west from Hobart this morning and you'll hit three national parks in one go. Mount Field comes first with Russell Falls and those massive old trees, then Lake St Clair (Australia's deepest freshwater lake) and Franklin-Gordon Wild Rivers National Park where rainforests meet buttongrass plains. Stop in Queenstown to check out some pioneer history, then it's on to Strahan where you'll stay the night by the harbour.
cities: Franklin Gordon Wild Rivers National Park

days.title: Strahan
included: Guided walk in West Coast wilderness and temperate rainforest (active option)
optional: Gordon River Cruise through Macquarie Harbour and World Heritage Area with visit to Sarah Island and ancient Huon pines (own cost)
days.description: On Tasmania's Wild West Coast you've got options. If you want to be active, there's a guided walk through the rainforest and the Henty Sand Dunes to explore. Not feeling that energetic? The Gordon River Cruise works too, taking you through Macquarie Harbour and past Sarah Island to see those ancient Huon pines (you'll pay separately for this). After that, Ocean Beach is worth seeing, stretching out as Tasmania's longest beach with air that's supposed to be really clean.

days.title: Cradle Mountain to Launceston
included: Walking options in Cradle Mountain National Park alpine environment
Visit Sheffield, the Town of Murals
days.description: Cradle Mountain National Park is a serious hiking spot in Tasmania's Wilderness World Heritage Area. Stop at Ronny Creek to look for wombats, then pick your walking route through the alpine landscape. Marion's Lookout summit or the Dove Lake Circuit are both good choices. Once you're done with the mountains, head through Sheffield (it's called the Town of Murals) on your way to Launceston, one of Australia's oldest cities.
cities: Cradle Mountain-Lake St Clair National Park

days.title: Launceston to St Helens
included: Short walk in Cataract Gorge nature reserve
Walk along Bay of Fires beaches
Learn about cultural significance of Larapuna for Tasmanian Aboriginal people
days.description: Start this morning in Launceston at Cataract Gorge nature reserve for a short walk and spotting wallabies. Then drive east toward the coast and grab lunch in St Helens. The afternoon's for walking along the beaches, including Bay of Fires with its turquoise water. You'll learn about what Larapuna means to Tasmanian Aboriginal people (palawa), then settle into the relaxed vibe of St Helens for the night.

days.title: Freycinet National Park to Hobart
included: Walk to Wineglass Bay beach or lookout
optional: Climb Mt Amos for panoramic vistas
days.description: Freycinet National Park is where you spend today. You can relax on white-sand beaches or walk out to Wineglass Bay beach or its lookout point. If you want a real climb, Mt Amos gives you panoramic views of those pink granite mountains and the coves and bushland below. Stop at Cape Tourville lighthouse overlooking the Tasman Sea. Later, follow the Great Eastern Drive back to Hobart where your Tasmanian trip wraps up.

attributes.name: Group Tour
attributes.tip: Join a group and forge lifelong friendships

attributes.tip: An experienced guide will be with you for the entire tour

attributes.tip: Travelers should be comfortable with somewhat-demanding activities

intro:
See southern Africa's incredible waterfalls, rivers and inland canals on this ten-day overland adventure. Canoe down the lush waterways of the Okavango Delta, watch hippos wallowing along the shores of the Chobe River, take a sunset cruise to spot exotic birdlife, witness the mirage of Makgadikgadi Salt Pans and see the crashing white water of Victoria Falls with free time to customise your experience. After cruising in a mokoro, you’ll spend a night at camp in the remote Okavango wilderness and fall asleep to the uninterrupted sounds of the wild. With early morning game drives to spot Africa’s iconic wildlife and expert guides with all the knowledge, this is set to be an experience of a lifetime.

No two journeys in Africa are identical. Be prepared for travel times to be longer or shorter than advised. Weather and road conditions can change things significantly, so embrace the detours, shortcuts and unforgettable moments along the way., This is an overland trip. That means you’ll be travelling with a group in a purpose-built vehicle, visiting remote communities, setting up your own tent, occasionally roughing it in the bush with no facilities, and getting the best possible views of Africa's iconic wildlife. While the trucks don’t have air conditioning, they do have sliding windows, which let in the breeze and make it even easier to take better snaps of the local wildlife. The drive days can be long, but it’s as much about the journey as the destination, and half the fun is the camaraderie. For more info on this style of travel, see our Africa overland page: https://www.intrepidtravel.com/africa/overland., There will be many early starts, either to make use of the better safari time or to beat the morning traffic on long travel days. Camping out in the amazing Okavango wilderness means digging a bush toilet and going without a shower. It's all part of the delta experience., The day-to-day itinerary features a selection of optional activities. Please note that this list is not exhaustive and is intended only as a guide. Prices are approximate and may change at the discretion of the local provider, and all activities are subject to availability., This trip can be partnered with other adventures into a ‘combo’, which means that some of your fellow travellers may carry on to further destinations at the end of this tour. If you’d like to spend more time in Africa, have a look at some other itineraries this trip combines with: Explore Southern Africa (UBOQC), Johannesburg to Gorillas (UBODC), Johannesburg to Zanzibar (UBOBC) and Johannesburg to Kenya (UBOAC).

days.title: Johannesburg
days.start_point: Pieter Wenning Road, Sandton, Johannesburg, Gauteng 2191, South Africa (Indaba Hotel, 18:00)
days.description: Your South Africa adventure starts in Johannesburg with an evening group meeting at 6 pm. If you're arriving before then, the Apartheid Museum gives important context about the country's history. After everyone gathers, there's an optional dinner where you can start connecting with your travel companions.

days.title: South Africa to Khama Rhino Sanctuary
included: Sunset game drive in open vehicle at Khama Rhino Sanctuary
days.description: You'll cross from South Africa into Botswana and head to Khama Rhino Sanctuary at the edge of the Kalahari Desert. This conservation area protects black and white rhinos along with zebras, giraffes, leopards, ostriches and wildebeest. By evening, join a dusk game drive which gives you the best chance to see rhinos when they're more active.

days.title: Khama Rhino Sanctuary to Maun
days.description: The drive takes you to Maun, which serves as your entry point to the Okavango Delta. This 16,000 square km wetland system is one of Earth's most intricate ecosystems, with hippos, crocodiles, elephants and big cats throughout. You'll have time once you arrive to gather supplies and walk around town before settling in.

days.title: Okavango Delta
included: Walking exploration of lagoons, lakes and streams with local guides
days.description: This is when things get into full adventure mode. You'll climb into a traditional mokoro dugout canoe and travel the Okavango waterways with local guides who propel the boats. Throughout the day, watch for wildlife and birds as you move through lagoons and streams. After hiking with experienced guides through the surrounding area, you'll set up camp on a remote island for the night.

days.title: Okavango Delta
days.description: Start early with a sunrise walk to spot elephants and Cape buffalo with your guide. Back at camp, you'll have breakfast and then the day opens up. Some people opt for another mokoro trip to experience the peaceful river setting, while others prefer to rest or nap in the afternoon heat.

days.title: Okavango Delta to Maun
optional: Scenic helicopter flight over Okavango Delta - From USD250 - USD280
days.description: Pack up camp and paddle back by mokoro to the canoe station, then travel by vehicle to Maun. Once there, you can take an optional helicopter flight that shows the Okavango Delta from above, giving perspective on the waterways and landscape that felt so immense from ground level.

days.title: Maun to Nata
included: Makgadikgadi Salt Pans 4WD excursion through Nata Bird Sanctuary
days.description: An early departure gets you to Nata, a small town near the Makgadikgadi Salt Pans which spread across roughly 12,000 square km. This afternoon, you'll drive through these vast plains in an open-air vehicle, passing through the Nata Bird Sanctuary. The landscape can look surreal with heat waves shimmering across empty terrain, though after rainfall the pans transform into grassland that attracts migratory birds and animals.

days.title: Nata to Chobe National Park
optional: Open safari vehicle morning game drive - BWP580
days.description: You'll head out early toward Chobe National Park, Botswana's oldest park and home to exceptional elephant populations that regularly wade into the Chobe River. Hippos, crocodiles, cheetahs and lions also roam here, plus an impressive range of birds. As you arrive, enjoy a sunset river cruise where wildlife comes to drink and cool off.

days.title: Chobe National Park to Victoria Falls
included: Traditional Zimbabwe Dinner with local community group
optional: Chobe National Park - Open Safari Vehicle Morning Game Drive (BWP580)
days.meals: Dinner (Traditional Zimbabwe dinner hosted by local community group with traditional song and dance performance)
days.description: This morning you have the option to head out on an early safari through Chobe National Park if you want to catch wildlife from a different angle. After that, you'll travel to Victoria Falls and cross into Zimbabwe to settle into camp. You'll have some free time to relax and chat with your local leader about what's coming next. Come evening, you're in for a traditional Zimbabwe dinner put on by a local community group, and they'll perform traditional songs and dances that highlight local youth arts education programs.

qa.question: Are there any restrictions concerning luggage?
qa.answer: As per our trip notes, there are some luggage restrictions on this trip: - The maximum luggage allowance is 20 kg per person. - We recommend packing as lightly as possible. - Backpacks or soft duffel bags are preferred, as large hard-shell suitcases can be difficult to fit, particularly when the truck is at full capacity. - Larger luggage will be stored in the compartments underneath the truck and generally won't be accessible until camp is set up. - You'll also need a smaller day pack or overnight bag, as on some parts of the trip you'll leave your main luggage behind for up to two nights and take only the essentials with you. - Each traveller will have access to a locker on the truck for valuables, and we recommend bringing a small padlock (20-30 mm). If you believe your luggage may exceed these limitations, please let us know and we can seek further guidance from our Operations team.

qa.question: My daughter will be 12 years in Sep. Where does this tour begin and end for planning flight? Which all visas should obtain? Flights / Transfers
qa.answer: For this Okavango Experience tour the minimum age is 15 years old. The Botswana Family Safari with Teenagers starts in Victoria Falls (VFA airport) and ends in Johannesburg (JNB airport). The itinerary includes information on visas.

qa.question: I'd be very interested in the upgrade options for hotel rooms on this trip (I would've been in South Africa for a month on other tours and trips by this stage and would prefer a hotel rooms where possible!) Also, what kind of luggage can I bring along on this tour? I will have at least one big suitcase with me and maybe a smaller one as well.
qa.answer: We do not offer the ability to directly upgrade the accommodations on this tour, as the majority of this tour is camping and part of a group experience. Although, there may be the occasional night stop when we stay on the grounds of a hotel or at a campsite, which may also have rooms/cabins available. In this case, there may be a choice of camping or upgrading to a room. Rooms cost approximately USD 40-100 per room per night for a twin room and cannot be pre-booked. Standards of these rooms vary greatly, and we recommend viewing the room before purchasing the night's accommodation. The day-by-day itinerary advises when upgrades may be possible (subject to availability). If you're looking for a tour that does not include camping, I would consider a Comfort or Premium style tour. name: China Highlights

attributes.name: Ancient Wonders
attributes.tip: Walk among ruins, temples, and timeless landmarks

attributes.name: Group Tour
attributes.tip: Join a group and forge lifelong friendships

attributes.name: Fully Guided
attributes.tip: An experienced guide will be with you for the entire tour

intro:
Get a taste of historical China on this culture-stuffed adventure. Travel from Shanghai to Beijing, taking in iconic attractions such as the Great Wall of China (one of the Seven Wonders of the World!) and the Terracotta Warriors along the way. In between the well-known sights, you'll delve beneath the surface, visit the ancient town and traditional garden in Wuxi City, snack through the Muslim Quarter in Xi’an and watch the sun setting on the Great Wall. In just eight days, you’ll have the perfect introduction to the highlights of China.

Be prepared for some long travel days as you’ll need to cover over 2000 km to see China's main highlights in this 8-day adventure, without a flight., This trip packs a lot in over a short amount of time, so it’s highly recommended you spend some extra time in Shanghai and Beijing before or after your trip to experience more of what these great cities have to offer., As a short, city-based trip, there isn't a lot of time to experience China's beautiful natural landscapes or get further off the beaten track. If you have more time to explore, consider China Experience (CBSE), or Beijing to Hong Kong Adventure (CBSJ)., China’s world-class sites and experiences draw large numbers of local and international travellers. We recommend a little patience and comfortable shoes as you may need to wait before entering the more popular locations on your itinerary.

days.title: Shanghai
optional: Shanghai Propaganda Poster Art Centre visit
Leader-led walking tour of the Bund
days.description: You'll arrive in Shanghai and meet up with your group at 4 pm. If you get there earlier, you've got time to walk around and see how the city mixes sleek modern buildings with older neighborhoods. After the welcome meeting, head out with your leader for a walk along the Bund to catch the city lights reflecting off the water at night. The rest of the evening is open for you to try different restaurants and food stands scattered throughout the city.

days.title: Shanghai to Wuxi
included: Leader-led walking tour of Huishan Ancient Town Scenic Area
days.description: Take a 30-minute bullet train to Wuxi in the morning, a town that's kept its historical character while modernizing. Once there, your leader takes you through Huishan Ancient Town Scenic Area where you'll see old structures and cultural landmarks. Wander the historic streets in the Huishan neighborhood, then spend time at Jichang Garden, which is one of the country's better traditional gardens. You'll head back to Shanghai by afternoon, leaving your evening free. Grab a drink at one of the rooftop bars overlooking the Bund if you like the view.

days.title: Shanghai to Xi'an
included: Muslim Quarter Walking Tour and Snack Sampling
days.description: Head outside Xi'an to see the Terracotta Warriors, an archaeological site that's really significant. You'll learn about the thousands of clay soldiers, horses, and chariots that Emperor Qin Shi Huangdi had made over 2,000 years ago. Each statue is different with its own clothes, height, and face details. After you return to Xi'an in the afternoon, your evening is completely free. Consider checking out the Tang Paradise walking street near the Big Wild Goose Pagoda if you want to explore local nightlife.

days.title: Xi'an
days.description: Board the bullet train this morning heading to Xi'an, the old imperial capital and where the Silk Road started. Your leader walks you through the city, passing the Bell and Drum Towers on the way. Next, you'll go into the Muslim Quarter where shops and market stalls line the streets around the Great Mosque. Try food from the vendors selling local snacks and street specialties. For dinner, you'll sample regional dishes like pao mo, hand-pulled noodles, and grilled meat skewers that the area is known for.

days.title: Xi'an to Great Wall
optional: Sunset hike to the Great Wall
days.description: This is a longer travel day, so grab some snacks and get comfortable for the high-speed train ride to Beijing. You'll watch the landscape shift from farmland and small villages to larger industrial areas as you travel. When you arrive, a private vehicle takes you out into the countryside to a family-run guesthouse positioned near the Great Wall. A short hike to the Wall at sunset is really worth doing, and you'll get to see one of the major wonders of the world on your first night there.

days.title: Great Wall
included: Visit to Great Wall of China Jinshanling section
Approximately 2-hour hike along the Great Wall
days.description: This morning you'll head to central Beijing and walk through Tiananmen Square, a massive open plaza at the heart of the city. It's surrounded by important buildings including the Gate of Heavenly Peace, Mao's Mausoleum, and the Great Hall of the People. From there, you'll enter the Forbidden City, an enormous complex built over 500 years ago. Walking through the halls and courtyards gives you a sense of what life was like for the imperial court. The afternoon is yours to do what you want, and you could visit the Temple of Heaven or other sites. Your trip ends with a farewell dinner featuring Beijing duck, where you'll celebrate with everyone else on the tour.

days.title: Beijing
days.description: Your China trip ends today with no scheduled activities. Beijing has plenty to explore if you want to spend the day on your own terms. If you're interested in staying longer, reach out to your booking agent about extending your stay for a few extra days.

days.title: Beijing
days.description: Today you'll spend time on the Great Wall itself, one of the world's most recognizable structures. You'll hike along an original section that doesn't get as many visitors, so it'll feel pretty quiet and peaceful. The 2-hour hike takes you along the top of the wall as it winds through the hills and valleys stretching out into the distance. The wall was built centuries ago to defend against invasions from the north. After you finish hiking, you'll head back to Beijing for the night.

There are usually a variety of meat-free dishes on menus, including vegetables, tofu, and egg-based meals, and your trip leader will be able to recommend local favourites.

name: Kenya Wildlife Safari

attributes.name: Safari
attributes.tip: Track iconic wildlife on unforgettable game drives

attributes.name: Group Tour
attributes.tip: Join a group and forge lifelong friendships

attributes.name: Fully Guided
attributes.tip: An experienced guide will be with you for the entire tour

intro:
Immerse yourself in the animal kingdom on this eight-day trip through Kenya. Veer off the beaten track to seek out elephants, hippos, leopards and lions against the impressive backdrop of the Great Rift Valley and Lake Naivasha. Then, staying in the world-famous Maasai Mara, deepen your understanding of Kenyan culture by experiencing tribal life in Loita Hills as you’re welcomed into the homes of the Maasai warriors and their proud village community. Take early morning game drives, optional hot air balloon rides and join a cooking class to learn how to make some traditional fare. Join this perspective-shifting journey of unforgettable moments and memorable wildlife encounters.

This is an overland trip. That means you’ll be travelling with a group in a purpose-built vehicle, visiting remote communities, setting up your own tent and getting the best possible views of the Big Five. While the trucks don’t have air conditioning, they do have drop-down windows, which let in the breeze and make it even easier to take spectacular snaps of the local wildlife. The drive days can be long, but it’s as much about the journey as the destination, and half the fun is the camaraderie. For more info on this style of travel, see our Africa overland page: https://www.intrepidtravel.com/africa/overland, In Loita Hills, you'll be staying in a secure bush camp with basic facilities, heated bucket showers in the morning, and no WiFi, but the rewards of experiencing Maasai culture should more than make up for the lack of creature comforts., As the early bird catches the worm, the early camper sights the animals. There will be many early starts either to make use of the better safari time or beat the morning traffic on long travel days.

days.title: Nairobi
optional: Nairobi Experience Urban Adventure (4-hour city tour including lunch at local restaurant)
Optional group dinner with travel companions
days.description: You'll arrive in Nairobi and meet up with your group at 6 pm. If your flight gets in earlier, there's an optional 'Nairobi Experience' tour where you can walk around the city and get a feel for things. After the welcome meeting, you can grab dinner with the other travelers if you'd like.

days.title: Nairobi to Lake Nakuru National Park
days.meals: Dinner (Shared meal featuring dishes from cooking class)
days.description: Drive northwest through the Great Rift Valley this morning, passing by Lake Naivasha and Lake Elementaita on your way to Lake Nakuru National Park. Once you arrive, head to a nearby village with your leader for a cooking class. You'll prepare dishes together and come back to share what you made with everyone over dinner.

days.title: Lake Nakuru National Park to Lake Naivasha
included: Overland Vehicle Safari in Lake Nakuru National Park
days.description: Get up early for breakfast, then drive into Lake Nakuru National Park for a game drive in the overland vehicle. You'll have chances to spot rhinos and other wildlife throughout the morning. After returning to camp for lunch, you'll head over to Lake Naivasha, one of the few freshwater lakes in the rift valley where hippos and lots of birds hang out.

days.title: Lake Naivasha
optional: Hell's Gate National Park Game Drive (USD 65)
Crater Lake Game Sanctuary Game Walk with entrance fee (USD 50)
days.description: Take a boat across Lake Naivasha this morning with the Eburru volcanic mountains as your backdrop. You'll watch for hippos, kingfishers, and fish eagles on the water. The afternoon is yours to fill with optional activities like visiting Hell's Gate National Park or renting a bike to explore the area around the lake.

days.title: Lake Naivasha to Loita Hills Maasai Village
included: Cultural Talk and Maasai Village Visit
Maasai Warrior Song and Dance Performance
days.description: Leave Lake Naivasha and stop in Narok to pick up supplies for meals, then continue to Loita Hills. When you arrive at Tepesua Village, traditional Maasai warriors will greet you with songs and dances. You'll learn about Maasai warrior training, visit a community village that supports Maasai widows, and spend the evening by the fire talking with the warriors.

days.title: Loita Hills to Maasai Mara National Reserve
included: 4WD Safari in Maasai Mara National Reserve
days.description: Travel from Loita Hills toward Maasai Mara, with the final 5 kilometers being rough and dusty or muddy depending on recent weather. Set up camp and grab lunch, then hop into 4WDs for an afternoon game drive. Keep an eye out for lions, leopards, cheetahs, wildebeest, buffalo, elephants, and rhinos as you explore.

days.title: Maasai Mara National Reserve
included: 4WD Safari in Maasai Mara National Reserve
optional: Hot air balloon ride over Maasai Mara at sunrise with bush breakfast (from USD 500)
days.description: If you book the hot air balloon option, you'll head out early for a sunrise flight over the Mara with a safety briefing first. After landing, enjoy a bush breakfast with other balloon passengers. Later, join a full-day 4WD game drive with local guides who know where to find wildlife in different parts of the reserve.

days.title: Maasai Mara to Nairobi
days.description: Head back to Nairobi today and get dropped at a central hotel where you can leave whenever you're ready. If you want to stay longer in Kenya, let your booking agent know ahead of time so they can help arrange accommodation and activities for extra days.

qa.question: Can you please tell me what type of sleeping accommodations are included with this tour? We aren't interested in participation camping but are open to sleeping in tents that have en-suite bathrooms :)
qa.answer: For the Kenya Wildlife Safari the accommodations are: Camping (with facilities) (5 nights), Hotel (1 night), Camping (with basic facilities) (1 night). Accommodation on this trip is mainly in two-person canvas dome tents with camping mattresses supplied. Campsites do have facilities, but they usually aren't to the same standard you would find in Western countries. For example, the bathroom facilities can be very basic. Toilet paper is rarely provided, and shower facilities can be as simple as a hose pipe spurting out cold water. Wild camps have no facilities at all. As you're not interested in the participation camping style, we would suggest East Africa Highlights - accommodations are Hotel (3 nights), Lodge (2 nights), Permanent Tented Camp (4 nights) and your safari tent is equipped with an ensuite, solar power, and private veranda. name: Mexico Unplugged

attributes.name: City & Culture
attributes.tip: Immerse yourself in rich history and local traditions

attributes.name: Group Tour
attributes.tip: Join a group and forge lifelong friendships

attributes.name: Fully Guided
attributes.tip: An experienced guide will be with you for the entire tour

intro:
Discover the heart of Mexico's Aztec, Zapotec, Maya and Spanish cultures on this 15-day adventure. Start by experiencing the mix of influences that make up Mexico City, then head out to taste pasita in Puebla, visit the markets of Oaxaca and learn about the textile traditions of Teotitlan del Valle. Immerse yourself in pre-Hispanic culture in San Cristobal de las Casas and unravel the magnificent mystery of ancient civilisations during guided tours in Chichen Itza and Palenque. Sample the incredible cuisine along the way, sharing meals with the communities of San Pedro Tlahuac and Piste, then relax beachside at Playa del Carmen. This is the ideal introduction to one of North America's most colourful and exciting destinations.

This trip involves some long days of travel by private and local transport. While this can be tiring, it's also a fantastic way to rub shoulders with the locals and get under the skin of a place., Mexico's climate is sultry and tropical, so can get really hot and humid. Wear loose clothing and make sure you stay hydrated, especially while out on walking tours. You can also expect to walk a lot and the terrain is rarely flat. Make sure to pack a jacket for the higher altitude cities like Mexico City, Puebla and San Cristóbal de las Casas.

days.title: Mexico City
optional: Palace of Fine Arts (Palacio de Bellas Artes) entrance fee - MXN80
National Museum of Anthropology entrance fee - MXN90
Frida Kahlo Museum entrance fee - MXN250
Torre Latino 360° Lookout entrance fee - MXN170
Diego Rivera Murals in the Mural Museum entrance fee - MXN35
days.description: You'll arrive in Mexico City and head to a welcome meeting at 6 pm. If you get there early, the Zocalo is worth checking out to see the Aztec ruins and colonial architecture, or you could just relax in one of the city's parks instead.

days.title: Mexico City
included: Leader-led orientation walk through Mexico City
Leader-led taco crawl with local leader
days.meals: Lunch (Taco crawl around town with local leader - tacos al pastor and other street food treats)
days.description: Your leader will take you on an orientation walk to see the Metropolitan Cathedral, Zocalo, National Palace, Bellas Artes, and Paseo de la Reforma. Around lunch, you'll join a taco crawl with your local leader, trying tacos al pastor and other street food. The afternoon and evening are yours to explore Plaza Garibaldi, wander around on your own, or grab cocktails at some of the trendier bars.

days.title: Mexico City - Puebla
included: Community visit to San Pedro Tlahuac with local family
Trajinera ride and chinampa agriculture learning experience
Local meal prepared with ingredients from chinampas
days.meals: Lunch (Delicious local meal prepared by community with ingredients from the chinampas)
days.description: You'll head to San Pedro Tlahuac for a cultural exchange with a local family. There's a trajinera ride, and you'll learn about chinampa agriculture before sharing a meal made with local ingredients. Later, you travel to Puebla where your leader guides you through an orientation walk and takes you to La Pasita bar to try pasita liqueur.

days.title: Puebla
optional: Santo Domingo Church and Rosary Chapel entrance fee - MXN20
San Pedro Art Museum entrance fee - MXN45
days.description: This day is free to explore Puebla on your own. The city has many well-kept churches and colonial buildings to see. You could visit Santo Domingo Church and the Rosary Chapel, or take a trip out to the Great Pyramid of Cholula, which has eight kilometers of tunnels and views of Popocatepetl Volcano. Local markets are good for browsing handicrafts too.

days.title: Puebla - Oaxaca
included: Visit to Mercado 20 de Noviembre fresh food market
Classic Oaxacan lunch at market tables
days.meals: Lunch (Classic Oaxacan lunch at Mercado 20 de Noviembre with fresh guacamole, salsa, and tortillas)
days.description: You'll take a local bus to Oaxaca, a colonial town with beautiful arcades and colorful markets. Your leader gives you an orientation walk and takes you to Mercado 20 de Noviembre to pick up fresh ingredients. After that, you'll sit down for a classic Oaxacan lunch with guacamole, salsa, and tortillas. The rest of the day is for walking the cobblestone streets, having mezcal in the squares, or checking out the arts scene.

days.title: Oaxaca
optional: Monte Alban archaeological site entrance fee - MXN90
Santo Domingo Cultural Centre entrance fee - MXN85
Mitla, Teotitlan weaving town & mezcal distillery tour - MXN850
days.description: You have choices for how to spend this day in Oaxaca. Monte Alban is an option if you want to see pre-Columbian temples with terraces, dams, canals, and pyramids. Or you could take a cooking class to learn how to prepare local dishes. In the evening, you'll head out for dinner with other travelers to experience the town's lively vibe.

days.title: Oaxaca - Tehuantepec
included: Arbol del Tule (Tree of Tule) visit
Teotitlan del Valle town visit with artisan weaving demonstrations
days.description: After leaving Oaxaca by private transfer, you'll stop at the Arbol del Tule, which holds a record for having the stoutest tree trunk in the world. You'll visit Teotitlan del Valle to see handcrafted textiles made by artisans, then tour a mezcal distillery to sample the smoky liquor before arriving in Tehuantepec for the evening.

days.title: Tehuantepec - San Cristobal de las Casas
included: Leader-led tour of San Cristobal de las Casas
days.description: You travel by road to San Cristobal de las Casas, arriving in the early afternoon. This highland town sits in a green Chiapas valley surrounded by pine trees. Your leader will take you around town and point out important spots. The evening is free, and your leader can suggest dinner places.

days.title: San Cristobal de las Casas
included: Iglesia de San Juan church visit
optional: Sumidero Canyon boat excursion (entrance and transport) - MXN565
days.description: In the morning, you'll visit San Juan Chamula to explore the Iglesia de San Juan, which has a pine-covered floor and incense-filled air where shamans do traditional cleansings. You'll browse the colorful markets outside selling local handicrafts. The rest of the day is free, and your leader can help you arrange an optional boating trip in the Sumidero Canyon if you're interested.

days.title: Palenque - Merida
days.description: You travel by private vehicle to Merida, the capital of the Yucatan region. On the way, you stop in Campeche, a harbor town with colonial remnants. Your leader walks you through its fortified center, and lunch is included. Then you continue to Merida, founded in 1542 on the site of the ancient Maya city Tho. Your leader does an orientation walk when you arrive, and then you have free time to settle in.

days.title: Merida
optional: Fernando Garcia Ponce-Macay Contemporary Art Museum entrance fee - Free
Uxmal Ruins tour (inc. shared transport and guide) - MXN1400
Celestun Bird Sanctuary tour (inc. shared transport and guide) - MXN1300
days.description: You have options for exploring the Yucatan today. There's an optional tour to Uxmal ruins, about an hour's drive away, where you'll see the Pyramid of the Soothsayer and other important buildings. Another choice is Celestun Bird Sanctuary to see flocks of flamingos and migratory birds. Or you can stay in Merida and explore at your own pace.

days.title: Merida - Playa del Carmen
included: Chichen Itza archaeological site guided tour
Piste community traditional Maya family lunch
days.meals: Lunch (Traditional Maya family lunch in Piste community with Yucatecan specialties)
days.description: You travel to Playa del Carmen by private vehicle with a stop at Chichen Itza for a guided tour of the famous Maya ruins, including El Castillo pyramid, the large ball court, and the Well of Sacrifice. Lunch happens in the nearby Piste community where you'll try Yucatecan specialties and talk with locals. After arriving in Playa del Carmen, your leader gives a quick orientation walk, then you relax with a margarita and watch the sunset. The group might gather for one last dinner together.

days.title: Playa del Carmen
optional: Dos Ojos Cenote fresh water rock pool entrance fee with snorkelling gear & life jacket included - MXN550
Playa del Carmen ferry to Cozumel (round-trip ticket) - MXN500
days.description: There are no planned activities on this final day. If you have time before leaving, you could take an optional tour to Dos Ojos Cenote for a swim in the turquoise freshwater cenote, or take a local ferry to explore Cozumel. Additional accommodation in Playa del Carmen can be set up if you need it.

name: Cape Town to Victoria Falls Adventure

attributes.name: Nature & Wildlife
attributes.tip: Explore untamed landscapes teeming with wildlife

attributes.name: Group Tour
attributes.tip: Join a group and forge lifelong friendships

attributes.name: Fully Guided
attributes.tip: An experienced guide will be with you for the entire tour

intro: This 18-day journey through four African countries hits the highlights and is perfect for the adventurer who wants to discover the region’s diversity. Explore the Okavango Delta by traditional mokoro canoe, marvel at some of the highest sand dunes in the world in the Namib Desert, and meet the San Bushmen of the Kalahari. Your knowledgeable CEO (Chief Experience Officer) will take care of the hassles and planning while you recharge in hotels, local lodges, and camps for an unforgettable cultural experience you'll forever treasure.

days.title: Cape Town
optional: South African Wine Tour and Tasting
days.description: You'll arrive in Cape Town and meet your CEO and group to get things started. If you've booked the optional wine tour, keep in mind it kicks off early the next morning, so you might want to arrive the day before to settle in and rest.

days.title: Cape Town to Lambert's Bay
included: !Khwa ttu San Culture and Education Centre
landmarks: !Khwa ttu San Culture and Education Centre
days.description: Head up the west coast toward Lambert's Bay, stopping at the !Khwa ttu San Culture and Education Centre along the way. Once there, you'll participate in an included wine tasting where you learn how to evaluate wines and match them with food. If you're interested, you can visit Bird Island or walk around the town on your own.

days.title: Lambert's Bay to Orange River
days.description: The drive takes you north through dry, remote landscapes before crossing into Namibia. You'll reach the Orange River in the mid-afternoon and have the rest of the evening to relax by the riverbank and get settled.

days.title: Orange River to Keetmanshoop
days.description: Start by heading to Fish River Canyon to see this dramatic natural formation. After that, continue north through striking Namibian terrain toward Keetmanshoop, then stop in the afternoon to check out Giant's Playground and Quiver Tree Forest.

days.title: Keetmanshoop to Namib Desert
days.description: Begin early and travel north through dramatic landscapes heading toward Sesriem. You'll arrive in the late afternoon at the entrance to the Namib Desert, where massive red sand dunes tower above the surrounding area.

days.title: Namib Desert
days.description: Spend the day exploring Sossusvlei, a clay pan surrounded by some of the world's largest sand dunes reaching up to 300 meters high. Climb Dune 45 and visit Sesriem Canyon. You'll have free time to wander the dunes, and there's an optional visit to Deadvlei if you want to go.

days.title: Namib Desert to Swakopmund
days.description: Cross the Namib Desert for hours with beautiful views the whole way before reaching the coast. Stop in Solitaire, a small quirky spot with a gas station and coffee shop, then pass through Walvis Bay. By evening you'll be in Swakopmund, where you'll stay for two nights and can try sandboarding, skydiving, or other activities.

days.title: Swakopmund
days.description: You have the full day to explore Swakopmund. Options include sandboarding, skydiving, scenic flights, or just walking around to see the lunar landscapes and unusual rock formations that give the town its character.

days.title: Swakopmund to Etosha National Park
included: Etosha National Park Wildlife Safari Drive
days.description: Head east into Namibia's interior, passing through lunar-like terrain with views of Spitzkoppe in the distance. By afternoon you'll enter Etosha National Park for a safari drive where you might spot lions, giraffes, elephants, rhinos, and antelopes. After sunset, animals come to drink at the watering holes near your camp.

days.title: Etosha National Park
included: Etosha National Park Wildlife Safari Drive
days.description: Spend another day on safari drives in your vehicle. Watch for the wide range of animals that Etosha is famous for, from large herds to smaller species.

days.title: Etosha National Park to Windhoek
days.description: Leave Etosha and drive south through the Namibian countryside toward Windhoek, arriving early in the afternoon. Stop for an included lunch at Penduka Village Restaurant & Shop, a G Adventures-supported spot. Spend the rest of the afternoon exploring this German-influenced capital.

days.title: Windhoek to Ghanzi
days.description: Cross from Namibia into Botswana and head east into the Kalahari Desert toward Ghanzi. You'll take a guided walk with the San Bushmen to see how they've adapted to this harsh environment. Stay at Dqae Qare San Lodge & Camp, spend time around the fire learning about their culture and history, and know your visit supports the community directly.

days.title: Ghanzi to Maun
days.description: Travel through the northern Kalahari Desert, a severe but beautiful landscape, then arrive in Maun. Grab any supplies you need before heading into the delta area. There's an optional helicopter ride available if you want to pre-book it during your free time.

days.title: Okavango Delta
days.description: Spend a full day in the Okavango Delta doing wildlife walks, birding, and traditional mokoro canoe trips. Local polers will teach you bush skills as you navigate the delta. After a safari vehicle drive to the dock and a 1-2 hour mokoro ride deep into the water, you'll reach camp. In the evening, watch a traditional Tswana dance.

days.title: Okavango Delta to Nata
days.description: Watch the sunrise in the delta, then head back to Maun by mokoro. Once there, pick up your luggage and have lunch before continuing east toward Nata. You can optionally do a sunset safari drive or bush walk to see animals at local watering holes, possibly including elephants drinking at night.

days.title: Nata to Kasane
days.description: Travel to Kasane, which sits just outside Chobe National Park, home to the largest elephant population in Southern Africa. There's an option to pre-book a sunset boat cruise on the Chobe River if you're interested.

days.title: Kasane to Victoria Falls
included: Border crossing from Botswana to Zimbabwe
optional: Chobe National Park early morning safari drive

days.meals: Breakfast, Lunch (Lunch at Lusumpuko Women's Club)
days.description: If you're up early, join the optional safari drive through Chobe National Park before crossing into Zimbabwe. The morning gives you a chance to spot wildlife in their natural habitat. Around midday, you'll have lunch at Lusumpuko Women's Club, where you can grab a meal and chat with locals. After that, you've got free time to do what appeals to you most. Some people head straight to Victoria Falls for a close-up look at the water and mist. Others prefer seeing it from the air on a helicopter ride, which gives you a totally different perspective of the falls and the gorge. By afternoon, you can pick your adventure. There's the option to walk right up to the falls themselves, or if you want something more intense, try whitewater rafting on the Zambezi River. If you're feeling bold, bungee jumping off the bridge is another possibility. The choice really depends on how much adrenaline you're after.

intro: Nature called you to Costa Rica — now here you are, suspended in the jungle canopy, locking eyes with a curious monkey. This action-packed tour of Costa Rica’s highlights is perfect for the adventurer with limited time who wants to explore the region’s diversity. Get your adrenaline pumping, follow a trail to the base of a waterfall, explore Manuel Antonio National Park, or relax on a beach — your CEO will help you find the secluded spots only the locals know.

days.title: San José
days.description: You'll arrive in San José whenever works for your flight. There's nothing scheduled during the day, so take time to settle in at your hotel or explore the city on your own. In the evening, you'll meet up with your CEO and the rest of the group at a welcome meeting to get acquainted and hear what's coming up over the next week.

days.title: San José to La Fortuna
optional: Hike nature trails in La Fortuna area
days.description: Head out early and drive toward Sarapiquí, stopping at La Paz Waterfall along the way to check out the scenery. Then you'll reach Mi Cafecito Community Coffee Plantation where you'll learn about the G for Good project and taste some local coffee products. After that, continue driving to the Arenal region. You'll have the afternoon free to do what you want, whether that's hiking trails, taking a dip at La Fortuna waterfall, or soaking in the natural hot springs nearby.

days.title: La Fortuna
optional: Hot Springs Soak (36 USD per person)
Stand-up Paddle Board on Lake Arenal
Gravity Falls Waterfall Jumping (133 USD per person)
La Fortuna Waterfall Swim (20 USD per person)
days.description: This is your day to do whatever appeals to you in La Fortuna. Spend time on outdoor activities, looking for wildlife, or just taking in the natural surroundings. The afternoon and evening are yours to fill, and many people choose to head to the hot springs to relax after being active all day.

days.title: La Fortuna to Monteverde
days.description: Travel by van and boat through the Costa Rican landscape as you head toward Monteverde. You'll cross Lake Arenal and then drive into the mountains. Once you arrive in the cloud forest, a guide will take you on a night walk to show you the jungle comes alive after dark. Then you'll settle in for the evening in this quieter, nature-focused area.

days.title: Monteverde
optional: Hanging Bridges Monteverde (56 USD per person)
Monteverde Horseback Riding (55 USD per person)
CASEM Coop Visit (14-25 USD per person)
El Trapiche Tour Monteverde (52 USD per person)
Santa Elena Cloud Forest Guided Tour (49 USD per person)

days.description: Take a free day to explore the cloud forest however you'd like. If you're looking for adventure, you can zipline through the canopy, walk across suspended bridges high up in the trees, or go horseback riding through the hills. Or just wander around and take in the scenery on your own.

days.title: Monteverde to Quepos
days.description: Drive to Quepos on the Pacific Coast near Manuel Antonio National Park. The town has a fun, laid-back surf town vibe with plenty going on. You can relax on the beach, swim, try fishing, go kayaking, or book a sailing trip out on the water. In the evening, head out and explore the local restaurants and nightlife.

days.title: Quepos
optional: Kayaking through mangroves (80-90 USD per person)
Whitewater Rafting Manuel Antonio (95-130 USD per person)
days.description: Your entrance to Manuel Antonio National Park is included today. After that, you've got free time to do what interests you. Some people swim in the Pacific, others paddle through the mangrove forests by kayak, and plenty of folks just hang out on the beach and soak up the sun.

days.title: Quepos to San José
days.description: Start with an optional morning at the beach or a sailing trip if you'd like (you can pre-book the Manuel Antonio Catamaran Tour before your trip starts). Later, you'll head back toward the capital. Plan to leave in the afternoon or early evening so you have time for a final swim or breakfast depending on your flight time.

qa.question: Is Costa Rica hiking friendly? If yes, do you also offer hiking itineraries?
qa.answer: We don't offer any customised tours, but we can run one of the tours selected from our website as a private departure for your group. Typical private group size is 8 or more. For most of our departures the minimum number of people required to run a private departure is 8 (with some exceptions). We can make some enhancements to some of our tours, but there are limitations and restrictions. If you don't meet the minimum of 8 travellers, we suggest to book on a public departure. Our public departures do not require a minimum number of travellers to run as we offer these as guaranteed departures. For private departures for groups with less than 8 passengers, the price will increase as the group size decreases.

name: Volcano Trail: Waves & Local Ways

attributes.name: City & Culture
attributes.tip: Immerse yourself in rich history and local traditions

attributes.name: Group Tour
attributes.tip: Join a group and forge lifelong friendships

attributes.name: Fully Guided
attributes.tip: An experienced guide will be with you for the entire tour

intro: From the laid-back vibes and waves of the Pacific Coast to tropical rainforests alive with jungle melodies, take the road less travelled on this trip through Guatemala, Honduras, El Salvador, Nicaragua, and Costa Rica with other travellers your own age. This is one of our most exciting trips, filled with breathtaking scenery and a chance to experience local culture with a two-night community guesthouse stay on the island of Ometepe. Enjoy a blend of public and private transportation, which not only keeps costs down but also gives you a chance to really meet the locals.

days.title: Antigua Guatemala
days.description: You'll arrive in Antigua from Guatemala City airport, which takes about an hour. After meeting your CEO and other travelers, head into El Barrio to check out the local marketplace filled with bars and pubs. This Spanish colonial city is a UNESCO World Heritage Site surrounded by volcanoes and colorful markets, so there's plenty to see as you settle in.

days.title: Antigua Guatemala to Copán Ruinas
days.description: Spend the full day traveling from Antigua across the border into Honduras, heading to Copán Ruinas. You'll arrive in the evening at this charming colonial highland town that sits along a river in the coffee-growing region. The Mayan ruins here are among the most important in the Mayan world, with some of the most detailed carvings you'll find.

days.title: Copán Ruinas
optional: Visit Copán ruins (25 USD per person)
Luna Jaguar Hot Springs visit (50 USD per person)
days.description: This is your free day in Copán to do what interests you. Walk through the ruins with local guides who can explain the detailed Mayan carvings that are over 1,000 years old, or if you want something more relaxing, head to hidden jungle hot springs in the countryside for a soak.

days.title: Copán Ruinas to Suchitoto
days.description: Cross the border into El Salvador and travel to Suchitoto, a colonial town. While you're here, try pupusas, which are the local Salvadorian specialty and really worth tasting. The town has a nice mix of history and local culture to explore.

days.title: Suchitoto to La Libertad Region
days.description: You've got free time to walk through Granada's busy markets and past colonial buildings and museums, or hire a horse and carriage if you prefer. Grab a meal on the calzada, the pedestrian street that goes from downtown to Lake Nicaragua. If you're interested, there are options to kayak around the isletas, swim in Laguna de Apoyo, or walk through the forest at Mombacho Volcano.

days.title: La Libertad Region
optional: Eat fresh ceviche at fish market
days.description: After a free morning in Suchitoto, head toward the coast in the La Libertad region. The sunsets at these small surfing towns are really great, so grab a cold drink and take in the atmosphere once you arrive.

days.title: La Libertad Region to León
days.description: Travel to Granada and walk around to see its colorful colonial buildings. Later, enjoy a group night out. The city has colonial charm and is surrounded by active volcanoes and lakes, plus there are many easy day trips available if you want to venture out.

days.title: León to Granada
days.description: Take a ferry back to the mainland and cross into Costa Rica. You'll finish the day in Monteverde, up at 1,400 meters in the cloudforest air. The Monteverde and Santa Elena Cloud Forest Reserves have tons of wildlife like sloths, monkeys, kinkajous, tapirs and large cats. More orchid species grow here than anywhere else.

days.title: Granada
optional: Swim in Laguna de Apoyo (35 USD per person)
Masaya Volcano Day Excursion (40 USD per person)
Mi Museo Cultural Museum (5 USD per person)
days.description: You've got a free day in these laid-back beach towns, so choose what sounds good. Try a surf lesson, eat fresh ceviche at the fish market in La Libertad, check out the Tamanique waterfalls, or just relax with a beer and enjoy the beach vibe.

days.title: Granada to Isla de Ometepe
included: Puesta del Sol Community Guesthouse Stay
days.meals: Dinner (Dinner provided in host family home)
days.description: Start early for a full day of travel by land and boat to Nicaragua. You'll take a private vehicle and boat, crossing the El Salvador-Nicaragua border. By evening you'll arrive in colonial León for a brief orientation walk to get your bearings.

days.title: Isla de Ometepe
included: Puesta del Sol Community Guesthouse Stay
optional: Climb Volcano Concepción (45 USD per person)
Ometepe Island Cultural and Pre-Columbian Petroglyphs Tour (45 USD per person)
Walk or kayak in Charco Verde reserve
Swim at Ojo de Agua (10-15 USD per person)
Visit museum of indigenous artifacts in Altagracia
days.meals: Breakfast (Breakfast provided in host family home), Dinner (Dinner provided in host family home)
days.description: You have a free day in Monteverde with lots of options to choose from. Zip through the jungle canopy, hike through the cloud forest reserves, ride a horse in the mountains, visit a coffee or sugar cane farm, tour the cheese factory, or check out the orchid garden, serpentarium, or frog pond in town.

days.title: Isla de Ometepe to Monteverde
days.description: Transfer to La Fortuna on bumpy roads, but you'll break up the journey with a peaceful boat ride on Lake Arenal. La Fortuna sits at the base of Arenal Volcano and is known as Costa Rica's adventure sports capital. Once there, you'll have access to canyoning, white water rafting, hiking, caving, horseback riding, paddleboarding, kayaking and wildlife refuge visits.

days.title: Monteverde
optional: Visit cloud forest reserve (35-50 USD per person)
Coffee plantation tour (40 USD per person)
CASEM Coop visit (14-25 USD per person)
Butterfly garden visit (21 USD per person)
days.description: Free time in the La Fortuna and Arenal area means you can pick what appeals to you. Try canyoneering, hiking, caving, rafting, horseback riding, paddleboarding, kayaking, or visit a wildlife refuge to see the local animals.

days.title: Monteverde to La Fortuna
days.description: Travel through the mountains to San José for your final night out. The capital has nice parks, museums and theaters, and from downtown streets you'll get views of the lush mountains surrounding the city.

days.title: La Fortuna
optional: La Fortuna Waterfall swim (20 USD per person)
Ecotermales Hot Springs (49 USD per person)
Lost Canyon Adventures Canyoning (90 USD per group)
Caño Negro Wildlife Refuge Tour (65-133 USD per person)
days.description: This free day on Ometepe is yours to explore with your host family. Climb Volcano Concepción or Volcano Maderas, look at pre-Columbian petroglyphs, walk or kayak in Charco Verde reserve, swim in clear spring water at Ojo de Agua, relax on the beach at Santo Domingo, or bike around the island.

days.title: La Fortuna to San José
optional: Sarapiqui River Rafting (99 USD per person)
days.description: Head from Granada to San Jorge and then take a ferry across Lake Nicaragua to Ometepe Island, which is formed from two volcanoes rising out of the water. Once there, you'll start a 2-night community homestay with a local family. Breakfast and dinner are provided, so you'll get to experience how rural Nicaraguans live and eat.

intro: Explore ancient sights and lost cities, overnight in a Bedouin tent and dine amidst the dramatic desert scenery of Wadi Rum. Take in Petra's fascinating history and marvel at its thrilling beauty, and still have a chance to relax in the therapeutic waters of the Dead Sea. This eight-day trip is ideal for the traveller who is short on time but wants to soak up the colours, culture, and history of a country that's small in size, but big in adventure.

days.title: Amman
days.description: You'll arrive in Amman whenever your flight gets in, and there's nothing scheduled until the evening. This gives you time to settle into your accommodation and freshen up. Later in the day, you'll head to the welcome meeting where you'll connect with your CEO and the rest of the group. There's an optional group dinner available if you want to join. The city sprawls across different neighborhoods, so if you want to explore on your own earlier in the day, your CEO can point you toward good spots. Getting around means grabbing a taxi, which your guide can help you arrange.

days.title: Amman to Dead Sea
optional: Site of Jesus' Baptism (18JOD per person)
days.description: Early morning, you'll drive out to Jerash for a half-day visit to these remarkable Roman ruins. The site is one of the largest and most intact outside of Italy, with columns and structures that really show what Roman engineering looked like. From there, you'll head to the Dead Sea. You can float in the water thanks to the extreme salt content, slather on some therapeutic mud if you're interested, or visit the baptism site of Jesus. The drive back to Amman happens in the evening, so you'll get back to the city by nightfall.

days.title: Amman to Wadi Musa
optional: Beit Al Jameed Optional Lunch Activity
days.description: Leave early and head to Mt Nebo, where you'll learn about the area's ancient history and take in panoramic views across the region. Then it's off to Madaba to see the famous Byzantine mosaics that date back to the sixth century. Next, you'll stop at Karak Castle, an impressive crusader fortress with significant historical importance. You'll roll into Wadi Musa in the early evening. This small town sits right outside Petra, so you'll be perfectly positioned for exploring the site tomorrow.

days.title: Petra
optional: Turkish Bath in Petra (45JOD per person)
days.description: Start early for your guided walking tour of Petra led by your CEO. The site is massive, so you can choose your own adventure. Some people hike to the top of the treasury, while others prefer exploring at their own pace. Fair warning: the terrain is sandy and rocky with a lot of ground to cover, so bring proper hiking shoes, drink plenty of water, and take breaks when you need them. By evening, you can either visit a Turkish bath for some relaxation or check out Petra by night if that appeals to you.

days.title: Petra to Wadi Rum
optional: Siq al-Barid (Little Petra) Visit (8JOD per person)
days.meals: Breakfast, Dinner (Traditional meal prepared in traditional fashion with meat and vegetables cooked in an underground oven)
days.description: If you're interested, there's an optional morning visit to Little Petra before you head deeper into the desert. Later, you'll drive to Wadi Rum and then go deep into the landscape by 4x4, stopping at famous landmarks as you travel. You'll arrive at a Bedouin desert camp in time for dinner, which is prepared in an underground oven using traditional methods. You'll sleep in individual cabins with bathrooms, so it's fairly comfortable for a desert experience. Bring a flashlight since lanterns light the pathways, and keep in mind that soft drinks and water are available to purchase.

days.title: Wadi Rum to Aqaba
optional: Beit Al Ward - Saayadia Cooking Class
days.description: You'll drive out to Aqaba, a resort city right on the Red Sea. Once you arrive, the rest of the day is yours to spend however you like. If you want to get in the water, snorkelling is a great option here with nice coral and fish. Alternatively, you can just walk around the beach, relax, or check out what the city has to offer. Later on, try to find a spot for dinner that serves fresh seafood, which is what Aqaba does well.

days.title: Aqaba to Amman
days.meals: Breakfast, Lunch (Community lunch at Safi Kitchen, a nonprofit organization supporting local community in the South Ghour region)
days.description: The journey back to Amman includes a lunch stop at Safi Kitchen, a community cafe in the South Ghour region south of the Dead Sea. It's supported by G Adventures and part of a nonprofit organization working to create opportunities for local people while focusing on environmental and social impact. You'll eat lunch here and help support their work. After you arrive back in Amman, you'll have your final evening in the city to explore, have dinner, or just relax.

days.title: Amman
days.description: You'll depart Amman whenever works for your travel plans. Head to the airport at whatever time gets you to your next destination.

Tour the Scottish Highlands on this fun-filled three-day adventure. Get Amongst It!

days.start_point: Castle Rock Hostel, 15 Johnston Terrace, Edinburgh, Scotland EH1 2PR, United Kingdom (Check-in at Castle Rock Hostel reception from 8.30 for a 9am departure, 09:00)

After that, the route takes you along the scenic Road to the Isles before catching a ferry across to the Isle of Skye. By evening you'll be settled in Kyleakin village for the night.

Full of incredible experiences, from Sydney’s iconic beaches and nightlife, to surf lessons from real Aussie surfer dudes in the famous Byron Bay, plus much more! You’ll have an awesome group leader from the moment you arrive and an instant group of friends to enjoy the trip with. Get ready for the trip of a lifetime!

days.title: Byron Bay

Since the tour officially departs on the 26th, how does the booking work for those initial days? qa.answer: If you arrive early, you can book 3 extra nights in the same accommodation via your Manage My Booking page once you are booked, or you can book somewhere independently and meet at the hostel on day one, it's completely up to you! However as the 10 day finishes in Brisbane, to ensure you get to see some local wildlife you could take a trip to Australia Zoo after the tour has ended! B

qa.question: I see the recommendation is to arrive on the start day. Would landing at 10pm be too late? How long is the trip from the airport to the hostel and will there be someone available to connect with them if they arrived at that time? Flights / Transfers
qa.answer: On Day 1 of the trip, there are no planned activities, so they can choose to arrive at any time. The group meets around 7pm for a welcome dinner, so we recommend arriving before then if possible. If arriving later that evening that's no problem - they'll still be able to check-in to the hostel and meet their Group Leader. The airport train operates until after midnight and it's an easy journey to the hostel. Ubers are always readily available if they prefer to share a taxi instead. Alternatively, if they'd prefer to arrive the evening before their tour starts, we can organise an extra night at the accommodation for them.

qa.question: How much would it be if I want to share a room with another girl. Now it cost 1.699 so if I would share how much would it be ?

qa.question: What is the average age at the tour? Are many about 19?
qa.answer: Our tours are for over 18's only. The majority of travellers that join us in Australia are aged 18 to mid 20s, but we regularly have people in their late 20s and 30s travel with us and have an incredible time too! As long as you have an appetite for adventure and are happy bonding with people of all backgrounds, you'll fit in perfectly!

intro:
Thai Intro is the most amazing way to experience Thailand! You’ll discover Bangkok by boat and tuk tuk, visit ancient temples, learn to cook delicious Thai food, sleep in floating bungalows in the middle of Khao Sok National Park, explore tropical islands, party on the world famous Full Moon Beach and so much more! With a knowledgable group leader, an instant group of friends and help with all your onward travel. Get ready for the trip of a lifetime!

+ Our tours are all 100% Carbon Neutral!

days.title: Bangkok

days.title: Bangkok to Khao Sok
days.description: Take a traditional Thai cooking class where a local chef teaches you how to prepare authentic Thai dishes. In the evening, you board an overnight train heading south toward Khao Sok National Park, sleeping in a shared cabin on the way.

days.description: Hop on a long-tail boat and explore Khao Sok National Park, winding through dramatic limestone cliffs to reach a freshwater lake. You'll stay overnight in floating bungalows with options to go kayaking, tubing, and looking for monkeys during the day.

days.title: Koh Phangan
days.description: This is a relaxing beach day with free time to swim and sunbathe as much as you want. Later you can get a traditional Thai massage to help recover from all the activity you've done so far.

days.title: Koh Phangan
days.description: Check out the island's different beaches and spend time in the clear water. When evening comes around, you'll gather with your group for a beach BBQ.

days.title: Koh Phangan

days.title: Koh Phangan

intro:
Southwest highlights. Enjoy our included overnight adventure in iconic Monument Valley, experience the real Wild Wild West, immerse yourselves in the amazing Utah landscapes of  Zion, Bryce, Antelope Canyon, Arches and Canyonlands National Parks. Stare into the mysterious depths of the Grand Canyon before heading back to Fabulous Las Vegas.

This tour has a free downloadable App with tour commentary in French, German, Spanish, Italian, Mandarin, Korean, Japanese.

Live commentary is provided in English. 

New Tour Option- Purchase 8 seats and have a fully private tour with camping.

days.title: Zion National Park
days.start_point: Palms Casino Resort, 4321 W Flamingo Rd, Las Vegas, Nevada 89103, United States (Tour bus pick up area, 07:00)
days.description: You'll leave Las Vegas early and drive toward Zion National Park in Utah, where towering canyon walls and red sandstone cliffs come into view. Once you arrive, there's plenty to do depending on your energy level. The Narrows is a popular walk that takes you right through the river corridor between sheer rock faces. If you want something different, the Emerald Pools trail offers a shorter option with great views, or you can do a longer river hike that takes you deeper into the canyon. By evening you'll head back to camp where a BBQ dinner waits, and you can relax under the stars.

days.title: Bryce National Park
days.description: A short drive takes you to Bryce National Park, which sits at 8,000 feet elevation. You'll walk along the rim and see the unique sandstone spires called hoodoos rising from the natural amphitheater below. In the afternoon, hike down for a closer look at these formations. Back at camp, soak in the outdoor hot tub and relax around the campfire as the evening cools down.

days.title: Day 3
days.description: These two days take in two different landscapes across the region. First, head to Arches National Park to hike up to Delicate Arch, which sits among over 2,000 arches in the area. Then move on to Canyonlands, where you can walk around and see where the Green River meets the Colorado River amid the scenery. You'll hear stories about Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid, and get to know the local adventure capital.

days.title: Monument Valley
included: Navajo guided 4X4 jeep tour of Monument Valley
days.description: Start with an optional visit to Antelope Canyon, a famous slot canyon, followed by a scenic walk to see Horseshoe Bend. Then continue toward the Grand Canyon, where you'll visit a Navajo trading post and follow the Colorado River through the painted desert. Take in the views of this natural wonder, then end with a final cookout before making your way back to the city.

days.title: Antelope Canyon - Horseshoe Bend - Grand Canyon
included: Stroll along the rim at sunset
optional: Optional helicopter ride at the Grand Canyon
Relax in one of the rim cafes
days.description: Get your kicks on Historic Route 66 as you head back to Las Vegas, arriving at approximately 4-5pm to finish your trip.
