name: 14-Day Everest Base Camp Trek Adventure

attributes.name: Hiking & Trekking
attributes.tip: Conquer epic trails and breathtaking landscapes

attributes.name: Group Tour
attributes.tip: Join a group and forge lifelong friendships

attributes.name: Fully Guided
attributes.tip: An experienced guide will be with you for the entire tour

attributes.name: Medium Intensity
attributes.tip: Travelers should be comfortable with somewhat-demanding activities

intro:
The Everest Base Camp Trek offers an unparalleled adventure on one of the planet's most stunning trekking trails. While reaching the summit of the world’s highest peak is an unparalleled achievement, the journey to Everest Base Camp itself is a trophy, filled with breathtaking scenery and the profound experience of traversing one of the most heavenly places on Earth. This trek challenges you in multiple ways, but each test is a step toward personal growth. It strengthens your endurance, broadens your understanding, and deepens your appreciation for the simple yet inspiring life of the people living in Nepal's Everest region.

­ 

Escape the hustle and bustle of the crowded city and immerse yourself in the tranquil and serene mountains. The Everest Base Camp Trek is designed to bring you close to the highest peak in the world—Mt. Everest. Imagine standing amidst snow-capped giants, with the Khumbu Icefall shimmering before you and the majestic Mt. Everest towering above. It’s a sensory experience like no other, a moment to be treasured where the entire atmosphere seems to celebrate your accomplishment. The trek will push you to your limits, testing your resolve with moments of exhaustion and uncertainty. Yet, an unseen force propels you forward, and upon reaching the top, the pain dissolves, leaving you in awe of the magnificent Mt. Everest standing before you.

­ 

Nepal Hiking Team, a top-rated and locally owned travel agency based in Kathmandu, will guide you on this 14-day Everest Base Camp Trek with full and proper acclimatization. Your journey begins with an exhilarating flight in a small aircraft to Lukla, followed by an ascent through well-paved trails to Phakding. The trek continues with a steep climb along stone-paved staircases through forests, across rivers, and over suspension bridges, leading you to Namche Bazaar. From Namche, you’ll navigate the high-altitude paths to Everest Base Camp, passing through Tengboche, Dingboche, Lobuche, and Gorakshep. Along the way, the majestic views of the towering Himalayas, including Mt. Everest, Mt. Lhotse, Mt. Ama Dablam, Mt. Pumori, and Mt. Nuptse, will keep you inspired. The 360-degree panoramic view of the mountainous valley from Kala Patthar is an unforgettable experience. Spirituality is woven into this journey, particularly at the Tengboche Monastery, where the presence of Tibetan Buddhist culture is palpable in the Mani walls, prayer flags, chortens, and stupas you’ll encounter along the way. If fortunate, you may even spot rare flora and fauna unique to these high-altitude regions.

­ 

The best seasons for trekking to the Everest region in Nepal are from March to May and September to December. With Nepal Hiking Team, you can expect a well-organized and secure journey, ensuring that your trek to Everest Base Camp is as rewarding as it is memorable. Join us, one of the most highly-rated trekking agencies in Nepal, and let our expert team turn your dream adventure into a reality.

days.title: Arrival in Kathmandu
days.start_point: Tribhuvan International Airport (KTM) त्रिभुवन विमानस्थल, त्रिभुवन विमानस्थल, Kathmandu, Bagmati Province, Nepal (Provide us with your arrival time at Kathmandu Airport., 00:00)
days.description: You'll arrive in Kathmandu whenever your flight gets in. Someone from the tour company meets you at the airport and walks through how everything works. There's nothing scheduled for today, so you'll head to your hotel and get settled in for the trek ahead.

days.title: Kathmandu to Lukla to Phakding
included: Trek to Phakding with views of Kusum Kangraru
days.description: An early morning transfer takes you to Ramechhap Airport for the flight to Lukla. This is the famous mountain flight with incredible views of the Himalayas as you approach. Once you land at Lukla's high-altitude airfield, trekking starts right away through forests and open terrain toward Phakding, with Kusum Kangraru visible along the way.

days.title: Phakding to Namche Bazaar
included: Views of Mount Everest and neighboring peaks
optional: Shopping for traditional crafts at local markets
days.description: You trek along the Dudh Koshi River through pine and cedar forests, gradually climbing to Namche Bazaar, the main trading hub where merchants from Nepal and Tibet have done business for centuries. On clear days you'll catch sight of Mount Everest for the first time. You'll spend two days here for acclimatization, so take the afternoon to rest and explore.

days.title: Namche Bazaar Acclimatization Day
included: Visit Everest View Hotel for panoramic views
days.description: This day focuses on acclimatization around Namche. You hike up to Syangboche Airport, the world's highest airstrip, then continue to Everest View Hotel where the views open up to show Everest, Lhotse, Amadablam, and Tawache. On the way back down, you'll check out the Sherpa Culture Museum and Everest Photo Gallery to learn more about the region and mountaineering history.

days.title: Namche Bazaar to Tengboche
days.description: The trek follows an easy trail initially, then descends into the Dudh Koshi Valley at Pungki Thanka before climbing up the right side to reach Tengboche Monastery at 3,860 meters. This is the spiritual heart of the Khumbu region. It's a long day but the views of Amadablam make it worthwhile, and if the weather cooperates, you'll see Everest and the surrounding peaks from here.

days.title: Tengboche to Dingboche
included: Trek through forest and Pangboche village
Views of Mount Amadablam and Lhotse
days.description: After walking through forest and crossing the Imja Khola, you'll pass through Pangboche village at 3,900 meters. This is considered one of the best trekking days because you maintain your altitude and get solid views of Amadablam, Lhotse, and other major peaks. The route then goes through pastures before reaching Dingboche, which locals call the 'summer valley.'

days.title: Dingboche Acclimatization Day
days.description: Your second acclimatization day involves about 6 hours of trekking. After breakfast, you ascend Nangkartsang hill at 5,100 meters, which is steep and physically tough, taking roughly 5 hours to reach the top. From that height you see Lobuche East and West, Taboche Peak, Thamserku, Kangtega, Ama Dablam, and possibly Makalu if conditions are clear. The descent takes about 2 hours, then you rest for the remainder of the afternoon.

days.title: Dingboche to Lobuche
included: Pass Trekkers Aid Post at Pheriche
days.description: You trek across a broad valley floor heading toward Dughla, passing the Trekkers Aid Post at Pheriche where western volunteer doctors and the Himalayan Rescue Association help trekkers. From there the route continues up the valley as altitude increases, then drops down to the yak pastures of Lobuche.

days.title: Lobuche to Gorekshep to Everest Base Camp
included: Views of Khumbu glacier and icefall
days.description: A short climb through meadows gives you views of the Khumbu glacier. Then it's on to Gorekshep before the final push to Everest Base Camp. The hike takes about 3 hours with plenty of ups and downs that can tire you out at this altitude, but reaching Base Camp is worth every step. You'll see the Khumbu glacier and icefall where climbers stage their Everest expeditions.

days.title: Gorekshep to Kalapattar to Pheriche
included: Panoramic views of Mount Everest and Himalayan range
days.description: Start early with a hike up to Kalapattar at 5,545 meters, which offers the best view of Mount Everest and the surrounding Himalayan range. After soaking in the views, you trek back to Gorekshep for breakfast, then descend to Pheriche for the night.

days.title: Pheriche to Namche Bazaar
included: Trek from Pheriche to Namche Bazaar
days.description: An easy walk along the Imja Khola leads to a short climb back to Tengboche. From there you descend via Pungki Thanka, navigate some steep sections to Kyangjuma, then take an easier trail back down to Namche Bazaar where you started your higher altitude days.

days.title: Namche Bazaar to Lukla
included: Trek to Lukla along Dudh Kosi River
days.description: The trek follows the Dudh Kosi River down to Lukla, the small mountain airstrip where your return flight departs. This is mostly downhill, which feels good after the higher elevation days, and you'll reach the airstrip in time for your flight back to Kathmandu.

days.title: Lukla to Kathmandu
days.description: You fly from Lukla back toward Kathmandu, possibly connecting through Ramechhap during busy seasons (direct flights happen during slower times). After landing, you drive to Kathmandu and check into your hotel for the night.

days.title: Departure from Kathmandu
days.description: After breakfast at the hotel, a representative from Nepal Hiking Team will meet you about 3 hours before your flight and take you to the airport for your departure.

qa.question: I am 67 and would like to do this trip. I am fitter than most 50 year olds and a very experienced hiker. I have previously summitted Kilimanjaro. I hike regularly in Australia carrying all my own equipment, tent, food etc... for 6 day trips. Please let me know if you require a doctor's certificate as to my capacity to join your trip to Everest Base Camp.
qa.answer: It is great to hear about your trekking background and experience. Completing Mount Kilimanjaro and continuing regular multi-day hikes with full gear already shows strong endurance and preparation. Your level of fitness and experience is very well suited for the Everest Base Camp trek. We are happy to confirm that there is no issue at all with your age, and we would be glad to have you join the trip. Many of our trekkers in their 60s successfully complete this journey each season with proper pacing and acclimatization. Regarding the medical certificate, it is not mandatory. However, if you have any pre-existing conditions or would like additional reassurance, you may consult your doctor before the trek.

qa.question: I'm looking to do a tour end of May into June and spending my birthday (10 June) on the trek. I was wondering if there was anyone booked on around my age already??
qa.answer: We have a confirmed group starting on 31st May, with the flight to Lukla scheduled for 1st June. You are very welcome to join this departure. At the moment, we already have two solo travelers confirmed for this trip, so you will be in good company with others joining individually as well.

qa.question: Could you please provide details on the best time to travel, along with the itinerary and inclusions for this tour?
qa.answer: The best time to plan this journey is during spring (March to May) and autumn (September to November). These months usually offer stable weather, clear skies, and excellent visibility of the Himalayan peaks. Our standard Everest Base Camp itinerary runs for 14 days, beginning with a flight to Lukla and gradually ascending through the Sherpa heartland. Key highlights include acclimatization in Namche Bazaar and Dingboche, visits to Tengboche Monastery, and the trek to Everest Base Camp itself at 5,364 meters. The journey also includes a climb to Kala Patthar at 5,545 meters for breathtaking sunrise views of Everest and its neighboring giants.

qa.question: We are interested in taking the Everest Base Camp Trek 14-days trip. Please send some information and photos of examples of the kind of accommodations included on the trek.
qa.answer: We would be pleased to arrange the 14-day Everest Base Camp Trek for you starting 2nd September. We operate small group departures, with a maximum of 10 participants and a typical group size of 7-8 people, ensuring a more personalized and enjoyable trekking experience.

intro:
Discover the cultural treasures of Cusco and take on one of Peru’s most spectacular alternative routes to Machu Picchu.

Begin with time to acclimatize in Cusco before exploring Chinchero, Moray, and the Maras Salt Mines. Then, set out on the five-day Salkantay Trek, crossing dramatic Andean valleys, visiting the turquoise waters of Humantay Lake, and reaching the challenging Salkantay Pass at approximately 4,600 meters (15,092 feet).

As the trail descends, watch the landscape transform from snow-covered mountains to cloud forest, waterfalls, tropical vegetation, coffee plantations, and warmer valleys. Visit the lesser-known archaeological site of Llactapata, where you can admire distant views of Machu Picchu, before continuing to Aguas Calientes.

Complete your journey with a guided visit to the legendary Machu Picchu citadel. Professional guides, an experienced trekking chef, support staff, mules, camping equipment, scheduled transportation, and carefully prepared meals are included throughout the trek.

days.title: Cusco
optional: Explore historic center of Cusco at own pace
days.start_point: Aeropuerto Internacional Alejandro Velasco Astete (CUZ), Av. Velasco Astete S/N, Wanchaq, Cusco 08006, Peru (Ourside the luggage claim area, 00:00 - 00:00)
days.description: You'll arrive in Cusco and your tour representative will pick you up at the airport for the transfer to your hotel. Since you're coming in at 3,350 meters elevation, it's best to take things easy and let your body adjust to the altitude. Later in the afternoon, you'll sit down with your guide for a pre-trek briefing covering the route details, gear, safety protocols, and what the next few days will look like.

days.title: Chinchero - Moray - Maras
days.description: After breakfast you'll head to Chinchero, a traditional Andean town where local artisans show how they weave textiles using natural dyes and alpaca wool. From there you'll continue to Moray to see the circular agricultural terraces carved into the mountainside. Before heading back to Cusco for the evening, you'll stop at the Maras Salt Mines where thousands of pools step down the slope. It's quite a lot of ground to cover in one day, but you'll return to your hotel by evening.

days.title: Cusco - Mollepata - Soraypampa - Humantay Lake
included: Early pick-up from hotel in Cusco
optional: Horse rental for additional fee based on local availability
days.meals: Breakfast (Box breakfast from the hotel), Lunch, Snack (Afternoon snack), Dinner
days.description: The hotel pickup happens early so you can get to Mollepata for final supplies and breakfast. From Challacancha you'll begin trekking toward Soraypampa through Andean valleys with mountain scenery all around. After lunch at the campsite, you'll hike up to turquoise Humantay Lake with dramatic peaks surrounding it, then head back to camp for dinner. This is your first night sleeping in the camp, so settle in early.

days.title: Soraypampa - Salkantay Pass - Huayracmachay - Challway
days.description: Today is the most physically challenging part of the trek. You'll start early after breakfast and gradually climb to Salkantay Pass at 4,600 meters, which is the highest point of the entire route. The views of snow-covered peaks and glacial valleys are spread out below as you rest and get some cultural context from your guide. Then you'll descend into greener areas and head toward Huayracmachay for lunch. The trek continues down to Challway where you'll camp for the night.

days.title: Challway - Collpabamba - La Playa - Lucmabamba
days.description: You'll start descending into cloud forest where everything changes dramatically. Waterfalls, orchids, tropical vegetation, and birds fill the landscape as you walk through different environments. Your guide talks through the biodiversity and how the landscape shifts between high Andes and the upper Amazon rainforest. After lunch near La Playa Sahuayaco, you'll continue to Lucmabamba surrounded by coffee and fruit plantations. The afternoon at camp is quieter so you can rest up.

days.title: Lucmabamba - Llactapata - Hydroelectric - Aguas Calientes
included: Guided visit to Llactapata archaeological site
Distant views of Machu Picchu (weather permitting)
Walk from Hydroelectric to Aguas Calientes
days.description: Early breakfast gets you ready for an ascent along an original Inca trail toward Llactapata archaeological site. From that viewpoint, if the weather cooperates, you'll see Machu Picchu in the distance. Your guide explains the historical significance and how this site connects to Machu Picchu. Then you'll descend toward the Hydroelectric Station, grab lunch, and walk along the railway beside the Urubamba River toward Aguas Calientes. You'll check into your hotel and get final details about tomorrow's visit.

days.title: Aguas Calientes - Machu Picchu - Ollantaytambo - Cusco
included: Round-trip shuttle bus between Aguas Calientes and Machu Picchu
Guided tour of assigned Machu Picchu circuit
Tourist train from Aguas Calientes to Ollantaytambo
optional: Entrance ticket to Huayna Picchu (subject to availability and advance reservation)
Entrance ticket to Machu Picchu Mountain (subject to availability and advance reservation)
days.description: Eat early, then the shuttle bus takes you up to Machu Picchu. You'll show your passport and entrance ticket at the gate. Your guide walks you through the assigned circuit, explaining the history, architecture, and meaning of this Inca site. After returning by shuttle to Aguas Calientes, you'll have time for lunch on your own. Later you'll catch the train to Ollantaytambo, then private transportation brings you back to your hotel in Cusco.

days.title: Cusco
days.description: You'll have breakfast at the hotel and free time until your departure. Your tour representative will meet you at the hotel at the scheduled time and drive you to Alejandro Velasco Astete International Airport for your flight home.

intro:
Adventure Holidays in Ireland Have Never Been So Good!


Take the road less travelled with this immersive 1-week Ireland itinerary.


On this adventure holiday, you will journey from Kinsale in County Cork to Westport in County Mayo, exploring over 1,100 km of rugged coastline on an unforgettable 7-day tour packed with excitement, culture and history.


Part of our Active Small Group Irish Tours, this trip is designed for travellers who want to blend relaxed sightseeing with soft adventure, including cycling, hiking, kayaking and more. It is the perfect mix of culture, activity and authentic Irish charm.


Leaving Dublin behind, we travel southwest along the Wild Atlantic Way, uncovering the very best of Ireland’s landscapes, legends and local life.


A Packed Itinerary for This 7-Day Trip to Ireland


As one of our most popular adventure holidays in Ireland, this tour is bursting with experiences that bring the country to life.


Imagine kayaking along Dingle Bay, cycling through Killarney National Park or marvelling at breathtaking views from Moll’s Gap and Ladies View. If you would like to explore the full Ring of Kerry, be sure to check out our Ireland to Island Tour.


You will also stand on the edge of the world at the Cliffs of Moher, soak up the bohemian spirit of Galway City and fall under the spell of the Aran Islands. To finish, challenge yourself with a hike on Croagh Patrick, Ireland’s holiest mountain, for sweeping views over Clew Bay, the perfect finale to your adventure.


Your week in Ireland is filled with castles, coastline, culture and craic, plus wildlife, history and plenty of photo-worthy moments.


If you are wondering whether this tour is right for you, take a look at our glowing guest reviews, they say it all! And if you would like to make this adventure completely your own, consider our Private Guided Tours of Ireland or Tailor-Made Ireland Tours.


Read the full itinerary and highlights below, and please don’t hesitate to get in touch if you have any questions.


Accessibility: Our small-group tours are not wheelchair accessible due to the off-the-beaten-path nature of our routes, the size of our vehicles, and the fact that not all accommodation partners have ramps or elevators.


Please note: While we always aim to follow the outlined itinerary, unforeseen circumstances such as weather, traffic, or local events may require adjustments. In some cases, certain activities may be cancelled. If this happens, your guide will always provide a thoughtful and enjoyable alternative to ensure your experience remains unforgettable. For this reason, we do not offer refunds for cancelled activities. Your comfort and enjoyment are always at the heart of everything we do.

days.title: Dublin to Kinsale
included: Visit Rock of Cashel - explore medieval round tower, cathedral and chapel
Kiss the Blarney Stone at Blarney Castle
Explore Blarney Castle Gardens and Rock Close
days.start_point: Ashling Hotel, Parkgate St, Dublin, D07, Ireland (Meeting point: The Ashling Hotel Dublin,10 - 13 Parkgate St, Stoneybatter, Dublin 8, D08 P38N, 08:00)
days.description: Head south from Dublin through the Irish countryside toward Cork. Your first stop is the Rock of Cashel, where you'll walk through medieval ruins sitting dramatically on a limestone outcrop. From there, it's on to Blarney Castle to kiss the famous Blarney Stone and check out its gardens. You'll finish the day in Kinsale, a colorful harbor town where you can grab seafood for dinner and walk around at sunset.

days.title: Kinsale to Dingle
included: Cycle through Killarney National Park - woodland and lakeshore routes
Pass Muckross House & Gardens on cycling trail
optional: Traditional music and pub experience in Dingle
days.description: After breakfast in Kinsale, drive west toward Kenmare, stopping to see the colorful streets and the ancient Kenmare Stone Circle. The route heading onward is one of Ireland's most scenic, so you'll pause at Moll's Gap and Ladies' View for photos. Later, cycle through Killarney National Park past Muckross House and toward Torc Waterfall on woodland trails. By evening you'll reach Dingle, a vibrant coastal town with colorful shopfronts and lively pubs.

days.title: Dingle
included: Kayaking adventure in Dingle Bay - paddle through sea caves
Slea Head Drive scenic route exploration
Visit Blasket Centre - learn about island life
optional: Explore Dingle's colorful streets and cosy pubs
days.description: Start the morning with a kayaking adventure in Dingle Bay, paddling through clear waters and into hidden sea caves with rugged cliff views. After lunch, drive the Slea Head route, one of Ireland's most spectacular coastal drives. You'll visit Famine Cottages, ancient Beehive Huts, Coomeenoule Beach, Dunquin Pier, and the Blasket Centre to learn about island life. Return to Dingle in the evening with free time to explore the town and its seafood restaurants.

days.title: Dingle to Doolin
included: Cliffs of Moher guided coastal walk - two-and-a-half hours on quieter paths
optional: Dinner and traditional Irish music in Doolin pubs
days.description: Travel north from Dingle with beautiful coastline views as you leave the peninsula behind. You'll watch a traditional sheepdog demonstration with local border collies and their handler. Cross the River Shannon by ferry into County Clare, then hike the famous Cliffs of Moher on a guided two-and-a-half-hour coastal walk along quieter paths with panoramic views. The day ends in Doolin, a charming village known for colorful cottages and traditional Irish music sessions.

days.title: Doolin to Galway
included: Return ferry to Inis Oírr (Aran Islands)
Bicycle hire on Inis Oírr - explore at own pace
Ferry cruise beneath Cliffs of Moher
Pass through Burren National Park landscape
optional: Live music and pub experience in Galway
days.description: Take a ferry to Inisheer, the smallest Aran Island, and explore by bicycle. Cycle past the Plassey shipwreck, wander through ancient stone-walled fields, visit the lighthouse, or just soak in Atlantic views. You'll have lunch on the island before heading back. The ferry ride back takes you beneath the Cliffs of Moher. After that, drive north through Burren National Park's limestone landscape, stopping to see Dunguaire Castle overlooking Galway Bay. You'll end in Galway, known for live music, restaurants, and vibrant pubs.

days.title: Galway to Westport
included: Explore Kylemore Abbey & Victorian Walled Gardens - three hours
optional: Coffee stop and leg stretch in Louisburgh
days.description: Leave Galway for Connemara, where rugged mountains, lakes, and winding valleys create dramatic scenery. Stop at Lough Inagh Valley for photos, then spend the late morning and early afternoon at Kylemore Abbey and its Victorian Walled Gardens. Walk the lakeside estate, see the Neo-Gothic Church, and stroll through the gardens. Continue north through Connemara to Louisburgh for a coffee break with Atlantic views. Finish with a scenic drive to Westport, one of Ireland's prettiest towns, with evening free to explore its streets and restaurants.

days.title: Westport to Dublin
included: Croagh Patrick hike - access to mountain trail, all levels welcome
optional: Explore Westport - boutique shops and waterfront
days.description: Your final morning offers options. Hike Croagh Patrick, Ireland's holiest mountain and a sacred pilgrimage site for over 1,500 years. Climb part or all of the trail for sweeping views over Clew Bay with its 365 islands. If you prefer a slower pace, spend the morning in Westport browsing shops or enjoying coffee by the Quay. Then drive back east to Dublin filled with memories, and your guide shares recommendations for exploring Ireland's capital.

intro:
Bali Intro is the most amazing way to experience Bali! You’ll discover crazy Bali nightlife, visit ancient temples, learn to surf on iconic Bali beaches, swim under amazing waterfalls, experience local culture, spot wild dolphins, explore tropical islands, snorkel with turtles, party on the beach and more! With an awesome group leader from the moment your tour starts, an instant group of friends to share your adventure with and help with all your onward travel. Get ready for the trip of a lifetime! 

+ Our tours are all 100% Carbon Neutral!

days.title: Bali
days.start_point: Ngurah Rai International Airport (DPS), Jalan Airport Ngurah Rai, Badung, Bali 80361, Indonesia (Denpasar Airport)
days.description: You'll touch down in Bali and get picked up at the airport for the drive to your hotel. After settling in and shaking off the flight, you'll have time to rest and meet the rest of your group.

days.title: Bali
included: Learn to make Canang Sari (local offering)
days.description: This morning you'll visit some of Bali's old temples to get a feel for the local culture, then take an Indonesian language lesson. You'll learn how to make a Canang Sari, which is a traditional local offering. Later on, head to a beach club to catch the sunset and get ready for the evening out.

days.title: Bali
days.description: Head down to the beach for a surf lesson with local instructors. Bali's known as one of the top surf spots in the world, so you'll be learning in a pretty good location.

days.title: Canggu to Lovina
optional: Purchase snacks at Nadia & Willy's snack shack
Taste coffee at local Luwak coffee plantation
days.description: Travel up toward Lovina and stop at a temple and some waterfalls on the way. You'll pass through the Jatiluwih Rice Fields, which are really beautiful, before arriving at your mountain accommodation that overlooks both rice paddies and the ocean.

days.title: Lovina
included: Visit local family home for basket weaving lesson
Traditional outrigger boat trip to see dolphins
days.description: Spend the morning with a local family learning basket weaving and getting a real sense of how Balinese people live. In the afternoon, take a traditional outrigger boat out along the coast to look for wild dolphins. Back at the villa, you can cool off in the infinity pool.

days.title: Lovina to Gili Trawangan
days.description: You'll hop on a fast ferry to Gili Trawangan, a tropical island with white sand beaches and clear turquoise water. The rest of the day is yours to relax and wander around, and later you can check out what the island has for nightlife.

days.title: Gili Trawangan
optional: Join Gili Eco Trust for beach cleanup (available on Fridays)
days.description: Get around Gili Trawangan by bike since the island doesn't have motorized vehicles, which makes it pretty unique. Spend time on the white sandy beaches and stick around for the sunset.

days.title: Gili Islands
days.description: Take a boat out to explore the Gili Islands with stops for snorkeling in crystal clear water. You should have a good shot at spotting sea turtles during the day.

days.title: Bali
optional: Extend stay in Bali with tour operator assistance
days.description: Your 9-day trip wraps up today. Make your way to the airport for your flight home, or talk with your group leader about staying longer in Bali if you want to extend things with your new friends.

attributes.name: Nature & Wildlife
attributes.tip: Explore untamed landscapes teeming with wildlife

attributes.name: Group Tour
attributes.tip: Join a group and forge lifelong friendships

intro: Your Canada tour in the Rocky Mountains begins in a stunning natural setting, ticking off Jasper and Banff, Lake Louise and a scenic trek across the Athabasca Glacier in an Ice Explorer. Enjoy a MAKE TRAVEL MATTER® Experience as a Cree guide gives insight into the importance of buffalo.

days.title: Calgary
days.description: You'll arrive in Calgary, which serves as the gateway to the Canadian Rockies. After getting settled into your accommodations, you'll meet your Travel Director and join the group for a welcome dinner this evening.

days.title: Lake Louise - Icefields Parkway - Jasper
included: Stop at Lake Louise and explore the shoreline, learning about its turquoise waters, Victoria Glacier and scenic mountain backdrop
Drive the Icefields Parkway through the Continental Divide, rocky peaks, waterfalls and ancient glaciers
days.description: The day takes you into the heart of the Canadian Rockies starting at Lake Louise, where you'll have time to walk around and grab lunch. From there, you'll drive along the Icefields Parkway with stops at Big Bend Viewpoint and Sunwapta Falls. Keep watch for bears, elk and mountain goats as you travel through Jasper National Park. You'll stop at Athabasca Falls before arriving in Jasper for a two-night stay.

days.title: Jasper National Park
included: Be My Guest experience lunch at Maligne Lake Chalet
Jasper Theater Productions performance and stories
Cruise across Maligne Lake to Spirit Island (seasonal)
View Spirit Island and three glaciers
days.meals: Breakfast, Lunch (Be My Guest experience at Maligne Lake Chalet)
days.description: Start with a leisurely morning in Jasper where you can either relax or join an optional float trip. Lunch happens at the Maligne Lake Chalet as a Be My Guest experience, followed by entertainment from Jasper Theater Productions where you'll hear local stories. After that, you'll take a cruise across Maligne Lake to see Spirit Island, which features three glaciers and mountain views. Note that Spirit Island is only accessible by water and seasonal conditions may apply.

days.title: Athabasca Glacier - Banff
included: Ride on an all-terrain Ice Explorer onto Athabasca Glacier
Learn about glaciers and environmental impact from driver-guide
days.description: You'll ride an all-terrain Ice Explorer onto the Athabasca Glacier, one of the largest non-polar icefields in the world. Your driver-guide explains how glaciers work and their environmental impact. You'll get to walk on the glacier itself, taste glacier water and take in the surrounding snowcapped peaks. Later, you'll continue your journey to Banff village.

days.title: Canmore - Banff
included: Learn to play hockey like a pro with a professional hockey coach in Canmore
Meet a real Canadian hockey player
Put on full hockey gear with coach assistance
Practice on ice and learn how to score
optional: Helicopter ride over the Canadian Rockies
Banff Gondola ride to top of Sulphur Mountain
days.description: Head to Canmore to meet a professional Canadian hockey player who'll teach you the sport like someone training to play. A coach guides you through what a player's day looks like, shares insider secrets and superstitions, and helps you get into full gear. Then you'll hit the ice to learn fundamentals and try scoring. Alternatively, you can choose a helicopter ride over the Canadian Rockies or a trip on the Banff Gondola up Sulphur Mountain for views of six mountain ranges.

days.title: Banff
included: MAKE TRAVEL MATTER® Experience with Cree guide
Learn about buffalo importance to survival and indigenous teachings
optional: Guided excursion to Yoho National Park and Moraine Lake (seasonal) in Valley of Ten Peaks
days.description: You have the option to explore Yoho National Park and Moraine Lake in the Valley of Ten Peaks this morning (seasonal availability), or spend time in Banff on your own. This evening, a Cree guide will meet with you for a MAKE TRAVEL MATTER Experience where you'll learn about the importance of buffalo to indigenous peoples and gain insight into indigenous teachings and the sacred relationship with nature. You'll toast to your travels and shared experiences with the group over dinner.

days.title: Banff to Calgary
days.description: You'll say goodbye to the Canadian Rockies and head from Banff back to Calgary. An included airport transfer takes you to Calgary International Airport for your return flight, or to The Westin Calgary if you're extending your stay.

name: Central American Journey

attributes.name: City & Culture
attributes.tip: Immerse yourself in rich history and local traditions

attributes.name: Group Tour
attributes.tip: Join a group and forge lifelong friendships

attributes.name: Fully Guided
attributes.tip: An experienced guide will be with you for the entire tour

attributes.name: Medium Intensity
attributes.tip: Travelers should be comfortable with somewhat-demanding activities

intro:
Tropical cloud forests alive with jungle melodies and native wildlife, vast freshwater lakes and active volcanoes, historic cities and shared moments with locals – this pocket of Central America is a slice of paradise. On this 16-day Central American journey, take in all the must-visit spots like Guatemala, Honduras, El Salvador, Nicaragua and Costa Rica. You’ll spot sloths among the canopy of Monteverde, see how indigo dying works in Suchitoto, explore the World Heritage-listed ruins of Copan and stand in the shadow of mighty Arenal Volcano. This adventure is perfect for those who like to experience a destination 'la forma natural' (the natural way).

Compared to the other countries you visit on this trip, Costa Rica can sometimes seem expensive. Expect to pay more than you would in other Central American countries for a lot of things., You cover heaps of ground on this trip, with several border crossings and long travel days. This trip includes time spent travelling in a private vehicle with your group. Extra space can be tight, and conditions may feel a little cramped. Although this can be tiresome, it’s all part of the adventure and a great way to get to know your fellow travellers., Central America is generally hot and humid year-round. At nighttime and in locations at higher elevations it can get chilly. Protect yourself from the sun, bring light clothing you can layer and a waterproof jacket, and stay hydrated. Air conditioning may not always be available in your rooms. Occasionally, properties may require an additional charge for air conditioning., This trip can involve a lot of walking. Please ensure you bring sturdy walking shoes and comfortable clothes. To make the most of the trip, it's best if you have at least a moderate level of fitness., There will be times when you have to walk with your luggage, and for this reason, it is recommended you pack light and use a backpack or something easy to carry., If you are traveling with a UK passport, a visa is now required to enter Honduras. Please ensure you check the Important Notes and Essential Trip Information for more details.

days.title: Antigua
optional: Visit ChocoMuseo to learn about old-world chocolate production
days.description: Landing in Antigua means stepping into a colonial city with volcanic backdrops. If your flight gets in early, the ChocoMuseo offers a chance to learn how chocolate gets made using traditional methods, or you can relax by the fountain in Central Park. The official welcome meeting happens at 6 pm, and after that you're on your own to wander around the city. Grab some tamales with other travelers if you're hungry and want to start getting to know the group.

days.title: Antigua to Copan
optional: Explore Copan town and cobblestone streets
days.description: An early 7 am departure takes you from Antigua toward Honduras. During the drive, watch the landscape change and learn about Guatemalan local life from your guides. You'll cross into Honduras and arrive in the small town of Copan by early afternoon. Spend the rest of your day walking the cobblestone streets and finding a cafe to settle into while you adjust to the new surroundings.

days.title: Copan
included: Guided visit to Copan Archaeological site
optional: Natural hot springs tour with mud baths, natural steam baths, refreshing pools and included dinner
days.description: Meet your local guide this morning to see the Copan ruins, the southernmost of the great Maya sites and a World Heritage location. You'll walk past elaborate stelae, temples, excavated vaults, and walls carved with ancient faces. The afternoon opens up for what you want to do next: check out the colorful macaws at Macaw Mountain Park, visit the Temple of Rosalila, or soak in natural hot springs in the jungle with an included dinner.

days.title: Copan to Suchitoto
days.description: This morning you'll leave Copan and head across the border into Guatemala, then continuing into El Salvador. It's a long travel day, so bring a book or road trip games to pass the time. When you arrive in Suchitoto, El Salvador's cultural capital, your leader takes you on an orientation walk to see the elaborate building facades and get oriented. After that comes a pupusa-making demonstration where you'll learn to make these classic Salvadoran cornmeal flatbreads stuffed with cheese or chicharron.

days.title: Suchitoto
days.description: Head to a local designer's home this morning for an indigo-dyeing demonstration. You'll learn about Suchitoto's position as one of the world's best indigo-producing centers and see how the designer blends tradition with modern craft. Try the dyeing yourself and get hands-on with the process. The afternoon is free, so you could take a guided walk through Cinquera Forest where Civil War guerrilla fighters once sheltered, or enjoy views of Lago Suchitlan, a freshwater lake where migrating birds gather.

days.title: Pacific Coast
days.description: Drive to El Salvador's Pacific Coast this morning where dark-sand beaches and some of the country's best surf spots wait for you. The afternoon is yours to relax at the beach or at your accommodation. Find a local restaurant for dinner or simply unwind after your travels.

days.title: Pacific Coast to Leon
days.description: Rise early for a full day of travel. A boat crossing takes you across the Gulf of Fonseca to reach Nicaragua. By afternoon you'll land in Leon, Nicaragua's second-largest city. Your leader guides you on an orientation walk through the charming streets so you get your bearings. Leon is quiet and great for strolling past murals and contemporary architecture. Tonight, head out to dinner with your group.

days.title: Leon
optional: Street food tasting behind Lady of Grace Cathedral
Volcano sandboarding at Cerro Negro Volcano
days.description: Today you have the freedom to make of Leon what you want. Try a Nica taco, a rolled and deep-fried maize served with shredded cabbage and cream, from the street food area behind the Lady of Grace Cathedral. If adventure calls, volcano sandboarding on the black slopes of Cerro Negro Volcano is an option. Or explore the city's contemporary art scene and wander through the Leon Cathedral.

days.title: Leon to Granada
included: La Laguna de Apoyo Viewpoint visit
days.description: Drive to Granada, the oldest city in the New World, this morning. Along the way, stop at Laguna Apoyo, a volcanic crater lake formed around 23,000 years ago, to stretch your legs and take in the view. You'll have free time for lunch near the viewpoint. Continue to Masaya for an orientation walk and time to browse the stalls at the famous artisan market. Arriving in Granada, you'll see Moorish and Andalusian architecture set on Lake Nicaragua's banks and surrounded by active volcanoes. Your leader guides you through Parque Central and La Calzada, a busy pedestrian street with bars and restaurants. The afternoon is yours.

days.title: Granada
included: Breakfast at El Cafe de las Sonrisas
optional: Visit Convento y Museo San Francisco
Boat tour of Lake Nicaragua islets
days.meals: Breakfast (Breakfast at El Cafe de las Sonrisas)
days.description: Start your morning with breakfast at Cafe de las Sonrisas, a cafe run entirely by people who are deaf and hard of hearing. After that, the day is yours to explore. Visit the Convento y Museo San Francisco to see indigenous stone statues, or get out on Lake Nicaragua by boat or kayak to explore hundreds of evergreen islets and meet fishermen living in wooden huts. Just a heads up: freshwater sharks live in these waters, so swimming isn't recommended.

days.title: Granada to Monteverde
days.description: Another early start as you head to Monteverde for a full day of travel. This town was founded in 1951 by Quakers and sits home to the Cloud Forest Biological Preserve, a rainforest-like ecosystem that draws water from cloud cover. Begin exploring this afternoon on an orientation walk with your leader. With over 2,000 plant species, 320 bird species, and 100 mammal species, it's a nature lover's paradise.

days.title: Monteverde
optional: Night walk through cloud forest to spot nocturnal creatures
days.description: Begin the day with breakfast at a local women's cooperative cafe, a social enterprise started in 1982 by eight women that now helps many women without formal education earn income for their families. Browse the handmade products in the cafe. The rest of your day is free to explore Monteverde. Try ziplining through the treetops, discover Costa Rica's agricultural heritage on a coffee and chocolate tour, or spot nocturnal creatures on an optional night walk.

days.title: Monteverde to La Fortuna
included: Monteverde Cloud Forest Reserve guided walk with local guide
Leader-led orientation walk of La Fortuna
days.description: Start at the Monteverde Cloud Forest Reserve with a local guide, walking the trails to learn about the region's biodiversity. Look for the resplendent quetzal and listen for howler monkeys. This afternoon, take a minibus to Lake Arenal's shores, then board a boat across the lake to La Fortuna. On clear days you'll have fantastic views as the massive Arenal Volcano looms larger as you approach. Once ashore, transfer to your hotel and freshen up before your leader takes you on an orientation walk.

days.title: La Fortuna
optional: Guided nature hike through Arenal Volcano forest
Hanging bridges walk with wildlife spotting
Boat safari in Cano Negro Wildlife Refuge
days.description: Start your free day with a smoothie and plan your adventure. Take a guided nature hike through the forest surrounding Arenal Volcano, spotting rare plants and animals. Walk across hanging bridges for a great vantage point to see sloths and colorful birds, or relax in natural thermal hot springs. Visit the 70-meter La Fortuna waterfall in the rainforest or paddle across the lake on a stand-up paddleboard. If you're keen on wildlife, take a boat safari in Cano Negro Wildlife Refuge to spot lizards, crocodiles, and tropical birds.

days.title: La Fortuna to San Jose
optional: Shopping at Plaza de la Cultura outdoor market
Optional farewell dinner with fellow travelers
days.description: Spend your final morning learning the art of Costa Rican tortillas from a local family, and you'll get to try the results over lunch. Then transfer to San Jose, Costa Rica's capital, watching Arenal Volcano fade into the distance. Upon arrival, join your leader on an orientation walk to see the main highlights. Visit the Gold Museum with its fantastic collection of pre-Spanish gold art, or head to the outdoor market at Plaza de la Cultura or the Central Market for handicrafts and seafood. Maybe join your group for an optional farewell dinner.

days.title: San Jose
days.description: Your trip comes to an end this morning with no further activities planned. Plenty to see and do in and around San Jose if you'd like to stay longer, so speak to your booking agent ahead of time to arrange an extension if that interests you.

qa.question: I'm a solo traveller and interested in this tour. Unfortunately I have an injury that means I cannot walk long distances. I prefer not to walk more than say 1 km or I am in pain. Would i suit your tour?

A moderate level of fitness is recommended to get the most out of the experience. We would therefore recommend carefully considering whether the physical demands of the trip would be comfortable for you. If you would like, we can also suggest alternative trips that may be better suited to travellers with mobility limitations.

name: Contrasts of Switzerland

attributes.tip: Immerse yourself in rich history and local traditions

intro: All aboard the world's first-ever 'Swisstainable' tour. Experience the local culture and delight in regional produce as you support the ecology and economy of Switzerland. Every hotel, experience, meal and transport is accredited 'Swisstainable' - Switzerland's national benchmark certificate for sustainability.

days.title: Zürich
included: MAKE TRAVEL MATTER® Experience - guided walking tour of Zürich's old town led by local guide supporting community change makers
days.description: You'll arrive in Zürich and connect with your Travel Director and other travelers. A local guide takes you on a walking tour through the old town that focuses on social impact projects and community work. Later that evening, everyone gathers for a welcome dinner to start things off.

days.title: Zürich to St. Moritz
included: Scenic train journey from Zürich to St. Moritz via Chur
Travel across the Bernina Pass (subject to availability)
days.description: Board a scenic train heading toward St. Moritz, traveling through Switzerland via Chur. You'll see snow-capped peaks along the way, and this afternoon you can experience the Bernina Pass route if the timing works out. Dinner happens at your hotel once you arrive in this stylish mountain resort.

days.title: St. Moritz to Zermatt
included: Glacier Express train journey from St. Moritz to Zermatt (subject to availability)
Orientation tour of Zermatt with Travel Director
days.meals: Breakfast, Lunch (On board the Glacier Express), Dinner
days.description: The Glacier Express takes you on one of the world's most famous rail journeys. You'll cross hundreds of bridges and climb over the Oberalp Pass at 2,044 m (6,700 ft) while watching alpine scenery roll past. Lunch is included on board as you pass lakes and glaciers before arriving in Zermatt. Your Travel Director gives you an overview of the town once you get there.

days.title: Zermatt
days.description: This day is completely free in Zermatt. You can spend time relaxing in the crisp mountain air and taking in the views, or you might want to do the optional trip to Klein Matterhorn for even more spectacular panoramic vistas from above.

days.title: Zermatt to Geneva
included: Train journey from Zermatt to Geneva
Orientation tour with Travel Director including Jet d'Eau and Flower Clock
days.description: A train takes you from Zermatt to Geneva, with changing scenery of mountains and valleys throughout the journey. After arriving, your Travel Director shows you around and points out the Jet d'Eau fountain and the famous Flower Clock. The afternoon is yours to walk through the old town's narrow lanes, stroll along the lake, or check out one of the museums. Dinner is at a local restaurant in the evening.

days.title: Geneva - Interlaken - Lucerne
included: Train journey from Geneva to Interlaken via Golden Pass route
Leisure time in Interlaken with views of Eiger, Mönch, and Jungfrau
Train journey from Interlaken to Lucerne via Brünig Pass
Orientation tour in Lucerne including Chapel Bridge and Lion Monument
optional: Swiss folklore show with fondue dinner
days.description: You'll travel from Geneva along the Golden Pass route, stopping in Interlaken at the base of the Eiger, Mönch, and Jungfrau peaks. After some time to take in the Bernese Oberland views, the route heads over the Brünig Pass to Lucerne on the lakefront. Your Travel Director gives you an orientation covering the Chapel Bridge and Lion Monument. Later you can spend the evening freely, or join an optional Swiss folklore show and fondue dinner.

days.title: Lucerne
included: Be My Guest experience at Küssnachter Alpenhof with Meyer family on their farm
optional: Optional Experience to nearby mountain peak
Optional Experience - carriage ride through Lucerne
days.meals: Breakfast, Dinner (Home-cooked meal at Küssnachter Alpenhof with Meyer family)
days.description: You have a free day in lakeside Lucerne with mountain peaks surrounding the town. Walk through medieval streets and look for Swiss chocolate shops, or consider optional outings to nearby peaks or a carriage ride through town. In the evening, the Meyer family welcomes you at Küssnachter Alpenhof for a Be My Guest experience, serving a home-cooked meal with your Travel Director and fellow travelers.

days.title: Lucerne to Zürich
days.description: It's time to say goodbye to Switzerland and the people you've traveled with. Your Travel Director gives you a ticket for the short train ride from Lucerne to Zürich Airport, which you can use anytime that works for your onward journey. Or if you prefer, you can join a coach transfer to the airport instead.

qa.question: Chillon Castle is not offered as an optional experience at Montreux. Would we be able to go on our own while we're there?
qa.answer: You'll only have approximately 25 minutes in Montreux. That's not enough time to visit Chillon Castle independently, since the castle is about 3 km (roughly a 40-minute walk or a short bus/taxi ride) from Montreux station. The schedule is very tight, and the group will be boarding the Golden Pass train with assigned seats, so you wouldn't be able to break away for a side trip at that point. If visiting Chillon Castle is important to you, the best option would be to plan it outside of the guided schedule, which is by extending your trip after the tour ends. That way, you'll have the flexibility to explore the castle at your own pace without worrying about missing the train connection. B

Some areas may feature uneven terrain such as cobblestones, hills, and stairs, as well as 1–3 hours of cumulative standing time. Guests should be able to get on and off the coach without assistance. The terrain involves medium walking distances with a mix of flat and uneven surfaces. The itinerary includes a combination of relaxed starts and some evening activities.

For departure, guests can choose to take the complimentary coach transfer operated by Trafalgar or a train ticket from Lucerne to Zurich Airport (ZRH) on the last day of the tour only.

name: 5-Day Group Garden Route & Addo Adventure Tour (one-way)

attributes.name: Adventure & Adrenaline
attributes.tip: Seek thrilling adventures that keep you moving

attributes.name: Group Tour
attributes.tip: Join a group and forge lifelong friendships

attributes.name: Fully Guided
attributes.tip: An experienced guide will be with you for the entire tour

attributes.tip: Travelers should be comfortable with somewhat-demanding activities

intro: Join us for the road trip of a lifetime! Earthstompers Adventures has been operating Garden Route & Addo tours since 2005. Our group Adventure Tour is a safe and affordable way to explore the Western Cape, Little Karoo, Whale Route, Addo Elephant National Park, and Route 62. The tour has a good mix of nature, culture and adventure, so you can experience the best the Garden Route has to offer. This tour starts in Cape Town every Monday, and ends in Gqeberha (Port Elizabeth) every Friday.

days.title: Cape Town to Cape Agulhas
optional: Shark cage diving, R4305 (includes one way transport to/from Cape Town; note: participants will miss the first half of Day 1)
Whale watching boat trip, R1580 (seasonal, July to November)
days.start_point: Cape Town, Western Cape, South Africa (Your address in Cape Town CBD, 06:00 - 07:30)
days.description: Leave Cape Town early Monday morning and head toward Hermanus along the coast. Stop at Betties Bay first to see African penguins up close, then spend the afternoon in Hermanus checking out shops, restaurants, and local markets. Before the day ends, drive to Cape Agulhas at the southern tip of Africa to stand where the Indian and Atlantic Oceans meet.

days.title: Cape Agulhas to Oudtshoorn
days.description: Travel to Oudtshoorn using Route 62, which happens to be South Africa's longest wine route. Have lunch and do a wine tasting at a local winery before checking into accommodation on a working game farm. As the sun sets, take a tour of the ostrich farm with mountain views around you.

days.title: Oudtshoorn to Sedgefield
included: Canoeing and hiking in Wilderness National Park
days.description: After breakfast, cross over the Outeniqua Mountain pass and head into Wilderness National Park with canoes. Paddle up the Touw River through forest for about 40 minutes and watch for birds. Then leave the canoes and walk the 2 km boardwalk to a waterfall and rock pools. Later in the afternoon, explore Sedgefield and its beaches.

days.title: Sedgefield to Knysna to Tsitsikamma to Addo

intro:
Winner Tour of the Year Award 2019 - South Africa

Join us for the road trip of a lifetime! Earthstompers Adventures has been operating Garden Route & Addo tours since 2005. Our group Adventure Tour is a safe and affordable way to explore the Western Cape, Little Karoo, Whale Route, Addo Elephant National Park, and Route 62. The tour has a good mix of nature, culture and adventure, so you can experience the best the Garden Route has to offer. This tour starts & ends in Cape Town, and departs every Monday.

*Please note that this itinerary is sometimes done in a different order!*

days.title: Cape Town to Cape Agulhas
optional: Shark cage diving, R4305 (includes one way transport to/from Cape Town; participants will miss the first half of Day 1)
Whale watching boat trip (in season, July-November), R1580
days.start_point: Cape Town, Western Cape, South Africa (Your address in Cape Town CBD, 06:00 - 07:30)
days.description: You'll depart Cape Town early Monday morning and head south along the coast toward some different landscapes. The first stop is Betties Bay where you can see a colony of African penguins up close, which is a real highlight for wildlife viewing. After that, you'll spend the afternoon in Hermanus, a seaside town known for whale watching if you happen to visit between July and November. From there, continue down to Cape Agulhas, the southern tip of Africa, where you can stand at the viewpoint and see where the Indian and Atlantic Oceans actually meet.

days.title: Cape Agulhas to Oudtshoorn
days.description: This day takes you through Route 62, South Africa's longest wine route, as you head toward Oudtshoorn in the Little Karoo region. Plan to stop at a local winery for lunch and wine tasting to get a feel for what the area produces. You'll check in at accommodation on a working game farm, then as evening comes around, take a tour of the ostrich farm where you'll get views of the Outeniqua and Swartberg mountain ranges in the background.

days.title: Oudtshoorn to Sedgefield
included: Canoeing and hiking in Wilderness National Park
days.description: After breakfast, you'll cross the Outeniqua Mountain pass and make your way to Wilderness National Park. Once there, you'll paddle canoes up the Touw River through indigenous forest for roughly 40 minutes, watching for birds along the way. After paddling, you'll leave the canoes behind and hike about 2 km on a boardwalk that leads to a waterfall and some rock pools. Later in the afternoon, head over to Sedgefield where you can take in the expansive views and spend time on the beaches.

days.title: Sedgefield to Addo
optional: 216m Bloukrans bungee jump (world's highest bungee jump bridge), R1690
days.description: You'll head to Knysna by driving through the lush Lake District area of the Garden Route. Once there, visit the Knysna Heads viewpoint for great views of the river estuary and Indian Ocean. The Bloukrans Bridge is your next stop, which is known as the site of the world's highest bungee jump at 216 meters if you're interested in trying it. Around midday, spend time in Tsitsikamma National Park where you can hike through indigenous forest, use the suspension bridge, or swim depending on what appeals to you. In the afternoon, head into Big 5 country as you drive toward Addo.

days.title: Addo
included: Entrance and 2-3 hour drive with tour vehicle through Addo Elephant National Park
optional: 2-hour open vehicle game drive with Addo field guide, R540
days.description: Spend your morning on a 2 to 3 hour drive through Addo Elephant National Park, exploring the 28,000 hectare reserve. You'll see roughly 600 elephants and other wildlife like Cape buffalo, lions, black rhinos, warthogs, zebras, kudus, and hartebeests. After your game viewing in the morning, drive back toward the Garden Route and stay overnight in either Wilderness or Sedgefield.

days.title: Wilderness to Cape Town
optional: 10,000-foot tandem skydive, R4050 (extra R1050 for video)
Sandboarding on South Africa's longest dune, R600
days.description: After breakfast, you'll stop in Mossel Bay to spend time on the beaches there. The Cape St. Blaize trail is good for hiking if you want to see the cliffs overlooking the Indian Ocean, or check out the Diaz Museum complex which covers early European exploration around Africa's tip. For those wanting more adventure, there's skydiving from 10,000 feet or sandboarding on South Africa's longest dune. You'll arrive back in Cape Town by early evening.

reviews.body: Of course the wet and wild weather did not help but other things to consider 1. If you wish to include Addo in the...
reviews.reply:
Good day, Sue

Thank you for taking the time to share your feedback about your experience on our 6 day Garden Route & Addo group adventure tour. We are truly sorry to hear that aspects of the tour did not meet your expectations. As a small, owner run company offering a very personal service, this is very disappointing for the whole team to read, and we truly take every review, good or bad, to heart.

The storms and rainfall experienced during your trip were some of the most severe we have encountered since Earthstompers began operating in 2005, and whilst your group was able to visit all the destinations on our tour itinerary, we understand that the conditions were far from ideal and that attractions like the suspension bridge at Tsitsikamma was not accessable, for visitors' safety. We're sorry that the weather negatively impacted your trip. Like the guests on tour, we are also disappointed when the weather doesn’t cooperate, as our main goal is always to create happy, memorable experiences. Unfortunately, difficult weather can really put a damper on things.

Regarding the itinerary, our Garden Route tours are designed as balanced small group experiences that showcase a wide variety of South Africa’s landscapes, towns, highlights, and adventures, with the Addo safari experience included as one component of the journey. We wish time and budget were never a factor, as you could easily spend much longer exploring the Garden Route region in depth. However, over the past 20 years of operating these tours, we’ve learned that many guests have limited travel time, and that 6 days is generally the maximum amount of time most group tour guests have available for this region. Our scheduled group tours are therefore designed to showcase many highlights and regions within a relatively short period of time. At the same time, we understand that not all travellers are the same, and some guests do prefer a slower pace or longer stays in certain areas. We always aim to be as transparent as possible and provide guests with detailed information before booking. For example, we clearly outline the driving distances and daily itinerary breakdowns on our website.

For guests looking for a more wildlife-focused or experience or more leisure time in destinations, we recommend one of our dedicated safari packages, safari extensions, or private tours. These options allow for greater itinerary flexibility and a slower pace. Many of our group tour guests book a safari extension after their Garden Route experience, where we create a safari-based package for them following their Garden Route experience.

Regarding lunch stops. We appreciate your feedback regarding the lunch stops and are sorry that the style of lunches did not fully match your preference for more on-the-go meals. This can sometimes be a difficult balance to maintain. We always try to accommodate different travel styles, as some guests prefer quick, on-the-go lunches, while others enjoy slowing down and experiencing fresh local food at lunch stops along the route. Many guests see these meal stops as an important part of the overall travel experience. We agree that every day does not require a sit-down lunch stop. Our guides usually offer a combination of sit-down and on-the-go meals as some days are more relaxed than others. It's tricky, to cater for every individual's needs on a group tour with multiple individuals/couples from all over the world.

We are very sorry and disappointed to hear that your experience with Mark was not entirely positive, and we truly appreciate you taking the time to share this feedback with us. We never want any guest to feel unheard, uncomfortable, or frustrated during their travels, and we are sorry that parts of the experience left you feeling this way. While Mark is often highly praised for his knowledge, passion, and enthusiasm, we completely understand that his communication and guiding style did not align with your personal preferences on this occasion. It was also a particularly challenging week weather wise, which added extra pressure and stress for both guests and guides alike. Having personally guided hundreds of guests along the Garden Route myself, I understand how demanding it can be for a guide to drive safely in severe rain, while at the same time organising logistics, communicating with guests, and trying to keep everyone happy. The added pressure (like the difficult weather on this occasion) can sometimes become overwhelming. That said, this should never take away from the overall guest experience, and we do take your comments and feedback seriously. We will be discussing your feedback with Mark internally and using it as a constructive opportunity for reflection and growth.

We genuinely appreciate your feedback, as it helps us continue refining our tours and communication so that guests can choose the experience best suited to their travel style and expectations. We do hope that despite the challenges, there were still moments of beauty and memorable experiences during your time exploring South Africa. We want all our guests to have the best possible time on our tours and it is very disappointing when we don't succeed. Your comments are noted and we will continue to discuss and find ways to improve.

Best Regards,
Hendrik Human-Owner

intro:
The Philippines is an absolute gem, and we’ve crafted the ultimate 10-day Philippines group tour that’s packed with adventure, culture, and jaw-dropping scenery. From exploring the UNESCO-listed Underground River to island-hopping to some of the world’s most stunning destinations, this trip has it all. You’ll cook with locals, climb coconut trees, and even camp on a private beach under the stars.


Snorkel with turtles in Port Barton, float through crystal-clear waters, and be amazed by El Nido’s limestone cliffs. Whether you’re looking to unwind or push your limits, this bucket-list adventure has it all. Oh, and did we mention it’s been voted the #1 tour in the Philippines AND Asia? Ready for the trip of a lifetime? Let’s go!

days.description: The first day of your 2-day Islander Experience kicks off with island hopping around Port Barton. You'll visit a local school to meet students and see how your support makes a difference, so bring or pick up school supplies beforehand (or make a monetary donation). Later, you'll gather around a fire at a private beach camp for grilled meals and sleep in tents right on the beach.

days.title: Port Barton - Island Experience Day 2
included: Snorkelling around coral reefs and with turtles
days.description: Day two continues with snorkeling around coral reefs and swimming alongside turtles. You'll also experience jungle waterfall showers and explore some tiny islands. The specific activities can shift depending on when you're departing, so there's some flexibility built in here.

days.title: Port Barton to El Nido
days.description: After breakfast, you'll have time to soak in your surroundings before heading to El Nido by van. The drive gets you to this place surrounded by islands and towering cliffs. You'll check into a boutique-style hostel, then head to a beach restaurant where you can eat and hang out with your tour group.

days.title: El Nido - Filipino Cultural Day
included: Jungle hike with flora and fauna education
Filipino dance and children's games learning
days.meals: Breakfast, Lunch (Prepared during cooking class activities)
days.description: You're doing a jungle hike through the rainforest to reach an exclusive jungle hut where you'll participate in cooking authentic Filipino food, coconut tree climbing, traditional stick fighting, coconut shaving, learning dances and children's games, and coconut leaf weaving. There's an optional zipline between islands if you're interested, followed by relaxation at Las Cabanas Beach.

days.title: El Nido - Island Hopping
included: Island hopping boat tour around El Nido bay
days.meals: Breakfast, Lunch (Freshly prepared food onboard during island hopping)
days.description: You'll board a boat to explore the tiny islands scattered throughout El Nido bay. Snorkeling in the clear blue waters happens alongside your new friends, and you'll have freshly prepared food served onboard during the island hopping.

days.title: El Nido - Canopy Walk & Relaxation
included: Canopy walk to viewpoint overlooking El Nido bay and Cadlao Island
days.description: A short canopy walk takes you up to famous cliffs with panoramic views overlooking El Nido bay and Cadlao Island. After the hike, you'll get a traditional Filipino massage near the beach to work out tired muscles. The rest of your day is open for relaxing and enjoying the surroundings.

days.title: El Nido to Puerto Princesa - Departure
included: Private van transfer to Puerto Princesa
optional: Flight from El Nido to alternative destinations via Air Swift
days.description: Your final day includes a private van transfer back to Puerto Princesa, departing from your accommodation at 7 AM. If you'd rather fly out of El Nido instead, you can book through the Air Swift website (there's an extra cost but it saves you the Puerto Princesa drive).

intro:
Enjoy our included overnight adventure in iconic Monument Valley, experience the real Wild Wild West, immerse yourselves in the amazing Utah landscapes of  Zion, Bryce, Arches and Canyonlands National Parks. Marvel at the world most famous slot Canyon - Antelope Canyon, visit Horshoe Bend and stare into the mysterious depths of the Grand Canyon before heading back to Fabulous Las Vegas!

This tour has a free downloadable App with tour commentary in French, German, Spanish, Italian, Mandarin, Korean, Japanese.

Live commentary is provided in English. 

New Tour Option- Purchase 8 seats and have a fully private tour with selected ticket type.

days.title: Zion National Park
days.start_point: Palms Casino Resort, 4321 W Flamingo Rd, Las Vegas, Nevada 89103, United States (Tour pick up area, 07:00)
days.description: You'll leave Las Vegas early and drive toward Utah's Zion National Park. The landscape changes as you get closer, with massive canyon walls and red sandstone cliffs coming into view against the sky. Once you arrive, you can choose how to spend your time. The Emerald Pools offer a shorter walk with water features and shade, or if you're up for something more involved, the Narrows let you hike right through the river canyon at whatever pace works for you.

days.title: Bryce National Park
included: Rim walk at Bryce National Park
days.description: Drive up to Bryce National Park, climbing to 8,000 feet elevation. Walk along the rim to take in the hoodoos, those unique sandstone spires that rise from the natural amphitheater below. If you're up for it, you can hike down into the hoodoos themselves for a closer look at this geological landscape.

days.title: Day 3
days.description: Spend two days checking out Arches and Canyonlands National Parks near Moab. In Arches, you'll hike up to the famous Delicate Arch and see over 2,000 other arches scattered across the landscape. Then head to Canyonlands where the Green and Colorado Rivers meet. The area has options like a guided sunset jeep tour or an optional canyoneering adventure. You'll also learn about Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid, who hid out in these canyons in the late 1800s, and explore Moab itself, the region's adventure hub.

days.title: Monument Valley
included: Navajo guided 4x4 jeep tour of Monument Valley
days.description: Start the morning with an optional visit to Antelope Canyon and Horseshoe Bend, then stop at a Navajo trading post. Follow the Colorado River through the painted desert toward the Grand Canyon, one of the seven natural wonders. Once there, choose your activity: take a helicopter ride for a birds eye view, walk the rim at sunset, hike into the canyon itself, or sit at a rim café and watch the light change before sunset.

days.title: Antelope Canyon and Grand Canyon
days.description: Drive back toward Las Vegas along Route 66, traveling through more Southwest scenery. You'll arrive back around 4 to 5pm, ending your trip through Utah and Arizona's natural landscapes.

qa.question: Is camping or hotel accommodation available on this tour? Is it a round trip departure and return from Las Vegas, or are there options to depart from Vegas and return to another city? Flights / Transfers
qa.answer: Camping is available on this tour from April through October. We provide tents, thick foam camp pads and all other equipment except a sleeping bag, which you can bring your own or rent one with your guide for $40 on day one (advanced notification required). No single person supplement is charged. Tents are twin share and solo travelers will be paired with another client of the same sex. Lodging at 3 star and above hotels is available for an additional fee. Campgrounds are privately owned and operated and offer very high standards. Most campgrounds on these tours have full bathrooms and hot showers, as well as electricity and charging points for cameras and cell phones, etc. Most campgrounds have complimentary Wi-Fi. This tour begins and ends at The Palms Casino - East Side Coach Loading Curb- 4321 W Flamingo Road, Las Vegas, NV 89103.
