name: 13-Day Japan Tour: Tokyo, Mount Fuji, Kyoto, Nara, Osaka & Beyond

attributes.name: City & Culture
attributes.tip: Immerse yourself in rich history and local traditions

attributes.name: Group Tour
attributes.tip: Join a group and forge lifelong friendships

attributes.name: Fully Guided
attributes.tip: An experienced guide will be with you for the entire tour

intro:
Get ready for an unforgettable 13-day tour of Japan – the ultimate adventure designed for solo travellers who want to experience a different side of this fascinating country.


­One moment you are under the neon glow of Tokyo’s arcades, the next you are sipping matcha in the temples of Kyoto – every stop on this 13-day itinerary offers a fresh perspective on Japan’s culture.


You’ll zip across the country on bullet trains, soak in onsens, and master sushimaking and calligraphy. Whether it’s cycling through Kyoto like a local or belting out karaoke in Osaka, this journey is all about truly immersing yourself in Japanese culture. Led by our epic local Adventure Leaders, you’ll hit all the highlights, uncover local secrets, and make memories (and friends) to last a lifetime.

days.title: Tokyo
optional: Evening drinks at a local bar
days.start_point: 12 浅草3丁目4番 台東区, Tokyo Prefecture, Japan (Meet your group in front of the hostel)
days.description: You'll arrive in Tokyo and connect with your group during an afternoon briefing where your Adventure Leader fills you in on what's coming up. After that, you'll head to a welcome dinner with your travel crew to get to know everyone and start the adventure.

days.title: Tokyo
days.description: The morning starts with a hands-on sushi masterclass taught by local experts, and you'll eat what you make for lunch. Later in the afternoon, you'll visit the peaceful Meiji Shrine, then walk through Harajuku's colorful streets with vintage shops and quirky finds. Next you'll see the famous Shibuya Crossing and the Hachiko statue. Your afternoon is free after that to wander around or try optional go-kart racing if you're interested.

days.title: Tokyo
optional: Akihabara Maid Cafe (can be booked with Adventure Leader)
Sumo experience with dinner (must be pre-booked)
Dinner at Hoppy Street with izakaya and doburoku
days.description: Start your day at Yanaka Ginza, a retro shopping street with local stalls and street food. From there, head to Akihabara, Japan's electronics hub packed with arcades and anime stores where you can challenge your crew. You'll try a maid cafe for the quirky culture, then visit the historic Sensoji Temple in Asakusa and walk Nakamise-dori street. In the evening, you can either opt for a sumo experience with ex-wrestlers and chanko nabe dinner, or explore Hoppy Street's izakayas on your own.

days.title: Mt Fuji - Shimoyoshida - Oshino Hakkai
included: Hike up to Arakura Fuji Sengen Shrine
days.description: You'll take the train from Shinjuku to Shimoyoshida and hike to Arakura Fuji Sengen Shrine with its iconic pagoda and views of Mt Fuji (weather permitting). Then head to Oshino Hakkai, a traditional village with crystal-clear ponds and old thatched-roof houses. There's time to explore at your own pace and grab lunch before heading back to Tokyo for a free evening.

days.title: Tokyo to Shimoda
days.description: You'll travel to the coastal town of Shimoda with light luggage stored in lockers. Start with a Shimoda Bay sightseeing cruise along the coastline where you can feed birds. Walk Perry Road with its traditional houses, cafes and shops. Visit the Museum of Black Ships to see over 3,000 artifacts about Japan's transition to international trade, plus Ryosenji Temple where the Treaty of Shimoda was signed. Take the Shimoda Ropeway for panoramic views of the city and mountains, possibly catching a sunset. End with an onsen experience at your traditional hotel.

days.title: Shimoda - Atami - Kyoto
optional: Explore Atami - seaside city on Japan's Izu Peninsula
days.description: Say goodbye to Shimoda and travel to Atami where you'll have free time for lunch and exploring. Then you'll board the shinkansen bullet train to Kyoto, Japan's cultural heart. After arriving, your Adventure Leader takes you on a short orientation walk to get your bearings. In the evening, you'll go karaoke with your crew to kick off your stay in Kyoto.

days.title: Kyoto
included: Visit Kiyomizu-dera Temple (UNESCO World Heritage Site)
days.description: Begin with a traditional Japanese tea ceremony where you'll watch the instructor's precise movements, then whisk your own matcha bowl paired with sweet treats. Next you'll head to Kiyomizu-dera, a major Buddhist temple and UNESCO site with sweeping views from its wooden stage. There are shops nearby for lunch. In the afternoon, your Adventure Leader guides you through Gion, Kyoto's geisha district with narrow lanes and traditional wooden buildings. Your evening is free to browse Nishiki Market, shop at Teramachi, visit the Samurai Ninja Museum, or catch a performance.

days.title: Kyoto
days.description: This morning is yours to explore Kyoto at your own pace with help from your Adventure Leader via WhatsApp. You can stroll the Philosopher's Path and its temples, head to Arashiyama for the bamboo grove or Monkey Park, take a trip to Nara to see Todaiji Temple and meet friendly deer, or try another tea ceremony or kimono rental. In the afternoon, you'll regroup for a hands-on calligraphy class where you'll learn Japanese brush writing from a local teacher and create something to take home.

days.title: Kyoto to Hiroshima
included: Meditation session led by Buddhist monk
Visit The Golden Pavilion at Kinkaku-ji
optional: Okonomiyaki dinner (can be booked with Adventure Leader)
days.description: You'll hop on bikes and explore Kyoto like a local on a half-day ride through quieter streets to a serene Zen temple. There you'll join a meditation session led by a Buddhist monk, followed by a calming tea ceremony. After a quick lunch, you'll head to Kinkaku-ji, the Golden Pavilion, with its shimmering reflection in the pond. Then you'll take the bullet train west to Hiroshima, check into the hostel, and rest before an optional dinner at Okonomiyaki Village where chefs prepare Hiroshima's signature dishes.

days.title: Hiroshima - Miyajima Island
included: Visit The Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum & Atomic Bomb Dome
optional: Hike down Mt Misen through forest trails
days.description: You'll take a train and short ferry to Miyajima Island, famous for its giant torii gate that appears to float in the sea. At low tide, you'll walk across the sand to stand right beneath it. Then ride the Miyajima Ropeway up Mt Misen for incredible views, with the option to hike down through forest if you want. After free time for lunch, you'll catch the ferry back and visit the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum and Atomic Bomb Dome. The evening is free back at the hostel.

days.title: Hiroshima - Okayama - Osaka
days.description: You'll travel by bullet train from Hiroshima to Okayama and explore the beautifully preserved Kurashiki Bikan Quarter, an Edo period district with canals, traditional streets and cozy cafes. Wander at your own pace, try local sweets and browse shops. Visit Korakuen Garden, one of Japan's Three Great Gardens with peaceful grounds. After collecting your luggage, you'll continue to Shin Osaka and drop bags before the evening is free to rest or explore Shinsekai, Osaka's retro entertainment district, and try kushikatsu.

days.title: Osaka
days.description: Start with a short orientation walk to Shinsaibashi, one of Osaka's liveliest shopping streets. Take it in and grab lunch at a local spot. The rest of the afternoon is free to explore at your own pace, whether that's Osaka Castle for city views, Umeda's buzzing streets, or the National Museum to learn about Japan's history and culture. This evening you'll come together for a special farewell dinner with your group to share memories, swap photos and reflect on your time across Japan.

qa.question: How strict is the age limit? I am an active 60+ year old?
qa.answer: In regards to the age range, the 13-Day Japan Budget Tour is advertised for travellers aged 18–55 because of the overall travel style, accommodation, pace, and the typical demographics of the group. Standard accommodation on this tour is shared dorm rooms in hostels, but we do offer a single room upgrade if you do not fancy sharing. You could expect to walk up to 20,000 steps per day and the itinerary is jam-packed! As a result, the overall pace and group dynamic may be less suited to those looking for a more relaxed travel experience. That said, we can review travellers over the advertised age range on a case-by-case basis. Before confirming, we'd just ask you to complete a Tour Suitability Form so we can ensure the pace and style of the trip will be a good fit for you.

qa.question: How much the upgrade for 1 room 1 bed for the tour please?
qa.answer: The Single Room Upgrade is priced at £1,100 GBP. This upgrades travellers from sharing dorm rooms, to private rooms throughout the tour. The only exception here is 1 night in Shimoda, where the group stays at a traditional style guesthouse and enjoys an onsen experience. C

qa.question: Is breakfast included in the tour? Can it be added? If not, how do travellers normally handle breakfast?
qa.answer: We can't add breakfast in but there are many places nearby to get breakfast from in the area. Most travellers just grab something to go usually at a 711 store where there is plenty of choice.

qa.question: We are interested in this trip with upgraded accommodations. how much does it cost/person?
qa.answer: We can absolutely look at upgraded accommodation for you. Will there be two of you travelling? Are you looking for a Double or Twin room? Is there a particular time of year you're hoping to travel? If you let us know your preferred dates, we'd be more than happy to build a full quote for you. Just so you know, you can secure your place on any of our tours with only a small deposit, and the final balance won't be due until 70 days before departure, giving you plenty of time to plan and organise everything for your trip.

intro: A 6 day tour around the ring road, stopping at all of the highlights that Iceland has to offer

days.title: Reykjavik to South Coast
included: Walk the rift valley at Þingvellir National Park
Watch Strokkur geyser erupt at Geysir hot spring area
days.description: You'll get picked up in Reykjavik at 8:00 am and head out to Iceland's Golden Circle. Start by walking through the rift valley at Þingvellir National Park, then watch Strokkur geyser erupt before seeing Gullfoss waterfall. After lunch, drive south to see Seljalandsfoss and Skógafoss waterfalls. The day wraps up at Reynisfjara beach where you can walk along the black sand and check out the dramatic basalt columns. You'll stay overnight near Kirkjubæjarklaustur.

days.title: South Coast to Southeast
optional: Crystal Ice Cave journey (October to April, +€173)
days.description: Today is all about glaciers and ice. You'll cross the Eldhraun lava field before reaching Vatnajökull National Park, which has Europe's biggest glacier. At Jökulsárlón Glacier Lagoon, watch massive icebergs calve and drift across the water. Just beyond is Diamond Beach where glacier ice chunks wash up on black volcanic sand. You can do an optional glacier hike (April to October) or explore an ice cave (October to April). You'll overnight in the Southeast.

days.title: Southeast to Eastfjords
included: Experience traditional Viking-style hot spring bathhouse
optional: Dining on fresh local ingredients at Wilderness Center open kitchen
days.description: You're heading into East Iceland where sharp mountain peaks and quiet fjords show up instead of glaciers. Dj\u00fapivogur is a peaceful fishing village with outdoor art installations worth checking out. Then you'll pass through Egilsta\u00f0ir, the largest town in the east, near the legend-haunted Lagarfl\u00f3t lake. The day ends at the Wilderness Center, a unique highland retreat with restored farmhouses, museum exhibitions, and a traditional Viking-style hot spring bathhouse. You could also stay in Egilsta\u00f0ir if you prefer.

days.title: Eastfjords to Akureyri
optional: Earth Lagoon geothermal baths (€46 for Mývatn Nature Baths; Forest Lagoon in Akureyri until end of June 2026)
days.description: You're driving from East to North Iceland through some really nice scenery. Begin at Stud\u00f3lagil Canyon with its impressive basalt columns towering above turquoise river. After that, continue through N\u00e1maskar\u00f0 geothermal area with boiling mud pools and colorful mineral deposits. Stop at Lake M\u00fdvatn, a shallow volcanic lake with small islands and lots of birdlife, then explore Dimmuborgir's dramatic lava pillars. Finish up at Go\u00f0afoss waterfall before you arrive in Akureyri, the capital of the North.

days.title: Akureyri to Laugarbakki
optional: Whale-watching boat tour from Eyjafj\u00f6r\u00f0ur Fjord (+€100 Summer; +€84 Winter)
days.description: Start with an optional whale-watching boat tour from Eyjafj\u00f6r\u00f0ur Fjord early in the morning (98% success rate for spotting humpback whales, dolphins, and porpoises). Head north to Siglufj\u00f6r\u00f0ur, Iceland's northernmost town and former herring capital, with a colorful harbor. Drive around the Tr\u00f6llaskagi Peninsula to see some nice coastal scenery with rugged cliffs and ski areas. A scenic detour through Skagafj\u00f6r\u00f0ur brings fjord views before you settle in near Laugarbakki.

days.title: Laugarbakki to Reykjavik
days.description: On the final day, you'll explore West Iceland starting with a short hike up Gr\u00e1br\u00f3k volcano crater for sweeping views over lava fields. Visit Reykholt, the historic home of Snorri Sturluson, medieval historian and saga writer. Stop at Deildartunguhver, Europe's most powerful hot spring, then check out Hraunfossar with its hundreds of tiny streams seeping from a lava field and the dramatic Barnafoss rapids nearby. Round off your journey at a traditional Icelandic horse farm before the scenic drive back through Hvalfj\u00f6r\u00f0ur, arriving in Reykjavik around 5-6 pm.

intro:
Visit India and follow the famous Golden Triangle. Enjoy the perfect introduction to India's three most popular destinations - Delhi, Agra and Jaipur - as we explore the icons and discover the secrets of this fascinating region. Experience the history of massive forts, the opulence and splendour of Rajasthan's palaces, the bustle and buzz of markets and bazaars, and the traditions of a heritage homestay. Travel through a land full of contrasts on this compact India tour, jam-packed with unforgettable highlights.

This tour is a guaranteed departure, so even if you are the only one booked onto this tour, you will still be guaranteed to depart!

days.title: Delhi
included: Visit Jama Mosque with interior exploration
Visit Raj Ghat (Mahatma Gandhi cremation site)
Visit Qutub Minar (UNESCO World Heritage Site)
Visit Humayun's Tomb (UNESCO World Heritage Site)
days.description: Your driver picks you up from the hotel in an air-conditioned car to start exploring Delhi. The day begins at Jama Mosque where you'll walk through the interior with your guide, then head to Raj Ghat, the site where Mahatma Gandhi was cremated. From there, you'll see the Qutub Minar, a UNESCO-listed structure showing Afghan architectural style, followed by Humayun's Tomb, another UNESCO World Heritage Site. The day wraps up at India Gate, a 1931 memorial built to honor Indian soldiers.

days.title: Delhi to Agra
days.description: Start with breakfast at your hotel before heading out to Agra. The drive takes you through the region, and once you arrive, you'll have time to settle into your accommodation. Grab lunch on your own, then meet your private guide for the afternoon. From there, you'll check out Agra Fort, a massive red sandstone fortress that Emperor Akbar built back in the 16th century. After exploring the fort, you'll walk through Itmad-ud-Daulah, an intricate marble mausoleum with detailed inlay work. Later in the afternoon or early evening, head to Mehtab Bagh to wander the riverside parks and catch views of the Taj Mahal from across the river before the day winds down.

days.title: Agra to Jaipur
days.meals: Breakfast, Lunch (Lunch en-route Agra to Jaipur)
days.description: You start early to catch the sunrise at the Taj Mahal with your guide and spend time taking in this beautiful symbol of love. After heading back to your hotel for breakfast, the drive to Jaipur begins. Upon arrival, you check into your hotel and have the evening free to relax. You overnight in Jaipur.

days.title: Jaipur
days.description: Following breakfast, you meet your private guide to check out Jaipur's main highlights. Amber Fort comes first to learn about its history, then the City Palace in the city center, which combines Rajasthani and Mughal architectural styles and holds collections of textiles, costumes, and armor. After that you see the Hawa Mahal or Palace of Winds, built so royal women could watch processions without being seen. The day finishes at Jantar Mantar, the stargazing observatory that Maharaja Jai Singh built. You overnight in Jaipur.

days.title: Jaipur to Delhi
days.description: After breakfast at your hotel, you're transferred back to Delhi and driven directly to the airport for your departure.

intro: History meets the new age in vibrant London. You’re in for a royal time at Windsor Castle and the Changing of the Guard at Buckingham Palace. See life unfold from the water as you cruise to Greenwich and feel the buzz and spirit of one of London's oldest markets - Borough Market.

days.title: London
days.description: You'll arrive in London and have the day to yourself. Walk around at your own pace, check out neighborhoods that interest you, grab lunch wherever looks good. This evening you'll meet your Travel Director and the rest of the group for a welcome dinner to kick things off.

days.description: Start with an orientation tour that takes you past Big Ben, Houses of Parliament, Westminster Abbey, and Buckingham Palace. Then you'll head to St. James's Palace to watch the Old Guard parade and Changing of the Guard. The afternoon is free for you to explore using your travel pass, or you can join optional activities in Soho or the National Gallery. By evening, you'll have time to wander Covent Garden before dinner.

days.title: London
optional: Guided tour of St. Paul's Cathedral with Local Specialist
days.description: Begin your day at Borough Market where you can try different food stalls, everything from fresh pastries to street food from around the world. days.title: London
included: Guided visit to Westminster Abbey with Local Specialist

The day wraps up with English cream tea in The Orangery, where you can relax surrounded by formal gardens.

days.title: London

name: USA: LA to the Bay

attributes.name: City & Culture
attributes.tip: Immerse yourself in rich history and local traditions

attributes.name: Group Tour

intro: This California trip threads together big cities, open desert and some of the West’s most iconic landscapes into one seriously stacked journey. Start in LA, hike the Grand Canyon, swing through Vegas and roll through Yosemite National Park before arriving in San Francisco. From neon lights and canyon views to national park landscapes and coastal energy, the scenery keeps shifting in the best possible way.

days.title: Los Angeles
days.meals: Lunch (Farmers Market - legendary lunch spot by The Grove with local small businesses)
days.description: Your LA adventure kicks off with lunch at Farmers Market near The Grove, where you'll find plenty of casual dining spots and local vendors. From there, head to Beverly Hills to walk around the tree-lined streets and high-end shops. Stop by the TCL Chinese Theatre to see the Hollywood connection to the Oscars, then make your way to Santa Monica Pier. Spend the rest of the afternoon at the beach checking out the classic pier rides and soaking in the coastal atmosphere before heading back.

days.title: Los Angeles to San Diego
included: Stop at SoCal white sand beach
days.description: This morning you'll drive south along the Pacific Coast Highway, which takes you through some really nice coastal scenery. Stop at one of the white sand beaches along the way to stretch your legs and enjoy the ocean. Later, arrive in San Diego and explore the historic Gas Lamp District once the sun sets. The area has plenty of restaurants, shops, and galleries in restored 19th century buildings, so you'll have time to wander around and grab dinner.

days.title: San Diego to Phoenix
included: Arizonan BBQ dinner at Rustler's Rooste
days.description: Leave the California coast behind and head inland to Phoenix. The drive takes you into Arizona desert terrain where the landscape shifts completely. Phoenix sits in the Valley of the Sun and gets around 300 days of sunshine annually, so expect hot, dry weather. After checking into your hotel, head to Rustler's Rooste for an Arizona BBQ dinner with views of the city lights.

days.title: Phoenix to Grand Canyon
included: Hot air balloon ride over Valley of the Sun
Champagne breakfast (included with hot air balloon)
days.meals: Breakfast (Champagne breakfast (included with hot air balloon ride))
days.description: Start early with a hot air balloon ride over the Valley of the Sun, where you'll float above the desert landscape at sunrise. The experience includes champagne and breakfast once you land. Later that day, drive north to the Grand Canyon and position yourself for the sunset. The colors changing over the canyon at day's end are something you won't forget.

days.title: Grand Canyon
days.description: Spend your full day at the Grand Canyon exploring the landscape on foot. The area's a UNESCO World Heritage site with multiple hiking options depending on your fitness level. You can hike various trails along the rim or into the canyon itself. If you prefer, there's an optional helicopter tour available that shows you the canyon from above and gives a different perspective of the vast terrain.

days.title: Grand Canyon to Las Vegas
included: Light and laser show at Fremont Street
days.description: After the Grand Canyon, drive west and stop in historic Seligman along Route 66. This small town has old-school Americana vibes with vintage diners and quirky roadside attractions. Continue on to Las Vegas, where you'll tour the Strip checking out the major casinos and hotels. Grab photos at the famous Vegas sign, then head to Fremont Street in the evening for a light and laser show on the old downtown casinos.

days.title: Las Vegas
days.description: You have the full day to explore Las Vegas however you like. Visit the Bellagio fountains and watch the choreographed water shows, or take a gondola ride at the Venetian through indoor canals. Check out the Luxor's Egyptian pyramid and sphinx. If you're interested, there's an optional Elvis wedding ceremony available. Later, go out with your travel group for a night exploring Vegas nightlife and casinos.

days.title: Las Vegas to Oakhurst
days.description: Head out of Vegas early and drive through Barstow toward the Sierra Nevada mountains. Stop at an In-N-Out Burger along the way for a quick lunch or snack. Continue to Oakhurst, a quieter mountain town near Yosemite's south entrance. After checking into your hotel, you can relax and maybe take a dip in the pool if you want.

days.title: Oakhurst to Yosemite National Park
days.description: Explore Yosemite National Park starting with an orientation of Yosemite Valley. You'll see Half Dome, El Capitan, and Cook's Meadow from the valley floor. Then choose how you want to explore further: hiking various trails or mountain biking through the park. Return to Oakhurst later in the day, and if you want, spend some time at the hotel pool before dinner.

days.title: Oakhurst to San Francisco
days.description: Leave Oakhurst and drive toward San Francisco, heading through the Sierra foothills and into the Bay Area. Once you arrive in San Francisco, spend time walking the hilly streets and checking out different neighborhoods. This evening your travel group has an included dinner together to celebrate the end of your West Coast journey.

days.title: San Francisco
days.description: Your tour ends today in San Francisco. Pack up and head to the airport or your next destination, taking with you memories of two weeks on the West Coast from LA beaches to Yosemite mountains to Vegas casinos.

intro:
Vietnam Intro is the most amazing way to experience Vietnam! You’ll discover crazy Hanoi, experience the stunning Ha Long Bay, go sea kayaking, crab fishing with traditional fisherman, soak up fascinating local culture, learn to cook delicious Vietnamese food and much more. Plus you’ll have an awesome group leader with you from the moment you step off the plane, an instant group of friends to share your adventure with and help with all your onward travel. Get ready for the trip of a lifetime! 

+ Our tours are all 100% Carbon Neutral!

days.title: Hanoi
days.description: You'll land in Hanoi and get picked up at the airport for your transfer to the hotel. The rest of the day is yours to shake off the jet lag and get familiar with your group. Most people use this time to rest or grab dinner nearby and settle in for the night.

days.title: Hanoi
included: Walking and rickshaw tour of Hanoi
days.description: This morning you're walking through Hanoi's chaotic streets on foot and by rickshaw, soaking in the vibrant energy and stopping for street food along the way. In the evening, you'll head out for dinner and experience some of the city's best nightlife spots with the group.

days.title: Hanoi to Ha Long Bay
included: Overnight Ha Long Bay boat trip
days.description: You're traveling to Ha Long Bay where you'll board an overnight boat. Once aboard, you'll paddle through caves by kayak and take in the limestone rock formations rising from the water. Spend the night on the boat, waking up to views of the bay at dawn.

days.title: Ha Long Bay to Ninh Binh
days.description: Start your morning learning how to make traditional lanterns in a local workshop. The afternoon is relaxed, spending time at a beach club with the group. In the evening, everyone gathers for a farewell dinner to celebrate the trip and new friendships made.

days.title: Ninh Binh
days.description: Head south to Ninh Binh and check into your local homestay with private riverside bungalows. The landscape here has rice paddies stretching out with limestone mountains in the background. You'll have time to relax and watch the sunset from your riverside spot.

days.title: Hoi An
days.description: Spend the day cycling through Ninh Binh's rice paddies and then take a local row boat along rivers and through caves. Later, climb Dragon Mountain to the viewpoint for panoramic views of the area. By evening you'll board an overnight train heading south to Hoi An.

days.title: Hoi An
days.description: You'll arrive in Hoi An in the morning. The afternoon is yours to explore at your own pace, whether that's shopping, walking the historic streets, or getting custom clothes made at one of the tailor shops. Tonight you'll take out a lantern boat on the river, a signature Hoi An experience.

days.title: Hoi An
days.description: Local fishermen guide you through coconut groves and you'll try crab fishing from traditional basket boats. After that, you're joining a cooking class where you'll learn to make authentic local Vietnamese dishes and get to eat what you've prepared.

days.title: Hoi An - Departure
optional: Extend stay in Vietnam or Southeast Asia
days.description: Your 9-day trip wraps up today. Those heading home will make their way to the airport. If you're extending your stay in Vietnam or elsewhere in Southeast Asia, your group leader and new friends can help you figure out your next steps.

intro:
Taj Mahal & Wildlife with Royal Stay at Castles is the finest introduction perfect for those who want to get drenched in the varied hues of Indian culture and experience the Royalty of kings with a stay at Castle Rohetgarh/Sardar Samand Lake Palace & Sardargarh. This tour covers 9 eminent places positioned in the heartland of the country, i.e. Delhi

This tour is a guaranteed departure, so even if you are the only one booked onto this tour, you will still be guaranteed to depart!

days.title: Delhi to Jaipur
included: Visit Jama Mosque with private guide
Visit Qutub Minar (UNESCO World Heritage Site)
Visit Humayun's Tomb (UNESCO World Heritage Site)
days.description: Your private driver picks you up from your Delhi hotel and meets your tour guide for a full day of sightseeing. You'll visit Jama Mosque, then head to Raj Ghat where Mahatma Gandhi was cremated. After that, you'll see the UNESCO-listed Qutub Minar and Humayun's Tomb before stopping at India Gate. Later in the afternoon, you'll be driven to Jaipur and check into your hotel for the night.

days.title: Jaipur
included: Jeep ride to and from Amber Fort
Visit Amber Fort with private guide
days.description: After breakfast, you'll meet your private guide for a full day exploring Jaipur. The day starts with a jeep ride up to Amber Fort, then you'll visit the City Palace to see its textiles, costumes, and armor displays. From there, you'll explore Hawa Mahal (Palace of Winds) and finish with the stargazing observatory at Jantar Mantar before heading back to your hotel for the evening.

days.title: Jaipur to Jodhpur
days.description: After breakfast, you'll be driven to Jodhpur. Once you arrive and check in at your hotel, you'll have the rest of the day to yourself. This gives you time to walk around, grab lunch, or just relax and get a feel for the city at your own pace.

days.title: Jodhpur to Rohet Garh
included: Visit Mehrangarh Fort with private guide
Cultural activities at Rohet Garh/Chanwa Fort
days.description: After breakfast, your guide will lead you through Jodhpur's main attractions, starting with Mehrangarh Fort and its distinctive latticed windows. You'll then visit Jaswant Thada, the white marble royal cenotaph. Later you'll be driven to either Rohet Garh (Castle of Rohet) or Chanwa Fort in Luni for a royal experience with lavish meals. The evening includes a cattle safari in the village and cultural activities at the fort.

days.title: Rohet Garh to Sardargarh/Deogarh Mahal
days.description: After breakfast, you'll be driven to Sardargarh or Deogarh Mahal, one of Rajasthan's magnificent forts set amidst mountains and forests. You'll stay in royal accommodations with lavish meals included. During the evening, you'll explore the village and participate in cultural activities at the fort.

days.title: Sardargarh to Udaipur
days.description: After breakfast at the fort, you'll be driven to Udaipur. Check in at your hotel and have the rest of the day at leisure. You can relax, take it easy, or explore the city on your own if you feel up for it.

days.title: Udaipur
included: Visit Sahelion-Ki-Bari (Garden of the Maids of Honour)
days.description: Today you'll explore Udaipur starting with Sahelion-Ki-Bari (Garden of the Maids of Honour) and its museums featuring traditional costumes, ornaments, and puppets. You'll visit the City Palace, India's largest palace, with its peacock mosaics and Indian mythology paintings. After checking out a traditional painting school with its famous miniature paintings, you'll end your day with a boat ride on Lake Pichola, passing by the well-known Lake Palace.

days.title: Udaipur to Pushkar
days.description: After breakfast, you'll be driven to Pushkar, a holy pilgrimage site known for its annual cattle fair. Once you check in at your hotel, you'll begin exploring the old temples and ghats of Pushkar on foot and get a sense of the spiritual atmosphere.

days.title: Pushkar to Ranthambore
included: Safari at Ranthambore National Park (1 round)
days.description: After breakfast, you'll be driven to Ranthambore. Once you've checked in and settled, you'll head out for an afternoon safari in an open canter through Ranthambore National Park. You may spot hyenas, cheetahs, jungle cats, and panthers during your ride, and if luck is on your side, Indian tigers.

days.title: Ranthambore to Agra
days.description: After breakfast, you'll be driven to Agra. Check in at your hotel and have the rest of the day to yourself. You can settle in, freshen up, or explore the city at your leisure and get oriented.

days.title: Agra to Delhi
included: Visit Taj Mahal with private guide
days.description: After breakfast, you'll start with a visit to the Taj Mahal where your guide will explain its significance and history. You'll then head to Agra Fort, the massive red sandstone fortress built by Emperor Akbar in 1565 on the Yamuna River. Next, you'll visit Itmad-ud-Daulah, the first entirely marble tomb in India, and finish at Mehtab Bagh, a series of parks on the Yamuna's east bank. Later in the afternoon, you'll be driven to Delhi and dropped at your hotel or airport.

name: Patagonia Hiking

attributes.name: Hiking & Trekking
attributes.tip: Conquer epic trails and breathtaking landscapes

attributes.name: Group Tour
attributes.tip: Join a group and forge lifelong friendships

attributes.tip: An experienced guide will be with you for the entire tour

intro: As a destination for active travellers, Patagonia is nothing short of iconic. The very best way to do this South American region justice is to hike all over it. Trek through the crisp air of El Chaltén (with its crazy beautiful Fitz Roy mountain) and then to the area near the imposing Perito Moreno Glacier. In between, marvel at the giant sky, vast views, and big city appeal of Buenos Aires while you revel in a sense of personal triumph. Patagonia's ready and waiting for you.

days.title: Buenos Aires
optional: Visit La Boca Neighbourhood (10USD per person)
days.description: You'll arrive in Buenos Aires whenever works for you and settle into your hotel. Spend the rest of the day getting to know the city on your own terms. La Boca, Recoleta, and San Telmo are all good neighborhoods to walk through if you want to get oriented, or you could catch a tango show if you're in the mood for that. Later on, there's a welcome meeting with your CEO and the group, so plan to be back for that.

days.title: Buenos Aires to El Chaltén
days.description: Early morning flight from Buenos Aires takes you down to El Calafate, then you'll head out by private vehicle toward El Chaltén in Los Glaciares National Park. During the drive you'll see the towering Andean peaks all around you. Once you arrive in El Chaltén (basically Argentina's trekking capital), you've got free time to wander around town or take a shorter hike to get your legs ready for the bigger hikes coming up.

days.title: El Chaltén
included: Loma del Pliegue Tumbado Guided Hike
days.description: Full day on the trail today with a guide heading to Loma del Pliegue Tumbado viewpoint. This one's different from a lot of the other routes here because instead of dropping down into a valley, you're climbing up to get 360 degree views of the entire El Chaltén region. You'll be on one of the less crowded trails in the national park, which is nice if you want to avoid the worst of the crowds.

days.title: El Chaltén
included: Los Glaciares National Park Guided Hike
days.description: Another full-day guided hike, this time heading to Laguna de los Tres. If the weather cooperates, you'll get incredible views of the Cerro Fitz Roy peaks and the teal-colored lake. The trail starts off relatively easy through tree-covered sections, then opens up into alpine landscape. There's a 400 meter climb to reach the lake, which will be tough, but the views at the top definitely make it worth the effort.

days.title: El Chaltén to El Calafate
optional: Chorrillo del Salto Waterfall hike (30USD per person)
days.description: You get to choose your own hiking adventure today. The Laguna Torre trail gets you close to the dramatic Cerro Torre formation, or you could go to Chorrillo del Salto Waterfall instead. Condor Mirador is another option if you want something with good town views. Later, you'll transfer back to El Calafate and have a substantial dinner to recover from all the hiking.

days.title: El Calafate
optional: Perito Moreno Glacier Boat (80USD per person)
days.description: Head out to Perito Moreno Glacier for your included guided tour. The metallic walkways get you right up close to the glacier for some great views. If you want a different perspective, you can add on a boat ride across Argentino Lake, which lets you see just how massive the glacier really is from out on the water.

days.title: El Calafate
optional: Navigation to see other glaciers (Upsala Glacier and Onelli Bay)
days.description: You have the day to yourself in El Calafate. Laguna Nimez has a nice short walk if you want to get out (it's 15 dollars per person). Otherwise, you can browse the souvenir shops and restaurants in town, or if you're looking for something more active, there are options like a full-day ranch experience or horseback riding out in the Patagonian steppe.

days.title: El Calafate to Buenos Aires
optional: Drinks at sidewalk cafes and restaurants
days.description: Fly back to Buenos Aires and spend the evening soaking in the tango culture of the city. Hit some sidewalk cafes for drinks, or book a tango show if that interests you. Get the group together for one final meal and open up a last bottle of Argentine wine. It's your final chance to try the famous bife and parrilladas before everyone heads different directions.

days.title: Buenos Aires
days.description: Whenever you're ready, head out of Buenos Aires. Safe travels.

qa.question: For the Patagonia Hiking Tour, would you please give me a general idea of the distance and elevation gain of each day's hike.
qa.answer: Daily Hiking Overview Day 2 Base Torres - 22 km roundtrip - 7–9 hrs - 750 m Day 3 Central → Serón - 19 km. - 5–7 hrs - 400 m Day 4 Serón → Dickson - 18 km - 6–7 hrs - 720 m Day 5 Dickson → Perros - 13 km - 5–6 hrs - 600 m Day 6 Perros → Grey - 18 km - 8–10 hrs - 1000 m Day 8 Grey → Paine Grande - 11 km - Approx. 5 hrs - 400 m Day 9 Paine Grande → Valle Francés → Cuernos - 17 km - 8–9 hrs - 500 m Hiking times can vary depending on weather conditions, trail conditions, and overall group pace. Weather in Patagonia is extremely unpredictable and can change very quickly from sunshine to rain and strong winds. Waterproof gear and layered clothing are highly recommended. There is no option to skip most trekking days on the O Circuit once inside the park, so travellers should be prepared for consecutive hiking days regardless of weather conditions. All refugios/lodges have electricity and...

qa.question: I'm planning to travel with my 27 years old son (I'm 57 years old with good health and reasonable physical condition), please advise what and how can we be prepared for this trip, especially for hiking. Travel Support
qa.answer: Our Patagonia itineraries are designed for active travellers, but you certainly don't need to be an athlete to enjoy the experience. Many of our guests are in their 50s and 60s and successfully complete the trip with good preparation and a positive mindset. In terms of hiking, you can expect several day hikes that range from moderate to challenging. These typically involve walking on uneven terrain, gravel paths, and occasional steep sections, with hikes lasting anywhere from 3 to 8 hours depending on the day and the route chosen. While some hikes are optional, the most iconic experiences—such as those in Torres del Paine or El Chaltén—are best enjoyed if you're comfortable with longer walking days. To prepare, we recommend: Building up your cardiovascular fitness with regular walking, hiking, cycling, or swimming. Practising longer walks on uneven or hilly terrain where possible....

name: Torres del Paine - The W Trek

attributes.name: Hiking & Trekking
attributes.tip: Conquer epic trails and breathtaking landscapes

attributes.name: Group Tour
attributes.tip: Join a group and forge lifelong friendships

attributes.tip: An experienced guide will be with you for the entire tour

intro: Here's a quick six-day trip that's simply perfect as an add-on to other Patagonian adventures. Torres del Paine's W Trek is celebrated by active travellers globally as one of the most scenic treks anywhere. Spend four days walking through stunning landscapes surrounding Grey Glacier, French Valley, and the imposing three towers. While the trek alone is challenging enough, the real contest comes in needing to take your camera out so frequently.

days.title: Puerto Natales
optional: Equipment rental for Torres del Paine trek
days.description: You'll arrive in Puerto Natales, which serves as your entry point to Torres del Paine National Park. Spend the day getting oriented around town, finding a good restaurant for lunch or dinner, and resting up before the trek begins. If you need any equipment rentals or last-minute supplies, this is the time to handle that. Your welcome meeting with the trip leader and the rest of the group starts between 5 and 6pm, so plan to be back at your accommodation by then.

days.title: Puerto Natales to Laguna Azul Camp
days.description: Your W Trek adventure kicks off in Torres del Paine National Park. You'll head out by private vehicle to reach the trailhead, then begin the 62km hike that makes up this route. The day takes you toward Las Torres, where you get your first real look at those three dramatic towers rising up above the turquoise lagoon below. After hiking, you'll set up camp at Laguna Azul Camp for the night.

days.title: Laguna Azul Camp to Cuernos Camp
included: W Trek - Day 2 Welcome Center to Cuernos Camp
days.description: After breakfast at camp, you'll board a van and drive along the Paine River toward the Welcome Center inside Torres del Paine National Park. Keep watching for wildlife along the route. Once at the center, you'll meet your porters and continue hiking the W route toward Cuernos Campsite. There's a stop at Nordenskjöld Lake where you can take in the views before you reach camp for the night.

days.title: Cuernos Camp to Paine Grande Camp
days.description: Today's hike leads you to the French Valley lookout, where you get views of the French Glacier hanging over Paine Grande mountain. From this vantage point, you'll see 360-degree views across the landscape with its dramatic mix of greens and greys. After you've soaked in the scenery, the trail continues through a forest of dead trees before reaching Paine Grande Campsite, where you'll stay the night.

days.title: Paine Grande Camp to Puerto Natales
included: W Trek - Day 4 Paine Grande Camp to Grey Lookout
days.description: The final day of the W Trek takes you to Grey Lake and the lookout point for Grey Glacier, where you can see the massive scale of the glacier itself. From there, you'll hike back toward Lake Pehoé and finish your four days of trekking with a scenic ferry ride across the water. It's a rewarding way to end the trek. After the ferry, you'll return to Puerto Natales for the night.

days.title: Puerto Natales
days.description: You're free to leave at any time this morning. Have breakfast before you head out. If you're connecting to flights through Punta Arenas or El Calafate, note that the transfer takes 3 to 4 hours, so booking an afternoon flight gives you enough time to get there without rushing.

name: Bali Experience

attributes.name: City & Culture
attributes.tip: Immerse yourself in rich history and local traditions

attributes.name: Group Tour
attributes.tip: Join a group and forge lifelong friendships

attributes.name: Fully Guided
attributes.tip: An experienced guide will be with you for the entire tour

intro: Join us on an epic adventure as we visit 3 awesome destinations across Bali and the Gili Islands. See amazing sights, explore majestic temples, splash around in waterfalls, visit an active volcano, wander through rice fields, discover idyllic islands and sip cocktails on white sandy beaches. Shop the markets, indulge in delicious food, learn to surf, snorkel in the crystal clear sea & lose yourself in the wild night life Bali has to offer!

days.title: Arrival in Bali
days.start_point: Jl. Pantai Berawa Gang Sri Kahyangan No. 88, Berawa,, Canggu, North Kuta, Badung Regency, Bali 80361, Indonesia (Koa D'Surfer Hotel, 19:00)
days.description: You'll land at Denpasar airport and get transferred to your hotel in Canggu. After settling in, the day is yours to relax by the pool or head to the beach if you feel like it. Later this evening, join the group for a rooftop dinner and drinks where you'll meet everyone on the tour.

days.title: Bali
days.description: You'll start by heading to Tanah Lot, where the temple sits out on a dramatic rocky outcrop in the ocean. It's one of Bali's most iconic spots, and you'll see why when you get there. From there, you'll make your way to Taman Ayun, the Royal Temple, to experience more of the island's spiritual side. Later in the afternoon, head over to one of Canggu's beaches to catch the sunset. After the sun goes down, you'll grab dinner and explore the nightlife in town.

days.title: Bali
days.description: This morning you'll head to Kuta Beach for a surf lesson with local instructors who know how to get beginners up on a board quickly. After spending time in the water, you'll head back to Canggu to either kick back or wander around the area for a bit. Later you'll settle in at a spot where you can watch the sunset with a cocktail while you swap stories about your time on the waves.

days.title: Canggu to Ubud
days.description: You're traveling inland to Ubud, and along the way you'll stop at Tegenungan waterfall to cool off and take a break. Once you arrive in Ubud, there's time to walk around town and check out the open-air market where you'll find locals shopping for fresh produce and handmade crafts. The rice paddies and temples scattered around the area give the town its distinctive character, and there are monkeys hanging around too.

days.title: Ubud
days.meals: Breakfast, Lunch (Balinese feast prepared during cooking class)
days.description: Start early and head to the local markets outside central Ubud to hunt for the freshest ingredients you can find. Then you'll join a cooking class with a Balinese family where you'll prepare a meal together and learn how things are done. After lunch, you'll visit the sacred monkey forest and spend time with the playful monkeys that live there. Later you'll return for dinner with the rest of your group.

days.title: Ubud
days.description: You'll trek through the rice terraces around Ubud, and there's fresh coconut water to sip while you walk and learn about how these agricultural areas work. Around lunch time, head to Kintamani where you'll eat with views of the active Mt. Batur volcano in the distance. After that, you can either relax by the pool back at your accommodation or spend the afternoon exploring the local markets at your own pace.

days.title: Ubud to Gili Trawangan
days.description: Today you're traveling to Gili Trawangan island by minibus and ferry, and once you arrive you'll check into your tropical accommodation right in the center of the island. The afternoon is yours to either relax by the pool with a beer or wander out to one of the beaches surrounding the island. Later you'll catch the sunset on the beach, then head out for dinner and explore the beachside bars where the nightlife happens.

days.title: Gili Trawangan - Island Hopping
days.description: You'll spend the day on a snorkeling adventure around Gili Trawangan and Gili Meno, checking out some of Indonesia's best underwater areas. There's plenty of jumping off the boat, discovering underwater statues, and seeing the marine life around you. By evening you'll head back to Gili Trawangan and watch the sunset from the beach with a beer in hand.

days.title: Gili Trawangan Bike Tour
included: Island bike tour of Gili Trawangan
days.description: Rent a bike and cycle around Gili Trawangan to see different beaches and activities across the island. Trek up to the island's main viewpoint hill and check out the remains of a WWII bunker. Catch one final sunset before gathering for a farewell dinner and celebration party with the group.

days.title: Departure
days.description: Check out of your accommodation and get help arranging your next steps, whether that's heading to another island or getting to the airport. Your group leader can sort out all the details and help make sure you get where you need to go.

name: 8 Days Northern Lights Exploration

attributes.tip: Chase the aurora across glittering night skies

intro:
• Also available as a Small Group departure with maximum 16 passengers. https://www.tourradar.com/t/238379

Experience the best of Iceland’s winter! Our Northern Lights Exploration series are designed to include the highlights of Iceland and aim to maximize the chances of seeing the elusive Northern Lights. In addition to a seven night stay with breakfast, this program includes our special six night Northern Lights Academy, a combination of evening presentations, lectures, film and guided lookouts for the Aurora Borealis – the Northern Lights. Experience Icelandic winter as good as it gets. Head to the countryside: from the regions of Snæfellsnes Peninsula in the west to the Vatnajökull glacier in the southeast. Profit to search for the Aurora Borealis away from the big city lights.

days.title: Arrival in Reykjavik
days.start_point: Keflavik International Airport / Keflavíkurflugvöllur (KEF), Keflavíkurflugvelli, Sandgerði, Southern Peninsula 235, Iceland (Flybus PLUS shuttle transfer from Keflavík International Airport to your accomodation in Reykjavík. The Flybus departs from Keflavík Airport 35-40 minutes after each flight arrival. )
days.description: You'll land at Keflavik Airport and catch the Flybus shuttle to your hotel in Reykjavik. If time allows after checking in, the rest of the afternoon and evening are yours to walk around the city and get a feel for Iceland's capital.

days.title: Borgarfjordur - Borgarnes
included: Northern Lights search with midnight refreshment
days.description: Your guide meets you at 09:00 for a city tour of Reykjavik, then you'll head west to Borgarnes to see the Settlement Center and learn about Iceland's earliest settlers. From there, you'll go into Saga Valley to climb Grábróк volcano crater, check out Deildartunguhver hot spring, and see Hraunfossar and Barnafoss waterfalls. After dinner, there's a Northern Lights Academy talk followed by a search from the hotel garden with hot chocolate or tea.

days.title: Snæfellsnes Peninsula
included: Guided tour into Vatnshellir cave (35 metres underground, approximately 200 metres into lava tube)
Explore Arnarstapi coastal cliffs and rock formations
Northern Lights Academy program - photography tips and guided Northern Lights search
Access to hotel outdoor hot tubs
days.description: Start your day on the Snaefellsnes Peninsula where you'll see rugged mountains and the distinctive shape of Kirkjufell rising up from the landscape. You'll drive through the fishing village of Grundarfjordur and then head underground to explore Vatnshellir lava cave, descending about 35 metres beneath the Snaefellsjokull glacier. After coming back up, you'll make your way to Arnarstapi to walk along the dramatic coastal cliffs. Later in the evening, your guide shares tips on photographing the Northern Lights before you head outside to the hotel's hot tubs to watch for them in the night sky, 45°F/7°C.

days.title: Golden Circle - Geothermal Areas - South Iceland
included: Visit Þingvellir National Park (UNESCO World Heritage site)
Hot spring tasting with geothermally cooked bread, eggs and herring
Learn about Icelandic horses at stables
days.meals: Lunch (Hot spring tasting with geothermally cooked bread, Icelandic butter, boiled eggs and herring)
days.description: You'll start by driving along Hvalfjarðar fjord toward Þingvellir National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage site where you can walk between the tectonic plates. From there, continue on the Golden Circle route to reach the Geysir geothermal fields and watch the steam rise from the hot springs. Stop for a traditional Icelandic meal of freshly baked hot spring bread with butter, boiled eggs, and herring. Next you'll head to Gullfoss to see the powerful double waterfall, then visit local stables to learn about Icelandic horses and their unique characteristics. After that, check out a geothermal greenhouse where they grow plants using the natural heat. By evening, head into the rural countryside for Northern Lights hunting, so bundle up and bring patience as you wait for the aurora to appear.

days.title: South Coast Exploration
included: Folk museum visit with turf-built houses
days.description: Along the South coast, you'll stop at the Lava and Volcano Exhibition Center to understand Iceland's geology and active volcanoes. Next comes one of Iceland's best folk museums with farm artifacts and several turf-built houses, then Skógafoss waterfall at 60 meters high. In the afternoon, you'll walk the black lava beach and bird cliffs at Reynisfjara. You're positioned well tonight for Northern Lights searching in this remote area.

days.title: Skaftafell National Park & Vatnajökull Glacier
included: Explore Jökulsárlón glacial lagoon and floating icebergs
Walk on Diamond Beach with stranded icebergs
Northern Lights Academy program - film presentation and guided Northern Lights search
optional: Ice Cave Tour in Vatnajökull National Park (October-April, weather permitting) - approximately 2.5 hours duration with 30-minute 4x4 transfer and 5-15 minute walk to cave entrance, exploring naturally formed ice structures and blue ice (ISK 25,000 per person, minimum age 10 years, warm waterproof clothing and sturdy hiking boots essential, note: participants miss visits to Skaftafell National Park and Hofs church)
days.description: You'll spend the day in Iceland's most dramatic glacial area, starting at Jokulsarlon glacial lagoon where icebergs float across the water. From there, head to Diamond Beach to see icebergs that have washed ashore and turned the black sand into a glittering landscape. Stop at Hof, a small turf church that sits quietly in this remote region. Then you'll explore Skaftafell National Park, walking among Iceland's highest mountains while being surrounded by Europe's largest glacier. By evening, watch a film about the Northern Lights, and then step outside to look for them across the night sky, 32°F/0°C.

days.title: South Coast Return and Blue Lagoon
optional: Blue Lagoon additional services or packages
days.description: Leaving Kirkjubaejarklaustur, you'll cross the Eldhraun lava field with a photo stop in Vik to see the black lava beach and high bird cliffs. Continuing west, you'll check out Seljalandsfoss waterfall dropping from the mountain. In the afternoon, you'll soak in the famous Blue Lagoon before heading back to Reykjavik around dinner time for your last night.

days.title: Departure from Reykjavik
days.description: The Flybus shuttle picks you up from your Reykjavik accommodation and takes you to Keflavik Airport for your departure.

intro: During the day we explore Southwest Iceland, known for its natural wonders and cultural sights. See glittering glaciers, snow-clad mountains, giant lava fields, steaming hot springs and beautiful waterfalls. Bathe in the mineral rich geothermal waters of the Blue Lagoon, walk on a black lava beach, visit Icelandic horses on their farm, photography idyllic turf houses and travel close to the famous Eyjafjallajökull volcano. This short getaway to Iceland offers insight into Iceland's nature and cultural life, with two nights in Iceland's capital and two nights in South Iceland, an ideal location for the search for the Northern Lights. Also called Aurora Borealis, they are visible in the northern sky from September through April when the sky is clear and free of clouds. During this tour it is possible to book an optional glacier hike.

days.description: Meet your guide at 09:00 for a highlights tour through Reykjavik's main attractions. From there, you'll head to the Reykjanes Peninsula to see hot springs, mountains, bird cliffs, lighthouses, and small fishing villages. By afternoon you'll soak in the Blue Lagoon's warm mineral waters. Later in the evening, your guide talks about Northern Lights activity, and you'll get a chance to search for them in the garden once it gets dark.

days.title: South Iceland
included: Explore Skógar folk museum and turf-built houses
Walk on black lava beach at Reynisfjara
View bird cliffs at Reynisfjara near Vík
Northern Lights presentation and guided search
days.description: Start your drive along Iceland's south coast early, heading toward Seljalandsfoss waterfall where you can walk right up close to the cascade. From there, it's a short trip to Skógar to check out the folk museum with its turf-built houses that really show what traditional Icelandic homes looked like. After exploring the museum, walk over to Skógafoss, which is a powerful waterfall nearby. Later in the afternoon, make your way to Reynisfjara and spend time on the black lava beach near Vík, where you can look up at the bird cliffs and watch the wildlife. Back at your hotel in the evening, there's a Northern Lights presentation happening, and after that, you'll head outside from the hotel grounds to search for the lights if the conditions are right and the sky cooperates.

days.title: Reykjavik

name: Explore Golden Triangle

attributes.name: City & Culture
attributes.tip: Immerse yourself in rich history and local traditions

attributes.name: Group Tour
attributes.tip: Join a group and forge lifelong friendships

attributes.name: Partially Guided
attributes.tip: Independent travel, featuring selected guided excursions

intro:
India's Golden Triangle Tour is one of the most popular and cherished travel routes for anyone visiting the country. This famous circuit connects three iconic cities: Delhi, Agra, and Jaipur, offering a perfect blend of history, culture, architecture, and adventure.


Guaranteed to depart! This tour is guaranteed to depart, so even if you're the only passenger confirmed, your tour will still go ahead as planned!

days.title: Delhi
days.start_point: Indira Gandhi International Airport (DEL), Airport Rd, New Delhi, Delhi 110037, India (Main Entrance)
days.description: You'll land at Delhi International Airport where a representative meets you and handles your transfer to the hotel. Delhi has this incredible mix of history and culture layered throughout the city, so you're starting in the right place to get a real sense of India's energy and character.

days.title: Delhi
included: Heritage Walking Tour of Old Delhi
Cycle rickshaw ride through Chandni Chowk Bazaar
Visit to Khari Bawli spice market
Local Family Home visit with cooking class and dinner
days.meals: Breakfast (Breakfast at hotel), Dinner (Indian Homemade Dinner with Local Family)
days.description: After breakfast at your hotel, you'll head into Old Delhi for a guided walking tour that includes cycle rickshaw rides through the ancient bazaars and spice markets. The day takes you past Jama Mosque, through the historic Chandni Chowk, and to Raj Ghat. In the afternoon you'll check out New Delhi's iconic spots like India Gate, and then the evening wraps up at a local family home where you'll cook and eat dinner with your hosts, which gives you a much more personal angle on how people actually live here.

days.title: Delhi to Agra
days.description: You'll drive to Agra after breakfast, about 220 kilometers and 4 hours on the express highway. Once you check in at your hotel, the afternoon is for visiting Agra Fort. After that you'll have time to head to Mehtab Bagh, the moonlit garden across the river, which has really nice views of the Taj Mahal from that side.

days.title: Agra - Fatehpur Sikri - Abhaneri - Jaipur
included: Visit to 9th Century Step Well Abhaneri
Traditional Rajasthani meal at heritage hotel
days.meals: Breakfast, Dinner (Traditional Rajasthani Dinner at Dhulagarh Village)
days.description: This is an early start for the sunrise tour of Taj Mahal, then back to your hotel for breakfast. From there you're driving to Jaipur, about 280 kilometers over 5 to 6 hours. On the way you'll stop at Fatehpur Sikri, the abandoned city, and the 9th century Abhaneri stepwell. Before you reach Jaipur you'll visit a rural village near sand dunes for something different, followed by traditional Rajasthani food at a heritage hotel that's connected to the royal family.

days.title: Jaipur
included: Visit to Panna Meena Ka Kund
days.description: After breakfast you're exploring Jaipur's forts and palaces, starting with the 16th-century Panna Meena Ka Kund stepwell. Then it's 11 kilometers out to Amer Fort, which has marble palaces and the Sheesh Mahal with all its mirror work. You'll stop at Jal Mahal for photos, visit the City Palace and its museum with royal collections, see the Jantar Mantar astronomical observatory, and drive past the Hawa Mahal. The day finishes with photos at Patrika Gate and then free time to wander around the Pink City on your own.

days.title: Jaipur to Delhi

intro:
North West Highlands, Skye, Eilean Donan Castle & Glenfinnan Viaduct

We don’t call this our Scottish Choice for nothing! Enjoy the full sweep of Scotland’s beauty with one night in Oban, two  nights on the Isle of Skye and a final night in Inverness, capital of the Highlands. You’ll get to know Scottish history and culture and have time to experience the places you visit. 

Meeting Point:

1 Parliament Sq, Royal Mile, EH1 1RE, inside Caffe Nero, besides St Giles Cathedral

Pick Up Time: 8.30am

Drop Off Time: 19.00

Highlights include

1. Loch Lomond, Kilmartin Glen & Oban

2. Glen Coe, Loch Ness Cruise & Urquhart Castle*

3. Eilean Donan Castle*

4. Kilt Rock, The Mealt Falls & Old Man of Storr

5. Culloden Battlefield* 

*Optional extra subject to availability

days.title: Glasgow to Oban
included: Stop and explore Luss village on the shores of Loch Lomond
Stop at Rest and Be Thankful viewpoint
days.start_point: 192 High Street, Edinburgh, EH1 1RW, United Kingdom (Highland Experience Tours, Caffe Nero, High Street, Edinburgh, 08:00 - 08:15)
days.description: You'll head west into Loch Lomond and Trossachs National Park, stopping in the village of Luss to walk around and get a feel for the area. From there, continue through Argyll and take a viewpoint stop at Rest and Be Thankful for views across the landscape. Inveraray Castle comes next, then you'll drive to Kilmartin Glen where there's a collection of ancient sites including Dunadd Hill Fort and Temple Wood Stone Circle to explore. By evening, you'll arrive in the seaside town of Oban and settle in for your first night.

days.title: Oban to Isle of Skye
included: Ferry crossing to Isle of Skye
days.description: Cross over the Connel Bridge through Appin into Glen Coe, where the dramatic mountain scenery is hard to miss, and you'll learn about the MacDonald Clan massacre that happened there. Stop in Fort William during lunch to grab something to eat. After that, head west to see the Glenfinnan Viaduct (you might recognize it from Harry Potter films) and check out the Glenfinnan Monument nearby. You'll spend some time in Mallaig before boarding a ferry that takes you across to the Isle of Skye for your overnight stay.

days.title: Isle of Skye
included: See The Old Man of Storr
days.meals: Breakfast (Continental breakfast, full Scottish Breakfast, or combination of both at your accommodation)
days.description: Your day on the Isle of Skye starts early with your driver-guide picking you up for a full day exploring the island's dramatic landscapes. You'll head to the Cuillin Mountains first, where the scenery shifts between rugged peaks and hidden valleys. From there, you move on to Kilt Rock, where a waterfall drops straight down the cliff face into the sea. The Old Man of Storr comes next, and you'll spend time at this iconic rock formation that juts out from the hillside. Later in the afternoon, you'll drive through the Trotternish Peninsula, taking in more of the island's unusual rock formations and viewpoints. You'll also stop in Portree, the island's main town, where you can grab lunch and walk around the colorful harbor. Throughout the day, your guide will take you to local spots that don't show up in most guidebooks, places where locals actually spend their time. The whole experience gives you a real sense of what makes Skye so different from anywhere else in Scotland.

days.title: Isle of Skye to Inverness
days.description: Leave Skye by crossing the Skye Bridge and head toward Eilean Donan Castle, which sits on its own island in Loch Duich with the Five Sisters of Kintail mountains rising behind it. It's one of the most photographed castles in Scotland. After visiting, continue toward the Great Glen and Loch Ness, where you can explore Urquhart Castle's ruins and optionally take a boat cruise on the loch if you're interested. You'll finish the day in Inverness, settling in for your final night.

days.title: Inverness to Edinburgh
days.description: Start your morning at the Culloden Battlefield learning about the final Jacobite defeat, then move on to Clava Cairns, a prehistoric burial site that inspired the Outlander series. If you'd like, there's an optional stop at a local distillery for a dram. Later, you'll pass through the Cairngorms National Park on your way through the landscape, with a stop in the town of Pitlochry before returning to Edinburgh.

reviews.reply:
Dear A’ra,

We are very sorry to read your negative feedback regarding your 5-Day Scottish Choice Tour and regret that your experience did not meet expectations. However, we must clarify several points in your review.

As explained in detail in the email correspondence sent to you, your tour departure did operate as scheduled, with all key elements of the itinerary covered to the best extent possible under the day’s conditions. The driver will always attempt to make a stop at the Glenfinnan monument itself, but unfortunately on this day the carpark was full, and the staff on site were not accepting any buses. We do reserve the right to alter our itineraries, and we are glad you were still able to experience the beautiful surrounding scenery and drive much of the route of the Jacobite Steam Train.

We are shocked to read your feedback regarding your expert driver guide. All our guides, including new members of the team, undergo extensive training and route familiarization before leading any multi-day tour. While Craig was newer to leading extended tours, he is a fully licensed and qualified guide who met all required standards before departure. Only a small handful of drivers are highlighted at any given time on our website and we have a large team of professional guides and drivers. Our quality records and passenger feedback from other customers do not reflect your comments. While regional accents can occasionally present challenges for some visitors, this does not reflect a lack of knowledge or effort on the guide’s part. We encourage passengers to voice such concerns during the tour so that accommodations can be made in real time. We can understand that a joke poking fun about not knowing some of the locations was not appreciated out of context and this feedback has been passed to our transport management.

Regarding the vehicle, it was fully inspected before departure and cleared for service. Our fleet is maintained to high standards, and we would not knowingly send out a vehicle that is not fully fit for purpose. Our vehicles are checked every morning and evening to ensure that everything is functioning properly, but unfortunately issues can occur whilst on tour. A minor noise was reported and monitored throughout the trip and did not pose a safety risk. We sincerely apologise for any inconvenience caused regarding the noise on the bus and we have taken your feedback on board.

We welcome all feedback that helps us improve, but we must also defend our guides and company and we are confident that your driver guide went above and beyond to try to give you a wonderful experience on tour. We remain committed to providing authentic, high-quality Highland experiences to every passenger but we regret that we were unable to match your expectations this time.

Kind regards,
Sofia
Shop Manager
Highland Experience

qa.question: Is this a bus trip? We are not familiar with this type of tour, can you provide any additional information about the transportation and lodging?
qa.answer: Yes, this is a bus trip that will take you throughout the Highlands. It will be operated on either a 16-seater van or a 35-seater bus. You will have stops every 1.5 hour or so, and most of your stops will be between 30 minutes and 1.5 hours, with some shorter photo stops. Travel on our spectacular Classic Tour with the option to enjoy the comfort of upgraded hotels throughout. This tour includes amazing sightseeing stops in the Okanagan Valley and the Rocky Mountains including gorgeous Canadian turquoise lakes and awesome mountain peaks! 

­ 

This tour requires a min. of 22 passengers to operate.

­ 

Please note: This itinerary is sometimes in reverse order (Valemount – Banff – Revelstoke) but the hotels, sightseeing highlights and inclusions are the same. It is also subject to change due to unforeseen circumstances. Departure times may vary by date, please see your confirmation email for exact departure times.


To ensure a smooth and enjoyable experience, we kindly recommend booking your flights for the day before our tour begins and the day after it concludes. This precaution helps avoid complications arising from potential flight delays or tour schedule changes, such as traffic, which could affect your travel plans.


Please note that in accordance with our policies, we are unable to offer refunds if you miss the tour due to delayed flights. Similarly, if unforeseen circumstances cause a delay in returning to Vancouver, you may miss your flight home. Booking your flights with this buffer will help ensure a worry-free journey.

days.description: You're heading out from Vancouver early this morning, driving through the Fraser Valley and Okanagan Valley with some really nice scenery along the way. Once you reach Kelowna, there's time to grab lunch and walk around the waterfront area before the drive continues to Revelstoke. After checking in at your hotel, you can spend the rest of the evening getting familiar with the mountain town and seeing what's around.

days.title: Revelstoke to Banff
optional: Banff Gondola ride this evening (at additional cost)
days.description: After breakfast in Revelstoke, you'll head toward the Rocky Mountains and stop at Rogers Pass Summit for photos and stretching your legs. The route takes you to Lake Louise, and in the afternoon you can walk around Moraine Lake and take pictures. There's an optional Banff Gondola ride available this evening if you want mountain views, or you can skip it. By evening you'll be in Banff with free time to find dinner and do some shopping.

days.description: Today follows the Icefields Parkway with several stops at lakes in the Columbia Icefields area along the route. If you're interested, there's an optional Ice Explorer Glacier Tour available for an extra fee that takes you onto the glacier itself. From there you'll continue to Jasper where dinner is on your own, and then you'll head to Valemount for the night.

days.description: You'll head out from downtown Vancouver early and drive through the Fraser Valley. After settling in, there's free time to explore nearby trails or head down to the wharf. Everyone gathers for a group dinner this evening.

days.title: Salmon Arm to Banff
included: Travel through Rogers Pass in Glacier National Park
days.description: Start with breakfast at the hotel before heading into the Rocky Mountains. You'll stop in Revelstoke for a coffee break and grab lunch supplies, then drive through Rogers Pass in Glacier National Park. From there it's on to Moraine Lake where you can rent a canoe if you want (depends on the season). Next you'll explore Lake Louise and drive into Banff. The evening is yours to find dinner somewhere in town.

days.title: Banff
included: Scenic tour around Lake Minnewanka and Two Jack Lake Loop
Tour of Banff townsite including Bow Falls, HooDoos, and Banff Springs Hotel
days.description: Take a gondola up to the top of Sulphur Mountain to see the Rocky Mountain views spread out below. After that you'll do a scenic drive around Lake Minnewanka and the Two Jack Lake Loop. Spend time in Banff townsite checking out Bow Falls, the HooDoos, and Banff Springs Hotel. The afternoon opens up for shopping on Banff Avenue or you can do optional outdoor activities at reduced rates. Evening is free to relax as you like.

days.title: Banff to Blue River
included: Visit alpine lake in Columbia Icefields area
days.description: Following breakfast, you'll travel the Icefields Parkway heading toward Jasper National Park. Tour through Columbia Icefields and stop at another alpine lake. There's an option to take the Ice Explorer Glacier Tour if you want (costs extra). You'll reach the mountain town of Jasper for dinner, then continue on to the Mike Wiegele cabins in Blue River to settle in for the night.

days.title: Blue River to Vancouver
included: Visit Spahats Falls in Wells Gray Provincial Park
days.description: Start the morning with breakfast before heading from Blue River back toward Vancouver. The route takes you through Clearwater where you'll stop at Spahats Falls in Wells Gray Provincial Park to catch one last look at the natural scenery. After that, grab lunch in Kamloops and continue your drive south. You should roll into Vancouver by around 7:30pm, wrapping up the trip.
