intro: Welkom in Suid-Afrika!Wamkelekile eMzantsi Afrika! Welcome to South Africa! Designed by South Africans, this jam-packed tour is the ultimate introduction to this colourful country affectionately called the Rainbow Nation. Explore the breathtaking coastlines of the Atlantic and Indian Oceans, travel to Cape Point, the southwestern tip of Africa, and discover the charming towns that tell the story of South Africa's rich history on the way. Wander at the world-renowned Garden Route, explore the breathtaking Route 62 and discover the semi-desert Great Karoo. Traverse the Kruger National Park Region up north for unforgettable wildlife sightings and marvel at the Panorama Route in Mpumalanga before ending in Johannesburg, the City of Gold!

days.title: Cape Town
included: Driving and walking tour of Cape Town
Buffet braai (BBQ) with African drumming performance at a local winery
days.meals: Dinner (Buffet braai (BBQ) at a local winery with African drumming performance)
days.start_point: 54 Breë Street, Cape Town, Western Cape 8001, South Africa (StayEasy City Bowl Cape Town, 14:00)
days.description: After meeting your tour leader at the hotel, you'll head out for a driving and walking tour of Cape Town. The route takes in Signal Hill, District Six, and the Company's Garden. By evening, there's a buffet braai dinner at a local winery with African drumming, so you'll get a real sense of the local food and music scene right from the start.

days.title: Cape Town
optional: Cape Peninsula Day Trip including penguin viewing at Boulders Beach, lunch in Kalk Bay, and V&A Waterfront
days.description: This is your free day to move around Cape Town however you like. You can check out Robben Island, Table Mountain, Kirstenbosch National Botanical Garden, or the Two Oceans Aquarium at whatever pace suits you. If you want a structured option, there's an optional Cape Peninsula Day Trip where you'll see penguins at Boulders Beach, grab lunch in Kalk Bay, and swing by the V&A Waterfront.

days.title: Cape Town - Stellenbosch - Hermanus
included: Wine tasting in Cape Winelands at a local vineyard with lunch
days.meals: Breakfast, Lunch (Lunch at a local vineyard with wine tasting featuring Pinotage varietal)
days.description: You'll head out to the Cape Winelands and start in Stellenbosch to walk around and see the Cape Dutch architecture, galleries, and boutiques. Lunch happens at a local vineyard with a wine tasting focused on South Africa's Pinotage. After that, you continue to Hermanus where you'll have time to explore this coastal town and take in the ocean views.

days.title: Hermanus - Swellendam - Mossel Bay
optional: Marine Eco Big 5 Trip to spot whales, sharks, seals, penguins and dolphins
Spirit of Hermanus craft beer and seafood pairing at a waterfront eatery
days.description: The morning in Hermanus is free, or you can join optional activities like spotting marine wildlife or doing a craft beer and seafood pairing. Then you'll travel to Swellendam, a charming Cape Dutch town, and on to Mossel Bay, a quiet harbour spot. An included hotel dinner wraps up the day.

days.title: Mossel Bay - Botlierskop - Knysna - Tsitsikamma
included: Garden Route Game Drive at Botlierskop Private Game Reserve
optional: Birds of Eden aviary and bird sanctuary visit
days.description: You'll spend time on a game drive at Botlierskop Private Game Reserve where you can see impala, wildebeest, rhinos, lions, and giraffes. From there, you head to Knysna with time to shop and eat lunch at the waterfront. You'll choose either Monkeyland or Birds of Eden aviary in the afternoon, then come back for an included dinner.

days.title: Tsitsikamma National Park - Storms River
included: Explore Storms River Mouth in Tsitsikamma National Park
days.description: The Tsitsikamma forest is next, with its rivers, ravines, and woodlands. In the morning you can pick optional activities like a tree-top canopy tour, kayak adventure, or just take a scenic drive. Later you'll hike to Storms River Mouth, cross the 77-metre suspension bridge, and have lunch with ocean views.

days.title: Tsitsikamma - Route 62 - Oudtshoorn - Cango Caves
included: Visit Klein Karoo ostrich farm with guided tour
Explore Cango Caves with guided walk
days.meals: Breakfast, Lunch (Three-course lunch at ostrich farm), Dinner (Traditional buffet dinner)
days.description: You'll travel along scenic Route 62 through Langkloof Valley to Oudtshoorn, the ostrich capital. A guided tour of a working ostrich farm comes first, followed by a three-course lunch. Then it's into the Cango Caves where a guide takes you through dripstone formations and caverns. A traditional buffet dinner ends the day.

days.title: Oudtshoorn - Route 62 - Robertson - Paarl - Cape Town
included: Visit winery in Robertson with lunch
Cheese and wine tasting in Paarl
days.description: The drive back to Cape Town follows scenic Route 62 with stops along the way. You'll visit Robertson, a winemaking area with an included lunch, then continue to Paarl in the Cape Winelands for cheese and wine tasting. Back at your Cape Town hotel, the evening is free to check out restaurants, bars, or head to Camps Bay.

days.title: Cape Town - Johannesburg - Kruger National Park Region
included: Included internal flight from Cape Town to Johannesburg
days.description: You'll start early and head to Cape Town airport for an included flight to Johannesburg. From there you travel to Mpumalanga in eastern South Africa and arrive at accommodation near Kruger National Park. Dinner with the group is included.

days.title: Kruger National Park Region
included: Full-day Kruger National Park game drive
Visit rest camps including Skukuza, Tshokwane and Satara
days.description: A full day on a game drive through Kruger National Park means you'll have good chances of seeing wildlife including the Big 5 like cheetahs, wild dogs, leopards, elephants, and rhinos. You'll visit rest camps like Skukuza, Tshokwane, and Satara throughout the day. Back at the lodge you can use the pool before an included dinner.

days.title: Kruger National Park Region
included: Full-day safari with local wildlife specialists
Visit prime game viewing areas including waterholes and rest camps
days.description: Another full day exploring Kruger with wildlife specialists who know where animals tend to gather. You'll check out waterholes and rest camps looking for antelope and birds. The park has massive diversity, so there's plenty to find. You'll have pool time before an African-style included dinner.

days.title: Kruger National Park Region
days.meals: Breakfast, Dinner (African dinner in the bush with Amarula liqueur (Marula fruit-based))
days.description: You get to pick your safari setup for the day, choosing a full-day, half-day, or sunrise game drive with your guide. You'll follow animals as they hunt and feed. That evening, you'll have your final African dinner in the bush and share favourite stories while sipping Amarula, a local liqueur from Marula fruit, around the campfire.

days.title: Kruger National Park - Panorama Route - Johannesburg
included: Visit Three Rondavels for Blyde River Canyon views
days.description: The Panorama Route takes you from Kruger National Park toward Johannesburg. You'll start at Three Rondavels viewpoint for views of the Blyde River Canyon. Then you stop at Bourke's Luck Potholes to see the wild water formations where the canyon begins. On clear days you can see into Kruger and across to Mozambique. A farewell dinner in Johannesburg caps off the journey.

days.title: Johannesburg
days.description: After breakfast the tour officially ends and the group goes their separate ways. You have the option to join an optional tour of Soweto, a lively township with plenty of history, or explore Johannesburg (called Jozi locally) on your own.

qa.question: What hotels do you use? Is there an option for Zimbabwe tour to see Victoria Falls?
qa.answer: Yes, we do offer a tour that includes Victoria Falls in Zimbabwe. The tour is called South Africa Escape with Victoria Falls. The tour combines South Africa and Zimbabwe, including: Cape Town and the Cape Winelands Hermanus and the Garden Route Oudtshoorn and the Cango Caves Johannesburg Kruger National Park with multiple safari experiences The Panorama Route and Blyde River Canyon Victoria Falls in Zimbabwe, including a guided tour of the falls A Zambezi River sunset cruise A free day in Victoria Falls with optional activities, including a Chobe Day Trip to Botswana For the hotels, the tour uses a range of hotels and safari lodges throughout the itinerary, depending on the location. The final hotel details are provided in the final tour program closer to departure.

Regarding the room, if you have booked a twin-share room and we are unable to match you with another same-gender traveller, you will usually be allocated a single room at no additional cost.

intro:
Explore one of Ireland’s most spectacular regions on this five day tour of Ireland.
You’ll capture Atlantic waves crashing against rugged cliffs, impressive castles looming over ancient monasteries, and cities bursting with myth and mystery.
It’s a tour that’s perfect for people who like their mountains mighty, their music merry, and their memories magnificent

days.title: Dublin to Galway
included: Visit Kilbeggan Distillery with whiskey tasting
Explore Clonmacnoise abbey with stone crosses, ancient churches and round towers
optional: Lunch at a traditional pub in a village near Clonmacnoise
days.start_point: The Kilkenny Design Shop, 6-15 Nassau St, Dublin, D02, Ireland (Opposite the Kilkenny Shop, Nassau St, Dublin, 09:00)
days.description: Head out west from Dublin through farmland and peat bogs toward Kilbeggan Distillery where you'll do a whiskey tasting. After that, you'll walk around Clonmacnoise to see the ruined abbey with its ancient stone crosses and round towers. Grab lunch at a traditional pub, then it's on to Galway City for your first night. The drive takes you through some real rural Irish countryside, so there's plenty to look at along the way.

days.title: Galway to Killarney
included: Admission to Cliffs of Moher with environmental exhibition
optional: Lunch in a village near Kilfenora
days.description: This morning you'll check out the Burren's limestone pavements and the rare plants that grow there. Stop at Kilfenora to see the ancient cathedral, then head to the Cliffs of Moher for walks along the cliff tops and to visit the environmental exhibition. You'll take a ferry across the Shannon Estuary, and from there continue south toward Killarney where you'll stay for three nights. It's quite a bit of ground to cover, but the scenery makes it worthwhile.

days.title: Dingle Peninsula
included: Visit Slea Head with views of Blasket Islands
optional: Walk along beaches and cliff tops near Slea Head
Evening stroll in Killarney National Park
days.description: Start your Dingle Peninsula exploration at Inch Beach with its long sandy stretch. Drive through the colorful town of Dingle itself, then continue to Slea Head where you'll get views out to the Blasket Islands. You've got time to spend on the beaches and up on the cliff tops, plus you'll try some seafood in Dingle village. By evening you'll head back to Killarney and take a stroll through the National Park before settling in for the night.

days.title: Ring of Kerry
included: Explore Ring of Kerry scenic route
Visit Derrynane House with scenic gardens and beach
optional: Alternative quick snack and visit to Valentia Island and Skellig Experience
Walk in Derrynane House gardens or along beach
days.description: You'll drive the Ring of Kerry route today, traveling through valleys and villages with Carrauntoohil mountain in view. There's Daniel O'Connell's birthplace to see, and you'll stop in Portmagee fishing village for lunch. If you're interested, there's the optional Valentia Island and Skellig Experience to fit in. Later you'll pass through Waterville, take in the views at Coonmakista pass, visit Derrynane House with its gardens and beach access, stop at Moll's Gap, and see Ladies View. Before heading back to Killarney, you'll check out Torc Waterfall. It's a full day but breaks up nicely with different stops along the way.

days.title: Blarney Castle - Kinsale - Rock of Cashel to Dublin
included: Opportunity to kiss the Blarney Stone
optional: Visit Charles Fort ruins in Kinsale
days.description: Starting out, you'll head east through West Cork's mountains and the Lee Valley toward Blarney Castle. Once there, you'll have time to walk around the grounds and, if you're interested, kiss the famous Blarney Stone. After that, you're heading to Kinsale, a historic port town where you'll grab lunch and check out the colorful harbour and the ruins of Charles Fort. From there, you'll make your way to the Rock of Cashel, a dramatic medieval complex sitting on limestone, where you can explore the site before heading back to Dublin in the early evening.

intro:
The archipelago of Orkney hides many treasures: and on our five day tour, your experienced guide will ensure you find the best of them.

You’ll unearth some of the most well-preserved prehistoric sites in Europe, examine a beautiful red sandstone coast, and discover the vibrant culture of remote island communities.

You’ll also have a chance to find the Loch Ness Monster, see Scotland’s beautiful north, and learn about the tragedy of Glencoe.

It’s an experience you’ll treasure for a lifetime

days.title: Edinburgh to Inverness
days.start_point: Edinburgh Bus Station, St Andrews Square, Edinburgh, Scotland EH1 3DQ, United Kingdom (Gate J and Gate K, Edinburgh Bus Station, St Andrew Square, Edinburgh, EH1 3DQ, 08:30)
days.description: You'll head west from Edinburgh, passing Stirling Castle and the Wallace Monument before stopping in Callander for a break. From there, the route crosses into the Highlands with views of Loch Lubnaig, Loch Earn, Glen Ogle, and Glen Dochart opening up around you. After passing through Glencoe, you'll travel north along the Great Glen toward Loch Ness, where there's time to scan the water if you're hoping to spot something legendary. You'll arrive in Inverness and get settled into your accommodation, leaving the evening free to walk around town at your own pace.

days.title: Inverness to Kirkwall
included: Optional visit to Kirkwall Viking Cathedral
days.description: Early morning departure from Inverness takes you across the Black Isle and past Dunrobin Castle along the northeast Highland coastline with dramatic scenery throughout. You'll head to John o' Groats (depending on weather and ferry schedules), then on to Gills Bay for the ferry crossing into Orkney. Once you arrive, you'll visit the Italian Chapel before reaching Kirkwall, where the evening is yours to explore the Viking Cathedral and the historic narrow streets winding through town.

days.title: Kirkwall
days.description: Today focuses on Orkney's landscapes and history. You'll see the green pastures and golden sand beaches, then visit Skara Brae, a 5,000-year-old village, followed by the Brodgar stone circle and the standing stones at Stenness. Next comes Maeshowe, where Norse runic inscriptions from the 12th century cover the walls inside. You'll return to Kirkwall for your second night there, giving you time to rest before heading back.

days.title: Kirkwall to Ullapool
included: Ferry crossing from Orkney to mainland
days.description: After sleeping in a bit, you'll take the ferry back to the mainland across waters with Viking history. The drive across Scotland's far north passes dramatic mountains like Ben Loyal and Ben Hope, rocky cliffs, and golden sand beaches. You'll explore the Assynt mountains and northwest Highlands, stopping to see the 15th-century ruins of Ardvreck Castle. Later, you'll reach Ullapool, a whitewashed fishing village where you'll stay your final night.

days.title: Ullapool to Edinburgh
included: Drive through Perthshire Big Tree country
days.meals: Breakfast, Lunch (Lunch in Caledonian Pine Forest surroundings)
days.description: You'll leave Ullapool and see Corrieshalloch Gorge, where the River Droma drops 60 metres down in a dramatic fall. After passing Loch Glascarnoch and Inverness, you'll stop at Culloden Moor to learn about the 1746 battle there, then visit the ancient standing stones at Clava Cairns (recognizable from the Outlander books). The route continues through the ancient Caledonian Pine Forest with the Cairngorm mountains alongside. You'll have lunch in the beautiful surroundings before traveling through Perthshire and the Kingdom of Fife, eventually returning to Edinburgh by evening.

attributes.tip: Walk among ruins, temples, and timeless landmarks

intro:
The fossils on the beaches resembled King Arthur’s slayed dragons. The stones of Stonehenge looked like they could have been moved by giants. And who could have known what beasts lurked the in misty, craggy climes of Dartmoor.
On this tour, we enliven your imagination and take you to all of Devon and Cornwall’s mystic landscapes and hidden-away alcoves.
You experience Norman Cathedrals, Roman towns, harbour villages, beautiful beaches, ruined castles, and more.
But watch out; because spend enough time here, and you may start to believe some of the mythical tales yourself

days.title: London to Exeter
included: Visit Stonehenge visitor centre and view prehistoric exhibition
Land train shuttle to Stonehenge stone circles
optional: Visit Norman Great Hall in Winchester
days.start_point: SW1W 9SH, London, Greater London, England, United Kingdom (Stance 3, Greenline Coach Terminal, Bulleid Way, Victoria, London, SW1W 9SH , 09:15)
days.description: Start your journey heading through historic Wessex toward Winchester, where you'll see the Anglo-Saxon heritage and the magnificent cathedral. From there, continue on to Stonehenge, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. You'll have time at the award-winning visitor centre and can take a land train shuttle right out to the famous stone circles themselves. Later in the day, travel to Exeter where you'll be staying for the next two nights.

days.title: Exeter
optional: Walk or sightsee at Clapper Bridge, Postbridge
days.description: This morning head out to explore the remote Dartmoor, which is home to native ponies and striking rock formations with diverse flora and fauna. You'll cross the ancient Clapper Bridge at Postbridge and stop in Tavistock, a historic market town that happens to be the birthplace of Sir Francis Drake. After that, return to Exeter in the early afternoon and spend the rest of the day leisurely checking out the city's ancient riches, including the city walls, Norman cathedral, Royal Albert Memorial, and the Quayside.

days.title: Exeter to Falmouth
optional: Visit Museum of Witchcraft in Boscastle
days.description: Travel west to Cornwall's North coast and explore Boscastle, an Elizabethan fishing village with dramatic headland views. From there, visit Tintagel and its clifftop castle ruins, which are purportedly the birthplace of King Arthur. Continue on to Port Isaac, another fishing village, and then head south to Falmouth where you'll settle in for the next two nights.

days.title: Falmouth
optional: Explore St Ives galleries and harbour-side streets
days.description: Head to England's westerly tip starting with St Michael's Mount, an island community. During the day you'll visit the unique Minack Theatre perched above the ocean, the National Trust beach at Porthcurno, and Land's End. Later travel through the Cornish tin mining heritage landscape (you might recognize it from the Poldark series), then finish at St Ives with its galleries and narrow harbour-side streets before returning to Falmouth for the evening.

days.title: Falmouth to London
days.description: Leave Cornwall and cross Bodmin Moor, a wild moorland that's designated as an area of outstanding natural beauty. Continue to Glastonbury where you can visit the 7th century Abbey ruins, grab lunch, or climb Glastonbury Tor if you want views across five counties. After that, it's time to travel back to London, concluding your journey through Devon and Cornwall.

intro:
Sun, sand and plenty of samba – see some of Brazil’s hottest highlights all packed together in an eight-day adventure. Start the party in Rio de Janeiro, where Copacabana, Ipanema and Christ the Redeemer all vie for your attention. Travel to the cobbled streets of Paraty, then cruise to the pristine Ilha Grande – an island where lush green rainforests meet untouched sandy beaches. You’ll have local knowledge to guide your way and plenty of time to explore at your own pace, and when it comes to free time in Brazil, all you need to know is the word ‘praia’ – beach.

This trip is designed for travellers who value their independence but also want the benefit of a local leader and a group to share the experience with. The itinerary has plenty of free time where your leader will suggest optional activities. Please budget spending money for these activities and transport to and from them., At certain times of year temperatures can be high in Brazil, but don’t let the heat keep you from exploring! Just make sure you use sun protection, wear layers to combat the heat, and drink plenty of water., While the crew will do their best to follow the itinerary, variations may occur due to weather or local conditions. A sense of humour and flexibility will ensure you have a fun, relaxing trip through this beautiful part of the world, no matter what happens., This trip doesn’t spend a lot of time in Rio de Janeiro. We highly recommend you plan extra time in this fascinating city if your time allows. Please speak to your booking agent if you are interested in booking additional nights in the city., We've sourced our accommodation very carefully and picked the best possible accommodations in line with the Intrepid style of travel, but please note that service and accommodation in Brazil may differ from standards at home. There may be times when you’ll need to carry your luggage for short distances, such as between transport and your accommodation.

intro: Journey through New Zealand's natural wonderland on a 7-day luxury road trip through the South Island. Explore Queenstown, the adventure capital, hike the Franz Josef glacier, cruise Milford Sound and discover NZ’s highest peak, Mount Cook.

days.title: Lake Tekapo
included: Explore local bike trails at Lake Tekapo
Relax in lakeside hot springs with stargazing at Dark Sky Reserve
landmarks: Aoraki Mackenzie International Dark Sky Reserve
days.start_point: JUCY Snooze, 5 Peter Leeming Rd, Christchurch, Canterbury Region 8053, New Zealand (Outside Main Entrance of Lylo Christchurch (Formally Jucy Snooze), 09:00 - 09:15)
days.description: You'll head out to Lake Tekapo and spend time around those turquoise waters that everyone photographs. There's bike trails in the area if you want to get active, or you can relax in the lakeside hot springs. Later in the evening, you'll have chances to look up at the night sky since this region is designated as a Dark Sky Reserve with minimal light pollution, which makes stargazing really something special here.

days.title: Tekapo to Queenstown
included: Transport to Queenstown in luxury vehicle
optional: Skydiving over the Southern Alps from $299
days.description: You'll start out in Tekapo with some free time to walk around or finish any trails from yesterday. After that, it's a drive to Queenstown, New Zealand's adventure hub. Once you arrive, you'll get settled into your place for the next three days and walk around town to get your bearings. The area has no shortage of activities on offer like skydiving, bungy jumping, canyoning, and ziplining if you're feeling adventurous.

days.title: Milford Sound
included: Transport to Milford Sound in luxury vehicle
days.description: Today you're heading out on a daytrip to Milford Sound, which is a UNESCO World Heritage site. The cruise takes you through the fiord where you'll see waterfalls, old-growth forests, and tall mountain faces. If you're lucky, you might catch dolphins leaping in the water. Back in Queenstown by evening, you can grab a beer, check out the nightlife, or stop by Fergburger, which is pretty famous around here.

days.title: Queenstown Adventures
optional: Skydiving over the Southern Alps from $299
Jet Boating up the canyon from $135
days.description: You've got a full day in Queenstown with lots of options depending on what you're comfortable doing. Want an adrenaline rush? Bungy jumping, canyon swings, skydiving over the Southern Alps, or jet boating are on the table. If you'd rather something less intense, horse riding, mountain biking, or luging are also available around the area.

days.title: Wanaka to Franz Josef
days.meals: Breakfast, Dinner (Group dinner at guide's favorite spot)
days.description: After taking time in Wanaka, you'll travel along the West Coast with rainforests and icy glaciers visible on either side. You'll go over Haast Pass, which takes you through rugged terrain with waterfalls along the way. By evening you'll reach Franz Josef, which sits near several glacier fields and serves as a gateway to explore them.

days.title: Franz Josef Glacier
included: Stop at the rugged West Coast township of Franz Josef
days.description: You'll spend the day at or around Franz Josef glacier. If you're up for hiking, you can go on a guided walk with crampons, or book a helicopter tour to see the formations from above. Not into that? Try quad biking, kayaking on glacier-fed lakes, or soak in the hot pools. Top it off with a cold drink to cool down after all that activity.

days.title: Arthur's Pass to Christchurch
included: Visit Mount Cook, one of the highest settlements in New Zealand
days.description: You'll stop briefly in Hokitika, then drive through Arthur's Pass with the snow-capped Southern Alps surrounding you on the journey. This route takes you back across the South Island toward Christchurch, where your trip wraps up. You'll say goodbye here after several days of driving, hiking, and experiencing different landscapes across the South Island.

intro:
WANT TO EXPLORE AND EXPERIENCE THE REAL IRELAND? 

­ 

Well, look no further, as we have the perfect 7 day tour experience that will definitely captivate your eyes and heart as we explore the most dramatic landscapes of Ireland’s wild Atlantic coastline. 

­ 

Our Wild South tour commences in Dublin and brings us from Cork’s wild Atlantic setting in the south to the bohemian capital of Ireland Galway city and back to Dublin. 

­ 

Experience jaw dropping scenery, unique towns and villages full of vibrant colors and Gaelic culture, the roar of the wild Atlantic Ocean and amazing activities such as kayaking on the Lakes of Killarney, hiking on the Ring of Kerry and Dingle, exploring the impressive Cliffs of Moher and the wild Burren. You can experience all this and more, as we take you off the beaten track to discover the real Ireland and its beautiful Wild Atlantic Way.

­ 

TOUR HIGHLIGHTS

  • Discover Ireland’s wild and rugged coastline
  • Visit the beautiful Killarney National Park
  • Discover the world famous destinations of the Ring of Kerry and Dingle
  • Explore the spectacular Cliffs of Moher and the wild Burren
  • Discover Galway City, the Bohemian capital of Ireland
  • Enjoy great food and fun traditional music nights

START POINT  The Ashling Hotel, Parkgate Street, Arran Quay, Dublin 8.

­

RETURN POINT  The Ashling Hotel, Parkgate Street, Arran Quay, Dublin 8.

­ 

DEPARTURE DAY(S) Sunday

­ 

DEPARTURE TIME(S) 11.00 am – Please arrive by 10:45 am for a prompt departure @ 11:00 am*

­ 

*From 1st September 2024 Tour Departure is @ 11:00 am – Please arrive by 10:45 am for a prompt departure @ 11:00 am*

days.title: Dublin to Cork
days.start_point: Ashling Hotel, Parkgate St, Bridewell, Dublin, Ireland (Entrance, 10:30 - 11:00)
days.description: Starting out from Dublin at 11am, you'll head south toward Cork with a stop planned at the Rock of Cashel. This medieval site sits on limestone and gives you views across the landscape. After grabbing lunch, it's a scenic drive along the Wild Atlantic Way coast toward Cork. You'll arrive and settle into the town, which has a relaxed, friendly feel to it.

days.title: Cork to Killarney
optional: Visit Mizen Head Signal Station (available Mid-March to October)
days.description: This morning you have time to relax in Killarney town or walk through the national park and around the lakes if you'd like. By midday, head to Muckross Park to see the gardens and Muckross Abbey, a 15th century Franciscan friary. After lunch, it's north along the coast toward the Cliffs of Moher, and you'll finish the evening in Lahinch where traditional music sessions and fresh seafood are part of the local scene.

days.title: Killarney to Lahinch
optional: Adventure through Killarney National Park and Lakes
days.description: Today focuses on the Ring of Kerry, featuring rugged coastline, golden beaches, lakes, and mountain ranges. You'll take a tour of Valentia Island to learn about its history and heritage on the Atlantic's edge. Weather allowing, you might catch views of the Skellig Islands. Throughout the route, there are viewing points where you'll learn about the historical significance and get chances for photos before heading back to Killarney.

days.title: Ring of Kerry and Valentia Island
days.description: You're heading to the Dingle Peninsula, which has deep archaeological and historical roots. Start at Inch beach for a walk along its famous golden sands with waves crashing in. Continue west to Slea Head at Europe's edge, where you can see the wild coastline and the Blasket Islands out in the water. Spend time exploring the peninsula's Gaelic culture and learning some Irish words, then visit Dingle town (known for Fungi the dolphin) before returning to Lahinch.

days.title: Dingle Peninsula
days.description: Leaving Galway at 9am, you'll head east back toward Dublin, crossing the River Shannon along the way. The tour concludes with drop-off at Dublin Airport at 1pm, then at The Ashling Hotel on Parkgate Street, Arran Quay, Dublin 8 at 1:30pm. It's the end of the journey, and you'll head home with memories from Ireland's varied destinations.

days.title: Cliffs of Moher, Burren, and Galway
included: Explore Cliffs of Moher interpretation centre
optional: Tour Galway's historical places of interest
days.description: Starting at the Cliffs of Moher in County Clare, these stretch almost 10 km with impressive views. Check out the interpretation centre to learn how the geological formations came about. From there, head north toward Galway, passing through the Burren with its unusual moon-like terrain. You'll have lunch along the Wild Atlantic Way, then arrive in Galway, the city's known for its bohemian vibe, good food scene, and historical spots worth checking out.

days.title: Galway to Dublin
days.description: The day takes you along Cork's coastline and up through mountain passes heading toward Killarney. You'll see the Altar Wedge Tomb overlooking Toormore Bay, then continue to Mizen Head at Ireland's southernmost point. From there, you can choose between checking out Mizen Head Signal Station or walking Barleycove beach with its golden sand. After crossing through mountainous terrain into Kerry, you'll reach Killarney and its national park with lakes and local character.

intro:
Thai Experience is our premium group tour. With epic upgraded accommodation and lots of amazing inclusions, it’s perfect for those wanting to see the best of Thailand in style. You’ll discover Bangkok by boat and tuk tuk, visit ancient temples, learn to cook delicious Thai food, sleep on floating bungalows, stay in jungle tree houses, explore tropical islands, snorkel in crystal clear water, learn the art of Muay Thai boxing, discover the famous Phi Phi Islands, visit an elephant sanctuary, have a Thai massage, party on the beach and more! With an awesome group leader and an instant group of friends, get ready for the trip of a lifetime!

+ Our tours are all 100% Carbon Neutral!

days.title: Arrival in Bangkok
days.description: Your driver meets you at the airport and takes you to your Bangkok hotel. After checking in, you'll have time to rest from your flight and get settled. This is when you'll meet the other travelers in your group, so grab a meal together if everyone's up for it.

days.title: Bangkok
included: Tuk tuk ride through Bangkok streets
days.description: This morning you'll board a long-tail boat and cruise through Bangkok's waterways, stopping at several sacred temples along the way. The water route gives you a different perspective of the city than most visitors see. After lunch, you'll navigate the bustling streets by tuk tuk, hitting different neighborhoods and getting a feel for how locals move around the city. By evening, you'll head into Bangkok's nightlife scene, checking out bars and clubs in the main entertainment areas. It's a full day that covers the city from multiple angles.

days.title: Bangkok to Southern Thailand
days.description: You'll spend the morning in a hands-on cooking class with a local chef who'll teach you traditional Thai techniques and recipes. You'll prepare several dishes from scratch and get to eat what you've made for lunch. Later in the afternoon, you'll head to the train station and board an overnight sleeper train heading south. You'll settle into your cabin as the train departs in the evening, and you can relax or explore the train before getting some sleep during the journey.

days.title: Khao Sok National Park
days.description: You arrive at Khao Sok National Park with its clear lakes and dramatic limestone cliffs. The morning and afternoon are for tubing or kayaking depending on what you choose. Then you'll move into your floating bungalow right on the water for the night, which is pretty cool.

days.title: Khao Sok
days.description: Today takes you deeper into Khao Sok's rainforest where you'll experience the jungle environment directly. In the morning, you'll visit a local family's plantation and learn how they practice sustainable farming methods. You'll have a choice for the afternoon: either go tubing down a river that winds through the jungle or take a trekking route on foot through the forest. After that, you'll head to your accommodation in tree houses built right into the forest canopy. Spending the night up in the trees gives you a real sense of being surrounded by nature.

days.title: Khao Sok to Koh Phangan
days.description: A boat takes you from the national park to Koh Phangan, a tropical island with white beaches. Once you check into your beachside bungalow, the afternoon is yours to either walk around and check out the island or just relax on the sand. Dinner and a beach party happen in the evening.

days.title: Koh Phangan
included: Visit amazing beaches on Koh Phangan
days.description: You're spending the day finding the best beaches on Koh Phangan, swimming, and soaking up sun. During the afternoon, you'll visit a viewpoint or two that look out over the island. Later on, there's a beach BBQ where everyone gathers for dinner right by the water.

days.title: Koh Phangan
days.description: You get to choose your activity today based on what appeals to you. If you want something active, sign up for a Muay Thai boxing session with an expert instructor who'll teach you proper technique. If you'd rather something more relaxing, there's a yoga class available instead. Later in the day, you'll get a traditional Thai massage to help your muscles recover or just to unwind. Since it's your final night on the island, you'll have the evening free to enjoy the atmosphere and prepare for your departure the next day.

days.title: Koh Phangan to Phi Phi Islands
days.description: You're traveling to the Phi Phi Islands using a combination of boat and bus. Once you arrive and settle into your accommodation, you'll have the evening free to explore and experience the island's nightlife with your group.

days.title: Phi Phi Leh
included: Private speedboat to Phi Phi Leh
days.description: This morning you're boarding a private speedboat to reach Phi Phi Leh. You'll visit hidden lagoons with turquoise water, snorkel in clear areas with fish, and walk across white sand beaches. It's a full water and beach day, so bring sunscreen.

days.title: Phi Phi Islands to Phuket
included: Morning hike to Phi Phi viewpoint
days.description: Early morning is for hiking up to the viewpoint that overlooks the Phi Phi Islands, which gives you great views to photograph. The rest of the morning and afternoon you'll relax on the beaches. Later, you take the ferry to Phuket and check into a boutique hotel. Dinner and drinks round out your evening there.

days.title: Elephant Sanctuary
days.description: You'll spend the day at a rescued elephant sanctuary where Thailand's most revered animal lives. You'll get close to these gentle giants, learn about their individual histories and backgrounds, and understand how the sanctuary protects and cares for them daily. This isn't just about watching from a distance, it's a real interaction with the animals. In the evening, you'll gather for a farewell dinner with drinks to celebrate the end of your trip and reflect on everything you've experienced. It's a meaningful way to wrap up your time in Thailand.

days.title: Phuket Departure
days.description: Your trip officially ends today. You can choose to stay longer in Phuket or keep moving through Thailand if you want. Your group leader will help you sort out whatever you decide to do next.

qa.question: How much is it to book a private room? Also, would I fly into Bangkok and fly home from Phuket? What do you recommend? Flights / Transfers
qa.answer: For this trip you will need to fly in to either airport in Bangkok: Suvarnabhumi International Airport (BKK) / Don Mueang International Airport (DMK). The trip will finish on the beautiful island of Phuket on the morning of Day 13. You can choose to stay on longer in Phuket and fly home from there if possible. Alternatively, if you need to get back to Bangkok the quickest option is a one hour internal flight. The earliest the Phuket to Bangkok flight should be booked is 8am on Day 13. The taxi can be booked locally, and the flight can be booked with a variety of airlines including Air Asia, Nok Air and Bangkok Air. For a private room on the Experience trip it would cost an extra £400. It wouldn't be possible to have a private room on the overnight train, and a private room in Sarana, Koh Phangan is dependant on availability. P

qa.question: I'm wanting to travel with my 21 yr old daughter to celebrate her college graduation, but I am a 51 yrs old. Would you allow us to book this tour?
qa.answer: Our tours are designed for travellers aged 18–40's, with a maximum age limit of 49. Unfortunately, this means we're unable to accept bookings for anyone over this age.

qa.question: I'm thinking of booking this tour for myself and kids (27 and 18), but I'll be 52 this year. Do I not qualify?
qa.answer: Our trips are designed specifically for travellers aged 18–40s, and so we have a maximum age limit of 49. This isn't based on attitude, fitness or ability. It's simply about maintaining the trip style and group dynamic that our travellers come expecting.

qa.question: what happens if our arrival flights are cancelled/ delayed ? Flights / Transfers
qa.answer: If your flight is delayed or cancelled, we would advise you to let us know as soon as possible so we can discuss the available options with you. If you're feeling concerned about potential disruptions, we recommend arriving one or two days before your trip begins. This can give you extra peace of mind and some time to settle in before the tour starts.

name: 31-Day Southeast Asia Adventure: Thailand, Laos, Vietnam, and Cambodia

attributes.name: City & Culture
attributes.tip: Immerse yourself in rich history and local traditions

attributes.name: Group Tour
attributes.tip: Join a group and forge lifelong friendships

attributes.name: Fully Guided
attributes.tip: An experienced guide will be with you for the entire tour

intro:
Ready for the ultimate Southeast Asia adventure? Over 31 epic days you’ll explore Thailand, Laos, Vietnam and Cambodia – from vibrant cities to paradise islands.


Trek through jungles to hidden waterfalls, meet gentle elephants, cruise Halong Bay, swim with glowing plankton, and watch the sunrise over Angkor Wat. With our Adventure Leaders guiding the way, you’ll hit all the highlights, uncover local secrets, and make memories (and friends) to last a lifetime.

days.title: Bangkok
included: Dinner and tuk-tuk tour of Bangkok highlights
days.start_point: Bangkok, Thailand (Lub d Chinatown Bangkok Hostel, 17:00)
days.description: You'll land in Bangkok and meet your Adventure Leader along with the rest of the group. After a quick rundown of what's coming up, you're heading out for dinner at a rooftop restaurant by tuk-tuk. Later that evening, you'll take a boat cruise past Bangkok's lit-up landmarks before wrapping up the night at one of the city's rooftop bars.

days.title: Bangkok to Chiang Mai
included: Overnight train journey to Chiang Mai
optional: Old City temple tour including Grand Palace, Wat Pho, and Wat Arun
days.description: There's an optional temple tour where you can visit the Grand Palace, Wat Pho's Reclining Buddha, and riverside Wat Arun if you're interested, though you'll need to arrange luggage storage first. Later in the day, you'll head to the train station by bus and board an overnight train heading north toward Chiang Mai.

days.title: Chiang Mai
days.description: You arrive in Chiang Mai and grab breakfast before heading to your countryside homestay. After getting settled in, there's a home-cooked lunch waiting for you. In the afternoon, you'll lace up for a jungle trek that's around 4-6km with a waterfall stop along the way. You'll return to the homestay for dinner and spend the night surrounded by nature.

days.title: Chiang Mai
included: Half-day elephant sanctuary visit with guided walk
Traditional Thai refreshments at rest station
days.description: Breakfast at the homestay gets you fueled up before spending a half-day at an elephant sanctuary where you'll walk with elephants in the forest and learn about them up close. Mid-trek, you'll have traditional Thai refreshments at a rest station. After lunch at a riverside location, you'll check into your hostel for some downtime. The afternoon gives you a choice between a Thai cooking class or an exciting Muay Thai show.

days.title: Chiang Mai
optional: Sticky Waterfall visit with rock climbing
days.description: You'll ride in a traditional red songthaew and start with local temples, including a Monk Chat experience where you can learn about Buddhism directly from monks. Then you're heading to the famous mountaintop Wat Doi Suthep with its golden stupa and panoramic views. Grab lunch at the temple or nearby, then return to the hostel. The afternoon gives you the option to ride out for 1.5 hours to the Sticky Waterfall for rock climbing, or stay put. The evening is free for dinner and optional clubbing at Zoe in Yellow.

days.title: Chiang Mai
days.description: Today is yours to shape. Adrenaline seekers can choose whitewater rafting on a 10km river stretch, a 3-hour trek through northern landscapes, or do both for a full adventure day. If you prefer a slower pace, you can wander through Chiang Mai's Old Town on your own, discovering temples, cafes, and hidden spots. In the afternoon, you'll check out a lively local market packed with souvenirs and street food.

days.title: Bangkok to Luang Prabang
days.description: You'll check out of your hostel and catch a flight to Luang Prabang, which sits in the heart of northern Laos. Once you're settled into your accommodation, the evening is yours to do as you please. There's an optional group dinner with fellow travelers, and you can explore the lively Hmong Night Market to browse souvenirs, crafts, and sample local street food.

days.title: Luang Prabang
included: Kuang Si Waterfalls visit with hiking and swimming
optional: Cycling tour through villages and pottery village
Dinner and Baci ceremony at local home
days.description: Rise early for an optional Takbat Lao Ceremony where monks collect alms through the streets, a fascinating cultural ritual. Active travelers can bike through surrounding villages, cross the Mekong River, visit Ban Som and Ban Na hill tribe villages, and check out Ban Chan's pottery village where you can try making traditional jars. You'll return for lunch. In the early afternoon, the whole group visits Kuang Si Waterfalls with tropical trails, swimming in turquoise pools, and exploring the natural sights. The evening offers an optional visit to a local home for dinner and a traditional Baci blessing ceremony.

days.title: Luang Prabang
optional: Cooking Experience with wet market visit
days.description: Your day is free to explore at your own pace with optional activities to go deeper into local culture. You can experience authentic farm life by learning the 14 steps of rice cultivation or trying traditional bamboo weaving or blacksmithing. Alternatively, take a tuk-tuk to the wet market, pick fresh ingredients, and learn to cook authentic Lao dishes in a cooking class. You could also spend time volunteering with Big Brother Mouse to help locals improve their English.

days.title: Luang Prabang to Vang Vieng
included: Blue Lagoon 2 visit with swimming and rope-swinging
days.description: You're heading to Vang Vieng, Laos's adventure hub surrounded by mountains, rivers, and caves. After catching the train and arriving, you'll grab lunch and check into your hostel. Then you'll dive right into action with a visit to Blue Lagoon 2 where you can swim, rope-swing, or simply relax in the turquoise waters. The evening is yours to recharge or explore local nightlife.

days.title: Vang Vieng
days.description: Today offers packed optional adventure choices. Thrill-seekers can go rock climbing, take a biking tour, or hike up to Pha Ngern Viewpoint for great vistas. Prefer something more relaxed? You can leisurely float down the Mekong River in a rubber tube while taking in the scenery. The evening is free to relax, recharge, or explore the vibrant nightlife.

days.title: Hanoi
optional: Group dinner and drinks at Old Quarter Night Market
days.description: You'll start with a visit to Hoa Lo Prison to learn about Vietnam's history. Then head to Hoan Kiem Lake with its central temple for a leisurely stroll while observing locals enjoying games and activities on tree-lined French colonial streets. Explore Old Quarter Street for dining options. Spend your free afternoon navigating Hanoi's narrow streets and bustling traffic like a local. Optional evening activities include a Water Puppet Show for a unique cultural experience and group dinner with drinks at the Old Quarter Night Market sampling street food. Take it easy tonight since there's an early bus tomorrow.

days.title: Hanoi to Halong Bay
days.meals: Lunch (Lunch on cruise), Dinner (Dinner on cruise)
days.description: Travel to Halong Bay in Vietnam's northeastern region and board a serene boat at Lan Ha for a cruise through limestone karsts and emerald waters. Enjoy a delicious lunch on board while taking in the scenery. Spend time swimming and jumping from the boat. As the sun sets, gather for dinner on board, then settle in for an overnight stay on the cruise surrounded by one of the world's most beautiful seascapes.

days.title: Halong Bay to Phong Nha
included: Morning kayaking through lagoons and limestone formations
days.description: Start with an energetic morning of kayaking through hidden lagoons and around towering limestone cliffs. Enjoy a hearty lunch on the cruise before departing Halong for the return bus journey to Hanoi. Freshen up at your accommodation, then climb aboard the sleeper bus from Hanoi heading south to Phong Nha for more epic exploration in Vietnam's landscapes.

days.title: Phong Nha
included: Bike ride to Bong Lai Village
days.description: You arrive and settle into your accommodation in Phong Nha, Vietnam's adventure hub. Hop on bikes and cycle to Bong Lai Village, a laid-back countryside spot with farms and jungle views, home to the famous 'Pub With Cold Beer'. Enjoy some cold Vietnamese beer, play volleyball, and relax for a few hours. As evening approaches, ask your Adventure Leader for suggestions on exploring Phong Nha's local nightlife.

days.title: Phong Nha
optional: Phong Nha Ke Bang National Park tour including Paradise Cave and Dark Cave
landmarks: Phong Nha Ke Bang National Park
days.description: Today is yours to relax or chase adventure. For thrill-seekers, join the optional tour of Phong Nha Ke Bang National Park to explore two incredible caves: Paradise Cave with limestone formations, and Dark Cave with ziplining, swimming, mud baths, and SUP boarding. The tour includes lunch, transport, and entrance fees. Wind down in the late afternoon and grab bakery snacks for tomorrow's sleeper bus, which passes through remote regions with limited food options.

days.title: Phong Nha to Hoi An
included: Ancient Town tour with guide introduction and free exploration
days.description: You arrive in Hoi An, a beautiful ancient town in Central Vietnam, and get picked up to your accommodation. Spend the morning resting and recharging after your journey, or ask your Adventure Leader for tips on exploring independently. Optional: take a ride in the famous coconut basket boats to glide along the water, learn about local farming practices, and experience rural Vietnamese life. In the afternoon, join a tour of Hoi An's Ancient Town, then wander the charming streets freely to discover hidden temples and the iconic Japanese Bridge. The evening offers optional group dinner and nightlife exploration.

days.title: Hoi An to Ho Chi Minh City
days.description: Start your morning with a hands-on cultural workshop making traditional lanterns so you can get creative, learn a local craft, and take home your handmade souvenir. Then transfer to Da Nang Airport for a short flight south to Ho Chi Minh City. Once checked into your hostel, the evening is yours to dive into the city's energy. Start with optional group dinner at a local spot, then choose your adventure: rooftop cocktails, explore the epic bar street, or join a lively bar crawl.

days.title: Hoi An to Ho Chi Minh City
days.description: Start your morning with an optional experience on iconic coconut basket boats before heading to a local farm. Later, proceed to the airport to catch a flight to Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam's final destination. Enjoy dinner in this vibrant city and soak in the nighttime cityscape from a rooftop bar. Consider joining an optional bar crawl to kick off your evening in style.

days.title: Ho Chi Minh City
days.description: Start with a guided tour of Ho Chi Minh City exploring popular landmarks. Join your group for a delightful lunch at a local restaurant, then the rest of the day is yours. Optionally visit the War Remnants Museum for vital insights into Vietnam War history. Come evening, dive into the vibrant nightlife with lively streets buzzing with energy, street vendors, and local aromas. Sample iconic Vietnamese dishes like banh mi, pho, goi cuon, banh xeo, BBQ skewers, or che dessert.

days.title: Ho Chi Minh City
days.description: Start the morning with an optional visit to the Cu Chi Tunnels, a fascinating network of connecting tunnels used during the war. Your Adventure Leader arranges private transport and you pay a small entrance fee. Crawl through tunnels, explore hidden chambers, and learn about Vietnam's history. In the afternoon, dive into Vietnam's legendary coffee culture with an optional coffee workshop to learn and taste famous Vietnamese coffee. Cap off the day with an unmissable karaoke experience in your private 2-hour room, belting out favorite tunes before continuing the party in the city.

days.title: Ho Chi Minh City to Phnom Penh
optional: Bassac Lane bar hop with free shots and karaoke
days.description: Rise and hit the road by bus from Ho Chi Minh City to Phnom Penh, crossing the Moc Bai border into Cambodia. The 9-hour journey offers perfect views of changing landscapes as you roll into a new country. Once in Phnom Penh, meet your Cambodian Adventure Leader, check into your hostel, and set out on a city walk to explore the sights. Enjoy a welcome chat at a rooftop restaurant to meet fellow travelers and hear about adventures ahead. In the evening, connect over an optional group welcome dinner before diving into Phnom Penh nightlife on Bassac Lane with free shots at every bar, karaoke, and vibrant energy.

days.title: Phnom Penh
included: Killing Fields of Choeung Ek tour
days.description: Start with a sobering but important tour of S21 Prison and the Killing Fields of Choeung Ek with a local guide via tuk tuk, offering vital insights into Cambodia's history. The rest of the day is yours with epic suggestions: feel fancy with an optional sunset cruise along the Tonle River enjoying unlimited beer or soft drinks, fresh fruit, and stunning riverside views. Finish by exploring the Phnom Penh Night Market, strolling stalls with your tour guide to grab souvenirs or sample delicious street food for dinner.

days.title: Phnom Penh to Koh Rong Sanloem
included: Cliffside sunset bar or rock pool trek (depending on season)
days.description: Head to Sihanoukville and catch a ferry to Koh Rong Sanloem, a peaceful island haven with powdery beaches, clear turquoise waters, and laid-back vibes. Meet local guides for a welcome chat and check-in. Depending on season: October to May brings an evening cliffside bar for sunset cocktails; June to September offers a walk through natural rock pools at sunset. Gather for dinner at Two Ducks restaurant featuring some of Cambodia's best burgers during happy hour. As night falls, grab your mask and snorkel for an unmissable bioluminescent plankton swim where you'll witness the magical glow of these tiny creatures.

days.title: Koh Rong Sanloem
included: Beach camping or pub quiz and bonfire (depending on season)
days.description: Begin with a delectable buffet breakfast setting the tone for an island day adventure. Trek through a local fishing village to Clearwater Bay for swimming, beach relaxation, and a picnic lunch. Hop on a boat for snorkeling at a nearby coral reef, then return to the village to unwind. Depending on season, wrap up with either beach camping under the stars or a beachfront pub quiz and bonfire.

days.title: Koh Rong Sanloem
included: Transfer to mainland for sleeper bus to Siem Reap
optional: Scuba diving with certified SSI instructors
days.description: Kickstart your day choosing from morning yoga (October to May), scuba diving with certified SSI instructors, leisurely kayaking, or experienced swimmers joining a coral reef clean-up. Prefer relaxing? Simply unwind under the sun. Enjoy a beachside BBQ lunch, then choose afternoon activities: beach clean-up with locals, kayaking to a neighboring island, or just chill. Later, head back to the mainland to catch your sleeper bus to Siem Reap.

days.title: Siem Reap
included: City orientation tour including riverside, Royal Gardens, and Made in Cambodia market
Blessing at Wat Prum Rat Temple
days.description: You arrive early and check in to your accommodation for a few hours' rest. In the late morning, enjoy an orientation tour exploring the riverside, Royal Gardens, Made in Cambodia market, and receive a blessing for safe travels at Wat Prum Rat Temple. In the afternoon, optionally indulge in a spa session at a nearby facility. Come evening, optionally join your group for a trip to Phare Circus, an incredible social organisation providing free education and arts training to over 1,200 children yearly with acrobatics shows featuring Cambodian storylines.

days.title: Siem Reap
included: Angkor Wat sunrise visit and temple exploration
days.description: Begin at dawn venturing to Angkor Wat, the UNESCO World Heritage Site and largest religious monument in the world. Explore temples including Ta Prohm, famous from the Lara Croft: Tomb Raider film. In the afternoon, optionally visit Apopo Hero Rats via tuk-tuk to learn how these creatures serve as effective demining tools in Cambodia. Come evening, choose a 1.5-hour pedal-pub car tour (including a drink) followed by sampling local Cambodian delicacies like crickets, frogs, and silkworms.

days.title: Siem Reap
included: Half-day lotus field and village cycling tour
days.description: Head out on a half-day cycling tour through lotus fields and a typical Cambodian village with various stops offering genuine glimpses of local life. Visit a duck farm, learn about rice cultivation, and savor local palm wine. In the afternoon, optionally head to Cambodia Wake Park for watersports including inflatable courses, wakeboarding, and an inland beach. In the evening, relish a farewell dinner with your group, reminiscing about the best bits of your tour.

qa.question: Why is the oldest age 45?
qa.answer: The age limit is in place because of the overall style, pace, accommodation, and group dynamic of the tour, and we aim to keep the experience consistent for everyone travelling. The 31-day Southeast Asia Tour includes shared dorm rooms in hostels and guesthouses, in addition to overnight trains and buses. The overall pace of the tour is moderate-high intensity, with travellers walking up to 20,000 steps per day. Although this tour is available to travellers aged 18–45, we generally find that most participants are in their 20s. name: Essential Costa Rica - Package with Manuel Antonio National Park

attributes.name: Nature & Wildlife
attributes.tip: Explore untamed landscapes teeming with wildlife

attributes.name: Group Tour
attributes.tip: Join a group and forge lifelong friendships

attributes.name: Partially Guided
attributes.tip: Independent travel, featuring selected guided excursions

intro: Uncover essential Costa Rica during this 10-day exotic adventure. Beginning and ending in the capital, San Jose, this tour offers you the chance to discover different aspects of this emblematic destination. Visit the most predominant natural areas of Costa Rica, including the Arenal Volcano National Park, and the cloud forest of Monteverde. Spend precious time visiting the Manuel Antonio National Park, one of the most stunning conservation areas on the planet. During the trip, keep an eye out for a variety of animals, bugs, as well as plants and don’t forget to mingle with the friendly locals for a versatile experience.

days.title: San Jose
days.start_point: Aeropuerto Internacional Juan Santamaría (SJO), Ruta Nacional 1, Alajuela, Alajuela, Costa Rica (Pick up at San Jose Airport)
days.description: You'll arrive in San Jose where a representative meets you at the airport. From there, it's a transfer to your hotel for your first night settling into Costa Rica.

days.title: San Jose - Tortuguero
included: Guided boat tour through Tortuguero National Park canals
Entrance fee to Tortuguero National Park
Walk around Tortuguero town and beach
days.description: Early morning departure by bus takes you through Braulio Carrillo National Park toward the Caribbean plains, with breakfast served along the way. The journey continues by boat through Tortuguero's rivers and canals until you reach the eco-lodge. After lunch, head into Tortuguero village to check out the town and beach. If you're visiting during turtle season (July-September hatching, September-December nesting), watch for baby turtles making their way to the ocean. The rest of your day is spent relaxing at the hotel with tropical forest and wildlife all around.

days.title: Tortuguero
included: Three-hour guided trip through Tortuguero National Park
optional: Optional late night turtle nesting tour (available during July-September season, purchasable directly at lodge)
days.description: You have the flexibility to spend the day relaxing by the pool or taking a three-hour guided trip into Tortuguero National Park. Watch for over 350 bird species, monkeys, crocodiles, sloths, and thick vegetation throughout the park. If you're there July through September, an optional late night turtle nesting tour is available through the lodge.

days.title: Tortuguero - Arenal
optional: Ecotermales Hot Springs (transportation, bilingual guide, entrance, dinner included; departure approximately 15:00 hrs, duration approximately 6 hrs)
days.description: Early morning boat ride takes you back to Guapiles, then it's a road transfer to a restaurant for lunch. After eating, you'll board a shared transfer heading toward the Arenal area. The afternoon and evening are yours to explore on your own or participate in optional activities like Ecotermales Hot Springs.

days.title: Arenal
included: Guided walking tour in Arenal Volcano National Park
optional: Zipline Adventure - Ama Extreme (7 extreme zip lines, park entrance, oxcart ride, Maleku Village visit; departure approximately 08:00 hrs / 10:30 hrs / 13:00 hrs / 14:00 hrs; duration approximately 2.5 hrs; minimum 2 participants required; restrictions apply)

La Fortuna Waterfall tour (500-meter trail descent, 60-meter waterfall, swimming available; transportation, bilingual guide, entrance fee included; departure approximately 08:00 hrs / 13:00 hrs; duration approximately 3 hrs)
days.description: Following breakfast, a guided walking tour through Arenal Volcano National Park shows you the volcano's activity patterns while your guide points out sloths, howler monkeys, anteaters, and the green landscapes. Back at the hotel by afternoon, you can relax or choose one optional activity like ziplining or visiting La Fortuna Waterfall.

days.title: Arenal - Monteverde
optional: Selvatura Treetop Walkway guided tour (3-hour hike, 8 suspension bridges, 3 km total trail length, bird's-eye rainforest canopy views)
Coffee Tour (learn about Costa Rican coffee, chocolate, and sugar cane production with cultural focus)
days.description: After breakfast and checkout, you'll head toward Monteverde. The journey includes a boat crossing at Arenal Lake, then a vehicle takes you up to Monteverde at 1,200 meters where rainforest transitions to cloud forest. The afternoon gives you time to wander through Santa Elena's shops and restaurants, or you can join optional activities like the Selvatura Treetop Walkway or Coffee Tour.

days.title: Monteverde
included: Hike through Monteverde Cloud Forest Biological Reserve
optional: Selvatura Treetop Walkway guided tour (3-hour hike, 8 suspension bridges, 3 km total trail length, bird's-eye rainforest canopy views)
Coffee Tour (learn about Costa Rican coffee, chocolate, and sugar cane production with cultural focus)
days.description: After breakfast, a hike through Monteverde Cloud Forest Biological Reserve shows you the forest's diverse wildlife including mammals, birds, butterflies, amphibians, reptiles, and insects. If you missed any optional tours the day before, like the Selvatura Treetop Walkway or Coffee Tour, you can join them today.

days.title: Monteverde - Manuel Antonio
days.description: Following breakfast, you'll travel toward Manuel Antonio National Park, descending to this beachside location. Once there, spend the rest of your day at the hotel, checking out the surrounding areas, using the facilities, or relaxing on the beach.

days.title: Manuel Antonio
included: Guided hike through Manuel Antonio National Park
days.description: After breakfast, head to Manuel Antonio National Park for a guided nature hike on the flat two-mile loop trail. Your guide explains the rainforest's natural history and points out plants and animals. Halfway through, take a 20-minute break at Third Beach where you can rest on the sand or swim. Look for sloths, birds, reptiles, wild orchids, butterflies, and tropical vegetation. The park is home to three of Costa Rica's four tropical primate species, and your guides have specialized equipment for wildlife watching and photography.

days.title: Manuel Antonio - San Jose
days.description: After a final breakfast, you'll transfer to Juan Santamaria International Airport at the right time to catch your flight home or onward to your next destination.

attributes.name: Nature & Wildlife
attributes.tip: Explore untamed landscapes teeming with wildlife

attributes.name: Group Tour
attributes.tip: Join a group and forge lifelong friendships

intro:
Join Southwest Adventure Tours for a 5 day adventure through Arches, Bryce Canyon, Canyonlands, Capitol Reef, and Zion National Parks. These magnificent parks are known as the Utah Mighty 5. Each park will enable you to see unique geological formations all within the region of Southern Utah. It will be a week you won’t soon forget!

Depart Las Vegas, NV early in a morning for a short drive to Zion National Park. (3 hours). Explore main canyon of Zion National Park. Late afternoon transfer to Kolob Fingers of Zion National Park for a walk to the Timber Creek Overlook.

days.title: Las Vegas to Zion National Park
included: Explore Zion Canyon via shuttle bus or vehicle
Scenic stops at one or more of five canyon overlooks
Optional guided hike to Scouts Lookout
Optional hike through Zion Canyon Narrows
Optional visit to Kolob Canyons and Timber Creek Overlook
days.start_point: 7250 Pollock Drive, Las Vegas, Nevada 89119, United States (At the Main Entrance of the hotel, 07:00 - 07:00)
days.description: You'll leave Las Vegas early and drive about 3 hours through the Mojave Desert and Virgin Gorge to reach Zion National Park. Once there, spend your day exploring Zion Canyon by shuttle bus or your own vehicle depending on the season. You have options for hikes ranging from the moderate Pa'rus Trail and Emerald Pools to the challenging Angels Landing or the water-filled Zion Canyon Narrows. The Riverside Walk is another choice if you want something easier. If daylight and weather cooperate, head to the Kolob Canyons section in the late afternoon before settling in for the night.

days.title: Zion to Canyonlands National Park to Moab
included: Drive through Hurricane Cliffs, Tushar Mountains, and San Rafael Swell
Optional stops at Eagle Canyon Overlook and Ghost Rock viewpoints
Explore Canyonlands National Park Island in the Sky District
days.description: This morning you'll drive just under 4 hours from Zion toward Canyonlands National Park, traveling through Hurricane Cliffs, the Tushar Mountains, and the remote San Rafael Swell. Along the way, you can stop at Eagle Canyon Overlook, Ghost Rock, and other viewpoints if you'd like. After grabbing lunch in Green River, spend the afternoon and evening in Canyonlands' Island in the Sky District. Check out Mesa Arch, Grand Viewpoint, Green River Overlook, Candlestick Tower, and ancestral Puebloan sites scattered throughout the area. You'll finish the day in Moab, the adventure town that'll be your base for the next couple of days.

days.title: Arches National Park to Capitol Reef National Park
included: Early morning exploration of Arches National Park
Scenic stops at Courthouse Towers and Park Avenue
Explore Windows Section including Turret Arch, North Window, and South Window
Optional visit to Grand Wash Narrows
days.description: Start early this morning to get ahead of the crowds at Arches National Park. Walk through Courthouse Towers, Park Avenue, and Balanced Rock, then head to the Windows Section to see Double Arch, Turret Arch, and the North and South Window formations. The Delicate Arch hike is on your list too, depending on how much time and parking you can find. You'll head back to Moab for lunch, then continue through the San Rafael Swell to Goblin Valley State Park to explore those strange, colorful rock formations. After passing Factory Butte and the Fremont River, you'll enter Capitol Reef National Park where you can check out Grand Wash Narrows, Hickman Bridge, or Panoramic Point before heading to Torrey for the night.

days.title: Capitol Reef to Bryce Canyon National Park
included: Morning hikes at Capitol Reef - optional Cohab Canyon, Cassidy Arch, Chimney Rock, or Sulphur Creek
View Gray Cliffs and Kaiparowits Plateau
Short hike to Mossy Cave at Bryce Canyon
days.description: Start your morning at Capitol Reef with optional hikes to Cohab Canyon, Cassidy Arch, Chimney Rock, or Sulphur Creek. Then you'll drive Highway 12, which ranks among the top scenic drives in the country, and it really lives up to that reputation. You'll pass through Grand Staircase-Escalante National Monument, traveling past Hoggs Back, the Calf Creek canyons, and Escalante Canyons. The route takes you over Gray Cliffs and past the Kaiparowits Plateau, where dinosaur fossils have been found over the years. By afternoon you'll reach Bryce Canyon and do a short hike to Mossy Cave before checking into Ruby's Inn, known for its western hospitality and charm.

days.title: Bryce Canyon to Las Vegas
included: Morning hiking at Bryce Amphitheater via Queen's Garden Trail or Peekaboo Loop (optional)
Leisurely walks between Sunrise Point and Sunset Point
Optional shuttle bus scenic viewing of different viewpoints
Visit East Section of Zion National Park
days.description: Catch the sunrise from Bryce Point early this morning. Then spend the morning hiking and looking around Bryce Canyon itself. You can take the Queen's Garden Trail through the Bryce Amphitheater if you want a moderate hike, or tackle the Peekaboo Loop for something more challenging. There are also shuttle bus options seasonally that stop at different viewpoints, and you can do leisurely walks between Sunrise Point and Sunset Point. After lunch, you'll start your return journey to Las Vegas, driving through Red Canyon and scenic Highway 89. The route passes through the East Section of Zion National Park where you'll see unique sandstone monoliths and towers before arriving back in Las Vegas by evening.

Join our small group tour of Tasmania to explore Cradle Mountain National Park, the Bay of Fires, Wineglass Bay, the wild West Coast, and the Tasman Peninsula. We’ll also guide you on several of Tasmania’s Great Short Walks throughout the journey around the island.  

Starts: Hobart 7.00am

Finishes: Hobart 5.30pm

days.title: Hobart to Strahan
included: Walk among eucalyptus trees at Mount Field National Park
Scenic drive through Lake St Clair
Scenic drive through Franklin-Gordon Wild Rivers National Park
Learn about Tasmania's mining history in Queenstown
days.start_point: 9 Argyle Street, Hobart Tasmania 7000, Australia (YHA Hobart Central , 07:00 - 07:15)
days.description: Your Tasmania adventure kicks off as you leave Hobart and head into the wilderness. Walk through Mount Field National Park where you'll see some of the tallest eucalyptus trees around, plus Russell Falls with its cascading water. The route takes you past Lake St Clair, one of Australia's deepest freshwater lakes, and through Franklin-Gordon Wild Rivers National Park. You'll stop in Queenstown to learn about Tasmania's mining heritage, then settle into Strahan, a small harbourside village where you'll spend two nights.
cities: Franklin Gordon Wild Rivers National Park

days.title: Strahan
included: Guided walk through temperate rainforest and Henty Sand Dunes
optional: Gordon River Cruise - glides through Macquarie Harbour, visits historic Sarah Island, enters World Heritage-listed wilderness
days.description: Your West Coast options give you flexibility today. If you're up for activity, there's a guided walk through temperate rainforest and across the windswept Henty Sand Dunes. Or you can do the Gordon River Cruise (costs extra) which takes you through Macquarie Harbour, past historic Sarah Island, and into World Heritage wilderness where ancient Huon pines line the water. Later in the afternoon, head to Ocean Beach, Tasmania's longest sandy stretch, and enjoy some of the cleanest air you'll find anywhere.

days.title: Strahan to Cradle Mountain to Launceston
included: Explore Cradle Mountain National Park alpine and glacial-carved wilderness
Wildlife viewing - wombats, echidnas, and Tasmanian wildlife
Choice of guided walks: Marion's Lookout summit track, Dove Lake circuit, or Boatshed stroll
Drive through Sheffield - Town of Murals
days.description: Cradle Mountain National Park is the focus today, and it's one of Tasmania's real highlights. The alpine and glacial-carved wilderness is where you'll look for wombats, echidnas, and other local wildlife. You can choose different walks like heading to Marion's Lookout summit, doing the Dove Lake circuit, or strolling to the Boatshed. After time in the park, you'll drive through Sheffield, known locally as the Town of Murals because of its colorful street art, then arrive in Launceston in northern Tasmania.
cities: Cradle Mountain-Lake St Clair National Park

days.title: Launceston to St Helens
included: Learn about spiritual connection of Bay of Fires to Tasmanian Aboriginal people
Walk along Bay of Fires white sands with turquoise waters and orange boulders
days.description: Start your day in Launceston by checking out Cataract Gorge along the South Esk River, which sits just minutes from the city center and is where you'll likely spot wallabies. From there, head toward the East Coast and stop for lunch in St Helens, a fishing town. You'll visit the Bay of Fires (Larapuna) to understand its spiritual importance to Tasmanian Aboriginal people. Walk along white sands with turquoise water and those striking orange boulders, then settle into your beachside accommodation.

days.title: Freycinet National Park to Hobart
included: Explore Freycinet National Park beaches and coastal forests
Hike to Wineglass Bay lookout or beach walk
Optional climb to Mt Amos summit or relaxing coastal walk
Visit Cape Tourville lighthouse with Tasman Sea ocean views
days.description: Freycinet National Park on the East Coast is your highlight today, with beautiful beaches, coastal forests, and pink granite mountains. You've got choices on how to spend your time here. Hike to the Wineglass Bay lookout, keep going down to the beach for a shoreline walk, tackle the tougher climb up Mt Amos, or take a relaxing coastal stroll. You'll also visit Cape Tourville's lighthouse for wild ocean views across the Tasman Sea before heading back to Hobart along the Great Eastern Drive.

days.title: Hobart
included: Visit Bonorong Wildlife Sanctuary - meet Tasmanian devils, quolls, wombats, kangaroos, and birds
Drive through Coal River Valley wine region
Explore Mount Wellington (Kunanyi) and Wellington Park
Walk through fern glades, eucalyptus forests, and dramatic rock formations at Wellington Park
days.description: Bonorong wildlife sanctuary is where you'll meet quolls, birds, wombats, kangaroos, and Tasmanian devils. From there, you can wander through Richmond, a heritage village worth exploring at your own pace. On the way back to Hobart, drive through Coal River Valley's winery region. Then head up Mount Wellington (Kunanyi), the city's outdoor space with fern glades, eucalyptus forests, dramatic rock columns, and boulder fields. There are excellent walking tracks up here leading to lookouts with great views. Later, relax in one of Hobart's historic pubs or restaurants.

days.title: Tasman Peninsula
included: Explore Port Arthur Historic Site - Australia's best-preserved convict settlement
Learn about Tasmania's convict history at Port Arthur
Walk to Remarkable Cave and experience Crescent Bay sand dunes
Visit Tasman Arch in Tasman National Park - highest sea cliffs in Australia
days.description: The Tasman Peninsula shows you rugged coastal scenery and convict history. Port Arthur Historic Site is Australia's best-preserved convict settlement and a UNESCO World Heritage location, where you can explore the grounds and see what remains of the structures from Tasmania's harsh convict past. At Remarkable Cave, there's one of Tasmania's better short walks to the impressive coastal sand dunes of Crescent Bay. Stop at Tasman Arch in Tasman National Park to see Australia's highest sea cliffs and feel the Southern Ocean's power. You'll head back to Hobart in the afternoon as your tour wraps up.

reviews.body: This tour is not for 40+ (not physically fit) whom want some reasonable relaxation luxury for their holidays. These...
reviews.reply:
Dear Mr Tang,

We’re sorry to learn that you were disappointed in our tour. We do try our best to ensure that guests have an enjoyable time, even if the tour was not the right fit for them. We wish to respond to your comments with the opportunity to explain the tour from our point of view, so that future potential customers can make informed choices about whether our tour is right for them.

Fitness/Activity Level – This active, nature based tour is designed for guests with moderate fitness and good mobility, as outlined on our website and through online agents including this platform. As noted in our itineraries, there are walks each day and, while participation is optional, being comfortable with walks ranging from around 20 minutes to 3 hours will help guests make the most of the national parks and attractions included in the tour. For this reason, our Original Style Tours are best suited to travellers who enjoy an active holiday.

Meals – Lunches on tour are generally more informal and suited to the day’s travel schedule. We usually suggest purchasing lunch earlier in the day so it can be enjoyed while visiting parks and attractions. Dinner arrangements are flexible and entirely up to each guest. While some travellers appreciate the convenience of dining at their accommodation, you are very welcome to dine out if you prefer. Some locations offer more restaurant choices than others, though it is certainly possible to arrange dinner at a restaurant each evening if that is your preference.

Vehicle – Your tour travelled in a Rosa vehicle, which has 24 guest seats. We are not familiar with the Mitsubishi Neo vehicle you mentioned, so we are unable to comment on that specifically.

Value – Our Original Tours are designed for budget to mid-range travellers and are often regarded as offering good value for money. That said, we are sorry to hear that the tour did not meet your expectations. We have never presented these tours as a luxury product. We also offer Comfort Tours, which include motel and hotel accommodation and are popular with older active travellers, although they are not positioned as luxury tours either.

Ultimately, we never like to disappoint people even if the tour was clearly not the right style for them, and we're sorry that you felt disappointed in us. Hopefully, Tasmania as a destination has left a wonderful impression on you, and you may visit another time in the future.

Kind regards,
Under Down Under
