intro:
Embark on an Exclusive 8-Day Sri Lankan Adventure!


This carefully curated 8-day tour offers a perfect blend of history, culture, nature, and relaxation. Discover the captivating allure of Sri Lanka as you explore its vibrant cities, pristine beaches, lush landscapes, and fascinating wildlife.


You’ll be welcomed with the renowned warmth of Sri Lankan hospitality, staying in charming hotels and resorts that make you feel right at home. Known as a comprehensive travel destination, Sri Lanka offers something for every traveller: golden beaches, misty mountains, ancient historical landmarks, abundant wildlife, and a rich cultural tapestry.


Guiding you on this journey will be a multilingual tour leader with deep knowledge of Sri Lanka’s history, traditions, and hidden gems. Their insights will bring each destination to life, ensuring you uncover the stories and beauty behind this extraordinary country.


Sri Lanka is also an economy-friendly destination, where you can enjoy world-class experiences without the hefty price tag. With its perfect mix of affordability and quality, this tour promises unforgettable memories and a holiday that exceeds expectations.


Prepare to be enchanted by the magic of Sri Lanka a destination that will leave you with incredible stories and cherished moments for a lifetime.

days.title: Colombo to Sigiriya
days.start_point: Colombo, Sri Lanka (Colombo, CMB Airport, 06:00 - 23:00)
days.description: Start the day with a tuk tuk ride to get a feel for local culture, then take a catamaran across a calm lake to a farmer's home. You'll watch how to make traditional Sri Lankan curry and eat lunch right there in the countryside. In the afternoon, head to Sigiriya Lion Rock Fortress, a UNESCO site. The climb takes some effort but you'll reach the top just as the sun starts to set, giving you incredible views over the ancient fortress that King Kasyapa built centuries ago.

days.title: Sigiriya
included: Cultural Village Tour including Tuk Tuk ride and catamaran boat ride
Traditional Sri Lankan curry cooking demonstration at local farmer's home
Authentic countryside meal at farmer's house
Sigiriya Lion Rock Fortress visit with sunset viewing
days.meals: Breakfast, Lunch (Authentic countryside food at local farmer's house), Dinner
days.description: After eating breakfast, travel toward Kandy, the historic mountain capital. First stop is the Royal Cave Temple and Golden Buddha in Dambulla, which sits 160 meters up on a rock and is also UNESCO listed. You'll walk through five separate cave temples decorated with historical paintings and sculptures. Later, once you reach Kandy, visit the Temple of the Tooth Relic, one of Buddhism's most important pilgrimage sites. By evening, catch a cultural dance performance that shows off Sri Lankan traditions and arts.

days.title: Dambulla to Kandy
included: Royal Cave Temple and Golden Buddha Statue visit in Dambulla
Temple of the Tooth Relic visit in Kandy
days.description: Today you're heading through tea plantations and waterfalls toward Nuwara Eliya, a hill town that feels like colonial England. Begin with the Gem Museum to see Sri Lanka's gem heritage. Then head to Peradeniya Royal Botanical Gardens, one of Asia's finest, full of rare plants and wide open spaces. As you climb into the misty hills, stop at an actual tea plantation and factory to see how Ceylon tea gets made and taste some fresh brewed. In the evening, walk around Nuwara Eliya's colonial center, check out Victoria Park, and browse the local fruit and vegetable market.

days.title: Kandy to Nuwara Eliya
included: Tea Plantation and Factory visit with Ceylon tea tasting
days.description: Board a train from Nanu-Oya Station heading to Ella Village. This train route cuts through the hill country with wonderful views along the way. When you arrive, explore Ella and see the iconic Nine Arch Bridge and Ravana Waterfall surrounded by green hills. After checking out Ella, continue to Yala National Park, which is Sri Lanka's largest wildlife area with different ecosystems and plenty of animals to spot.

days.title: Nuwara Eliya to Ella to Yala
included: Train journey from Nanu-Oya Station to Ella Village
days.description: Wake up early for a wildlife safari at Yala in a 4x4 jeep. You'll be looking for leopards, crocodiles, wild elephants, and other animals throughout the park. After finishing the safari, head down to the southern beaches and stop at Coconut Tree Hill in Mirissa for coastal views and photos. From there, go to the historic city of Galle and walk through Galle Fort, exploring its cobblestone streets and Dutch and British colonial buildings. Climb up to the Galle Lighthouse for sweeping views over the coast.

days.title: Yala to Galle
included: Wildlife safari at Yala National Park in 4x4 jeep
Coconut Tree Hill visit in Mirissa
Galle Fort exploration and Galle Lighthouse visit
days.description: This is your beach day. Hang out on the sand, order drinks under the coconut palms, and just take time to relax. If you want to do something, there are options like a boat ride through mangrove areas on the Madu River with fish therapy, visiting a turtle hatchery, or trying water activities such as diving, snorkeling, surfing, or fishing. The choice is completely up to you.

days.title: Galle - Beach Leisure Day
optional: Madu River boat ride through mangroves
days.description: Have breakfast and then travel to Colombo, the capital with history going back centuries. Visit the Red Mosque, Gangaramaya Temple which blends traditional and modern styles, Independence Square commemorating Sri Lanka's freedom, and Galle Face Green by the water. Wrap up with a meal at one of Colombo's known restaurants, then head to the airport for your flight home or get dropped off at a hotel in Colombo or Negombo.

days.title: Galle to Colombo
days.description: You'll be picked up at Colombo's Bandaranaike International Airport and driven to Sigiriya. Check into your hotel in Dambulla and take the rest of the day to settle in. The area around Dambulla is peaceful and worth exploring if you feel like wandering around, but there's no pressure to do anything specific. Just relax and get acclimated to the region.

attributes.tip: Join a group and forge lifelong friendships

intro:
This splendorous exclusive tour has been designed with a fine balance of history and culture, nature and wildlife, city and beach time. You will experience all the best adventures, wildlife, and social-cultural of the country while enjoying the warm Sri Lankan hospitality in cozy hotels and resorts. Sri Lanka is mostly a Buddhist country and it is very welcoming and safe for women traveling alone as well. Sri Lanka is famous as a comprehensive travel destination since it includes all the elements that you need as a traveler like beaches, mountains, historical sites, wildlife, and rich culture. Your tour leader, who has extensive knowledge of all aspects of this incredible country, will show you many fascinating and interesting places and he will share his knowledge about Sri Lankan history and culture. You will have the opportunity to experience exciting outdoor activities like jungle trekking, hiking, river rafting and safaris and also to explore remote areas with unique landscapes that you will remember forever. Sri Lanka is an economy friendly holiday destination; it’s a place where you can have world-class experiences without world-class costs.

TOUR HIGHLIGHTS:

  • While having an unique travel experience you'll get first-hand local knowledge, with on-the-ground expert’s guidance and the freedom and privacy to explore at your will.
  • Enjoy 4x4 jeep safaris through stunning National parks, home of Asian wild elephant families. Watching a hunting leopard is an unforgettable experience.
  • Explore the UNESCO World Heritage splendors, including Sigiriya Lion Rock fortress and the Temple of the Sacred Tooth in Kandy.
  • Spend some time on the Southern Beach, where you can either get active with sea adventures or chill out with a cocktail while laying under a palm tree.

days.title: Negombo
days.start_point: Colombo, Sri Lanka (Colombo CMB airport , 06:00 - 23:30)
days.description: Your flight lands at Bandaranaike International Airport in Colombo, then it's a transfer to your beachside hotel in Negombo. This first day has no scheduled activities, so you'll have time to get settled and relax. The afternoon is yours to spend lounging by the pool or on the beach, and you can take a quiet walk along the shore when the sun starts to set.

days.title: Negombo to Dambulla - Sigiriya
included: Cultural village tour with tuk-tuk ride
Catamaran boat ride across scenic lake
Live cooking demonstration for Sri Lankan curry
days.meals: Breakfast, Lunch (Homemade meal featuring authentic countryside flavors at a local farmer's house), Dinner
days.description: After breakfast, you'll drive through the countryside toward Dambulla and the Cultural Triangle. First stop is Kurunegala View Point where you can walk around Kurunegala Lake and take in the views. Once in Dambulla, you'll experience a cultural village tour with a tuk-tuk ride, catamaran boat ride, and a cooking demo where you'll learn to make authentic Sri Lankan curry at a local farmer's home. Later in the afternoon, you'll head to Sigiriya Lion Rock Fortress, a UNESCO World Heritage Site built by King Kasyapa. The climb happens in late afternoon light, which is ideal for photography.

days.title: Sigiriya
included: Bicycle tour of Polonnaruwa ancient city
4x4 jeep safari at Minneriya or Kaudulla National Park
days.description: There's an optional sunrise hike to Pidurangala Rock if you want to wake early and see the jungle and Sigiriya in morning light. After breakfast, you'll explore Polonnaruwa, the second ancient capital from 1070 AD, by bicycle. You'll pedal past grand ruins, temples, statues, and reservoirs across this UNESCO World Heritage Site. In the afternoon, a 4x4 jeep safari at Minneriya or Kaudulla National Park gives you a chance to spot large elephant herds and other wildlife. Evening returns you to the resort where you can relax, and an Ayurvedic herbal massage is available if you want one.

days.title: Sigiriya to Kandy
included: Dambulla Cave Temple and Golden Buddha Statue visit
Temple of the Tooth Relic visit
optional: Enjoy panoramic views from local viewpoint
days.description: After breakfast, you'll head toward Kandy, the cultural capital on a scenic plateau surrounded by mountains. On the way, you'll stop at Dambulla Cave Temple with the Golden Buddha Statue, a UNESCO World Heritage Site 160 meters above the plains featuring five cave temples with impressive statues and colorful frescoes. Once in Kandy, you'll visit the Temple of the Tooth Relic, one of Buddhism's most important pilgrimage sites and another UNESCO World Heritage Site. You'll have free time to explore Kandy's city center and Kandy Lake, then watch a traditional Kandyan cultural dance performance with vibrant costumes and rhythmic drumming.

days.title: Kandy to Kitulgala
included: White water rafting on Kelani River
Jungle hike to natural rock pool
days.description: You'll head to Kitulgala, a green rainforest area and eco-adventure destination in Sri Lanka. Upon arrival, you're preparing for white water rafting on the Kelani River surrounded by tropical forest and scenic hills. The rafting works for anyone aged 10 and older with full safety measures. After that, a short jungle hike takes you to a hidden natural rock pool where you can slide down a 5-meter waterfall into clear water, acting as a natural waterslide. Safety gear and guidance come with this. Later, you'll head back to your Kandy hotel.

days.title: Kandy to Nuwara Eliya
included: Guided visit to local Gem Museum
Tour through Nuwara Eliya local markets
days.description: After breakfast, you'll travel through lush tea plantations and waterfalls toward Nuwara Eliya, the hill country retreat known as 'Little England' for its colonial heritage. You'll visit a local Gem Museum to learn about Sri Lanka's famous gems and jewelry-making. Next comes Peradeniya Royal Garden, one of Asia's best botanical gardens. Then you'll visit a working tea plantation and factory to see how Ceylon tea is produced, learning about plucking, drying, and grading before enjoying fresh brewed tea. The afternoon lets you explore Nuwara Eliya's city center on foot, seeing the red-brick Post Office, historic Grand Hotel, Victoria Park, colonial architecture, and local markets.

days.title: Nuwara Eliya to Haputale
included: Train journey from Nanu Oya to Haputale
days.description: This is one of the trip's highlights: a train ride through Sri Lanka's highlands from Nanu Oya to Haputale. As the train moves through misty mountains, green tea plantations, and quiet rural villages, you'll have plenty of chances for photos and to take in the views. Train tickets are available at the station depending on what class is open. When you arrive in Haputale, you'll visit Adisham Bungalow, a historic colonial country house with peaceful surroundings, beautiful gardens, and panoramic hill country views. After checking in, the rest of the day is yours to relax.

days.title: Haputale to Ella
days.description: You'll arrive in Ella, one of Sri Lanka's most charming hill-country destinations. The day is for a relaxing walk through this laid-back village, taking in the peaceful atmosphere surrounded by misty mountains, lush forests, rolling tea plantations, and great viewpoints. You'll have the rest of the day to explore on your own pace or just enjoy the tranquil surroundings.

days.title: Ella to Yala
included: 4x4 jeep safari through Yala National Park
days.description: After breakfast, you're heading to Yala, traveling through Sri Lanka's varied landscapes toward the island's wildlife region. Upon arrival, you'll prepare for a 4x4 jeep safari through Yala National Park. The vast park, split into two zones by a river, is home to elusive leopards, sloth bears, crocodiles, wild elephants, and hundreds of bird species. You'll watch the sun set over the jungle while spotting baby elephants playing by the water, crocodiles on riverbanks, and hearing the jungle come alive.

days.title: Yala to South Coast
included: Fish therapy experience at local fish farm
optional: Visit Coconut Tree Hill in Mirissa
days.description: After breakfast, you'll travel along Sri Lanka's scenic southern coastline where history, culture, and natural beauty mix together. First stop is Coconut Tree Hill in Mirissa, an Instagram spot with rows of palms overlooking turquoise ocean. Next, you'll stop in Matara to see the iconic stilt fishermen, a centuries-old fishing tradition unique to this coast. You'll walk through historic Galle Fort, built first by the Portuguese and later strengthened by the Dutch, with cobblestone streets, colonial buildings, boutique cafes, and art galleries. A boat safari along the Madu River takes you through mangrove forests and islands, visiting a fish farm to try fish therapy. You'll also visit a Turtle Hatchery Centre caring for injured sea turtles and releasing baby turtles to the ocean. Evening brings you to Bentota where you'll check in to your beachside hotel.

days.title: South Coast
days.description: Today is a leisure day at your beachside hotel. You can relax by the pool or on the beach, soaking up the sun and listening to the waves in peaceful surroundings. It's the perfect time to unwind and recharge. In the evening, you'll enjoy the sunset views and the calm atmosphere of the seaside.

days.title: South Coast to Colombo
days.description: After breakfast on your final day, you'll visit Colombo, the lively capital of Sri Lanka with a history dating back to the 5th century. It's been an important center for sea trade and today blends modern style with colonial charm, busy markets, and cultural sites. A sightseeing tour hits famous attractions including the Red Mosque, Gangaramaya Temple, Independence Memorial Hall, Galle Face Green, colonial buildings, and upscale shopping malls for last-minute souvenirs. In the evening, you'll dine at one of Colombo's top restaurants celebrating your journey with authentic Sri Lankan dishes or global cuisine.

intro:
Golden Triangle Tours are a classic introduction to India especially for the first time visitors on holidays in India. If you've never been to the subcontinent before, start here for it could not get any more better and enriching cultural experience than a golden triangle holiday package.

­ 

Golden Triangle Tours cover the 3 most prominent tourist destinations in the heartland of India i.e. Delhi, Agra and Jaipur. These tour packages offer one of the finest cultural experience in India along with visit to some of the finest monuments and UNESCO World Heritage Sites including the Taj Mahal in Agra.

­ 

Ranthambore Tiger reserve (National Park): A natural home to Royal Bengal Tiger. This park has been well maintained and preserved because Royal Bengal Tigers are now an endangered species and a special Project Tiger was started in 1973 for their conservation. Spotting a tiger here will give you goose-bumps as you experience a sudden adrenaline rush on seeing it.

Note : Zone 1-5 Closed from July - 30th September

days.title: Delhi
included: Airport welcome in traditional Indian way
days.start_point: Indira Gandhi International Airport, New Delhi, New Delhi, Delhi, India (We will arrange your pick up either from Indra Gandhi International Airport or your Pre booked accommodation.)
days.description: Your flight lands at Delhi airport where a representative greets you in traditional Indian style. A private car takes you to your hotel so you can settle in and rest after traveling.

days.title: Delhi
included: Guided tour of Old Delhi including Red Fort, Jama Masjid, and Rajghat
Rickshaw ride through Chandani Chowk market
Guided tour of New Delhi including Rashtrapati Bhawan, India Gate, and Laxmi Narayan Temple
days.description: The day covers both North and South Delhi on a combined city tour. You'll see the Red Fort and Jama Masjid that Emperor Shah Jahan built, visit Rajghat memorial honoring Mahatma Gandhi, and take a rickshaw through the busy Chandani Chowk silver market. After lunch, the afternoon includes New Delhi's Rashtrapati Bhawan, India Gate, and Laxmi Narayan Temple.

days.title: Delhi to Jaipur
included: 1 cultural dinner with live Rajasthani folk music and dance show
Exclusive shopping tours in local markets
optional: Visit famous markets of Jaipur for textiles, gems, carpets, and handicrafts
days.meals: Breakfast (Buffet breakfast at hotel restaurant), Dinner (1 cultural dinner at Jaipur with live Rajasthani folk music and dance show)
days.description: After breakfast you'll drive to Jaipur, known as the pink city. Once at your hotel and checked in, the evening is yours to wander the local markets for textiles, gems, carpets, and handicrafts. Later you'll sit down for a cultural dinner with live Rajasthani folk music and dance performances.

days.title: Jaipur
included: Excursion to Amber Fort with elephant ride to and from the top
Visit to Hawa Mahal (Palace of Winds)
Exclusive shopping tours in local markets
optional: Elephant enjoy tour in Jaipur (elephant feeding, painting, bathing)
days.description: Following breakfast, you'll head to Amber Fort just outside the city and ride an elephant up to the top and back down. The afternoon brings a guided tour of City Palace in central Jaipur, the Jantar Mantar observatory, and the iconic Hawa Mahal. The rest of your afternoon is free to shop at the famous markets for textiles, gems, carpets, and handicrafts.

days.title: Jaipur to Ranthambore
included: Afternoon jeep safari in Ranthambore National Park
days.meals: Breakfast (Buffet breakfast at hotel restaurant), Lunch, Dinner
days.description: You'll drive out in the morning toward Ranthambore and check into your hotel upon arrival. In the afternoon, an open jeep safari takes you into Ranthambore National Park, a tiger reserve surrounded by the Vindhya and Aravali hill ranges. This is one of the world's top spots for photographing tigers in their natural setting.

days.title: Ranthambore to Agra
included: Early morning jungle safari with naturalist in Ranthambore for tiger tracking and wildlife exploration (approximately three hours)
Battery van ride in Agra to reach near Taj Mahal
days.description: An early morning jungle drive lasts about three hours through dense forest by open-top canter or jeep with a naturalist guide tracking tigers and wildlife. You'll head back to the resort for breakfast and rest, with optional time at the pool or exploring the area. Later you'll check out and drive to Agra, home to the Taj Mahal and known for inlay work, carpets, gold thread embroidery, and leather shoes.

days.title: Agra
included: Exclusive shopping tours in local markets
optional: Kalakriti Mohabbat E Taj Show Agra
days.description: After breakfast you'll visit the Taj Mahal, one of the Seven Wonders of the World and an architectural masterpiece. Next comes Agra Fort, an impressive red sandstone structure built by Akbar in 1565 that features the Pearl Mosque, historic palaces, and viewing points overlooking the Taj Mahal. The tour also includes shopping at local emporiums for traditional Indian inlay work.

days.title: Agra to Delhi
days.description: You'll leave Agra in the morning and drive back to Delhi. A car takes you to the airport upon arrival so you can board your connecting flight and head to your next destination.

name: Morocco Tours 10 Days Tour From Casablanca

attributes.name: City & Culture
attributes.tip: Immerse yourself in rich history and local traditions

attributes.name: Group Tour
attributes.tip: Join a group and forge lifelong friendships

attributes.name: Fully Guided
attributes.tip: An experienced guide will be with you for the entire tour

intro:
Discover the wonders of Morocco on a 10-day journey starting from Casablanca, where you will explore imperial cities, golden deserts, and the Atlantic coast. Your adventure begins in Casablanca, heading to Rabat, then to the enchanting blue-washed town of Chefchaouen. From there, you will travel to Fes, where you’ll wander through its ancient alleys and bustling traditional markets.


Next, you’ll cross the breathtaking Atlas Mountains on your way to the vast Sahara Desert, where you’ll experience a magical camel trek and spend the night in a desert camp beneath a star-filled sky.


Continuing your journey, you’ll pass through the stunning Dades Valley and Ouarzazate, visiting the famous Ait Ben Haddou Kasbah before arriving in the vibrant city of Marrakech. Here, you will explore its historical landmarks, lively souks, and bustling atmosphere.


After Marrakech, you will head to Essaouira, a charming coastal city known for its relaxed vibe, picturesque beaches, and rich cultural heritage. Finally, you will return to Casablanca, carrying unforgettable memories of Morocco’s diverse landscapes and unique charm.

days.title: Casablanca
days.start_point: Casablanca, Casablanca-Settat, Morocco (Pick you up from the Airport Casablanca or Hotel)
days.description: You'll arrive at Mohammad V Airport in Casablanca and head to your hotel by transfer. After settling in, the rest of the day is yours to wander around the city and check out the Atlantic coast at whatever pace feels right before getting some rest.

days.title: Casablanca - Rabat - Chefchaouen
included: Explore Chefchaouen blue-painted streets and alleys
optional: Enjoy local food and culture in Chefchaouen
days.description: Start the morning at Hassan II Mosque in Casablanca, then head to Rabat where you'll see Bab Challah, the Mausoleum of Mohammed V, and the Oudaya Kasbah. After lunch, it's about a two-hour drive to Chefchaouen where you'll spend the afternoon walking through the blue-painted streets and exploring the alleyways of this mountain town.

days.title: Chefchaouen - Volubilis - Fes
included: Explore Chefchaouen blue-painted streets and alleys
optional: Shop in Chefchaouen shops and cafes
days.description: You have the morning in Chefchaouen to wander the blue streets at your own pace, check out artisan workshops, and see the 15th-century kasbah and Great Mosque. In the afternoon, drive to the Roman ruins at Volubilis (a UNESCO site with impressive mosaics and remains), then continue on to Fes where you'll stay in a traditional riad for the night.

days.title: Fes
included: Explore Medina through Blue Gate (Bab Boujloud)
Visit ancient fortress with panoramic views
days.description: A full day exploring Fes with a local guide. You'll start at the Royal Palace gate, then enter the medieval Medina through the Blue Gate. Walk through Medrasa Bouanania, visit Najjarine Fountain, see the Tanneries with their traditional leather dyeing, and visit the Quaraouin Mosque and University (the world's oldest operating university). After exploring the Mellah, head to an ancient fortress for views over the city before heading back to your riad.

days.title: Fes - Ifrane - Azrou - Midelt - Errachidia - Merzouga
included: Visit Cedar Forest and see Barbary macaques
optional: Feed Barbary macaques in Cedar Forest
days.description: After breakfast, drive south through Imouzzer to Ifrane (known as Morocco's 'Switzerland' with its cool climate), then visit the Cedar Forest to see Barbary macaques. Later you'll have time for lunch and rest in Midelt before continuing through mountain valleys toward Merzouga. From there, swap to camels and ride through sand dunes, stopping at a high point for sunset. The evening brings traditional Berber drum music and dinner under the stars at your desert camp.

days.title: Merzouga - Todra Gorges - Dades Valley
days.meals: Breakfast, Dinner (Dinner at hotel in Dades Valley)
days.description: Wake early to see the sunrise over the dunes and have breakfast before leaving. You'll visit Rissani (the ancient Tafilalet capital) and explore its souk, then head to Erfoud to see fossilized marble workshops. From there, drive through palm groves to the Todra Gorges with their towering red cliffs carved by the river. After lunch, continue to Dades Valley, passing the 'Monkey Fingers' rock formations and scenic viewpoints before checking into your hotel.

days.title: Dades Valley - Ouarzazate - Ait Benhaddou - Marrakech
days.description: Head to Kalaa Magouna to explore the Rose Valley (famous for its May Rose Festival with rose perfumes and oils). Drive through palm groves toward Ouarzazate and visit the movie studios where major films have been shot. Then see Ait Ben Haddou, a UNESCO kasbah with mud-brick architecture from films like Gladiator and Game of Thrones. Drive toward Marrakech through the Tizi-N-Tichka pass in the High Atlas, stop for lunch, and arrive at your hotel.

days.title: Marrakech
days.description: Breakfast at your riad, then a guided tour of Marrakech includes Majorelle Gardens, Koutoubia Mosque, Saadian Tombs, and Bahia Palace. After lunch near Djemaa el-Fna Square, wander the souks to browse handcrafted goods. The afternoon is free to explore on your own, revisit favorite spots, or find hidden corners before returning to your hotel for the evening.

days.title: Marrakech to Essaouira
days.description: Travel to Essaouira, a coastal town known as Africa's 'Wind City' (popular for windsurfing April through November). Walk through the fortified medina (a UNESCO site), browse art galleries and boutique shops, and stroll the historic port watching fishermen work and traditional boats being built. It's a nice mix of history, art, and seaside atmosphere where you'll spend the night enjoying the ocean breeze.

days.title: Essaouira to Casablanca
days.description: Your final day starts with breakfast at your riad. Depending on your flight time, you'll either transfer to the airport with enough time to spare, or head to Casablanca for extra leisure time in the city. If you're leaving from Marrakech, a transfer to Marrakech Airport will get you there with plenty of time before your departure.

We understand your disappointment about some sites being closed during your visit, and we apologize for not communicating the holiday schedule more clearly before your booking. Your feedback is valuable, and we will work to ensure future travelers are better informed about major national and religious holidays so they can make the best decision for their travel dates.
At the same time, we are delighted that you were able to experience this important cultural and religious celebration firsthand and that it became a memorable part of your journey.
We also appreciate your observations regarding the driving distances and visits to artisan workshops. These workshops are intended to provide insight into traditional Moroccan crafts and support local artisans, but we understand that some guests may prefer less shopping-oriented experiences. Your feedback will help us improve the balance of our tours in the future.
Thank you again for traveling with us and for sharing both the highlights and the areas where we can improve. We hope to have the pleasure of welcoming you back to Morocco one day.
Warm regards,
Hassan

name: Perth to Exmouth Explorer & Ningaloo Reef 7 Day Original Tour

attributes.name: Nature & Wildlife
attributes.tip: Explore untamed landscapes teeming with wildlife

attributes.name: Group Tour
attributes.tip: Join a group and forge lifelong friendships

attributes.name: Fully Guided
attributes.tip: An experienced guide will be with you for the entire tour

attributes.name: Medium Intensity
attributes.tip: Travelers should be comfortable with somewhat-demanding activities

intro:
Discover why Western Australia is a nature lovers’ paradise. Become an Exmouth Explorer and experience the many wonders of the World Heritage Listed Ningaloo Reef. As you journey through the idyllic West Coast you will experience a totally different side to Australia, a region many are yet to discover!


Start your adventure in the most remote capital city of Perth before heading north into the nature lovers’  paradise that is  Western Australia. Hike down to the banks of the Murchison River and peek through  Nature’s  Window into an ancient gorge.  For those seeking a unique view over the gorge, there’ll also be an opportunity to test your abseil skills  (at guest’s own expense).  A visit to the World Heritage Listed region of Shark  Bay will leave you in awe of the beauty of nature.  Here you can marvel at a beach made entirely of tiny shells, meet the world’s oldest living fossils, the Stromatolites, and witness dolphins playing just offshore at Monkey Mia.    


The region is not only home to around 2000 dolphins but also turtles, dugongs, kangaroos, and emus!  Be amazed by your visit to the World Heritage Listed Ningaloo Reef, known for its diverse marine life, manta rays, and whale shark visitors!  Stay overnight in Coral Bay, a town right by the beach which boasts coral so close to shore you can swim out to view it.  Or join a tour in search of whale sharks or manta rays.  Whether you choose to join a boat tour or simply relax on the beach, the pristine beaches and turquoise waters here will leave a truly lasting impression.      


We follow the road as far north as Exmouth Cape Range National Park, a place where rugged mountains flow almost down to  the sea.  Stand atop Vlamingh Head at the lighthouse for views over the reef and ranges.  In spring, you  may even spot the migrating humpback and whalesharks as they go by.  Complete your tour of the Cape with a visit to the snorkelling haven of Turquoise Bay. From  Exmouth, we make our way back down towards Perth stopping for many comfort breaks and seaside stops. Take this last opportunity for you to solidify new friendships and reflect on your adventure together.

­ 

HIGHLIGHTS:

  • Marvel at the stunning limestone formations of The Pinnacles in Nambung National Park – a true natural wonder.
  • Experience jaw-dropping views from Kalbarri National Park’s Skywalk, perched high above the dramatic Murchison Gorge.
  • Hike early in the morning to iconic Nature’s Window, then descend into the Z-Bend for breathtaking clifftop views of the gorge.
  • Visit the World Heritage-listed Shark Bay and enjoy an unforgettable wild dolphin encounter at Monkey Mia.
  • Stroll along Shell Beach, a unique shoreline made entirely of tiny white cockle shells, and witness the ancient Stromatolites, the oldest living fossils on Earth.
  • Dive into the world-renowned Ningaloo Reef at Coral Bay, where you can snorkel amidst vibrant marine life.
  • Seize the opportunity to swim with majestic Manta Rays, Whale Sharks, or Humpback Whales (seasonal, Mar-Oct).
  • Relax and rejuvenate in the pristine, clear waters of Turquoise Bay, an idyllic paradise.

days.title: Perth to Kalbarri
included: Guided tour of Pinnacles Desert in Nambung National Park
days.meals: Lunch (Lunch by the sea at Jurien Bay), Dinner
days.start_point: The Criterion Hotel, 560 Hay St, Perth, Western Australia 6000, Australia (Our central meeting point for this tour will be outside the front of the Criterion Hotel. , 07:15 - 07:25)
days.description: Your adventure kicks off with a guided tour through the Pinnacles Desert in Nambung National Park, where you'll see thousands of limestone pillars rising from golden sand. After that, you head to Jurien Bay for lunch right by the water. Then you'll drive up Indian Ocean Drive with great coastal views along the way. If weather cooperates, there's a stop at the Pink Lake near Geraldton, which shifts color depending on the light. You'll finish up in Kalbarri, settling into your seaside accommodation for the night.

days.title: Kalbarri to Monkey Mia
included: Sunrise photo opportunity at Nature's Window or Kalbarri Skywalk
Visit Z-Bend in Kalbarri National Park
Lunch by the River mouth in Kalbarri
days.meals: Breakfast, Lunch (Lunch by the River mouth in Kalbarri), Dinner
days.description: Start early to catch sunrise at either Nature's Window or the Kalbarri Skywalk, with time to get some good photos. The morning involves exploring The Murchison Gorge and Z-Bend in Kalbarri National Park, where water has carved through the sandstone over time. During spring, you might spot bright wildflowers scattered around. Grab lunch by the river mouth in Kalbarri, then make the drive toward Monkey Mia. There are comfort stops along the route, and you'll reach your beachside accommodation by evening.

days.title: Monkey Mia to Coral Bay
included: Meet the famous Monkey Mia Dolphins
Visit Eagle Bluff for cliff views overlooking Denham
optional: Chill-out time on the beach at Monkey Mia
days.description: You'll get to meet the famous Monkey Mia dolphins and have time for photos. After that, it's your choice whether to relax on the beach or grab coffee at the restaurant. Next, head to Eagle Bluff for those cliff views overlooking Denham, then take a walk along a beach that's made entirely of tiny shells, which is pretty unique. After lunch, you'll head to Coral Bay and check into your accommodation right on the famous Ningaloo Reef, so you're positioned perfectly for the next part of the trip.

days.title: Coral Bay
included: Free time to explore Ningaloo Reef
optional: Stroll on beach and shark nursery viewing
days.description: Most of today is yours to spend however you'd like around the Ningaloo Reef, Australia's largest fringe reef. You can join a boat tour if that interests you, or just spend time on the beaches. There's a shark nursery to check out, or you can snorkel right on the Ningaloo Reef just a few meters from shore. Later this evening, take the short drive up the peninsula to Exmouth and settle into your accommodation for the next two nights.

days.title: Exmouth - Cape Range National Park
included: Drive through Cape Range National Park
Visit Vlamingh Head Lighthouse at sunset
optional: Whaleshark swim tour (Mar-Sep, pre-booking required, at guests' own expense)
Humpback swim tour (Aug-Oct, pre-booking required, at guests' own expense)
days.description: You'll drive through Cape Range National Park, where rugged limestone ranges and deep canyons create a dramatic landscape. There are about 50 kilometers of pristine beaches to see throughout the area. You can relax on the beach or snorkel at Turquoise Bay. The tour wraps up in early afternoon so you have time for lunch. Then spend the rest of the day exploring Exmouth itself or relaxing by the pool at your accommodation. Near sunset, head to Vlamingh Head Lighthouse for views.

days.title: Exmouth to Geraldton
included: Visit Gwoonwardu Mia Culture Centre in Carnarvon
Lunch at Gwoonwardu Mia Culture Centre onsite cafe
optional: Dinner at The Murchison Tavern (at guests' own expense)
days.meals: Breakfast, Lunch (Lunch at the onsite cafe at Gwoonwardu Mia Culture Centre)
days.description: The day begins in Carnarvon, where you'll visit the Gwoonwardu Mia Culture Centre to learn about the five Aboriginal language groups of the Gascoyne Region. There's an onsite cafe where you'll have lunch. You'll stop for a photo opportunity overlooking the Murchison River, which offers nice views. Later, there's a refreshment stop at Billabong where you can grab coffee and ice cream. You'll arrive in Geraldton for your final overnight stay on this leg of the journey.

days.title: Geraldton to Perth
included: HMAS Sydney Memorial with views of Geraldton
days.description: Start at the HMAS Sydney Memorial with views out over Geraldton. Then take a walk along the 3 bay walk at Green Head, and from there, wander through the stromatolites at Lake Thetis, which are these ancient rock structures formed by microorganisms. Stop at the Lancelin Sand Dunes Lookout to see the vast sand dunes and surrounding landscape. After that, it's a relaxing ride back to Perth on the bus, with drop-offs starting around 6pm, so you'll have time to settle in at home.

name: Cycle the Dalmatian Coast

attributes.name: Bicycle
attributes.tip: Pedal through scenic landscapes on two wheels

attributes.name: Group Tour
attributes.tip: Join a group and forge lifelong friendships

attributes.name: Fully Guided
attributes.tip: An experienced guide will be with you for the entire tour

intro: Breeze through Croatia along the beautiful Dalmatian Coast on this eight-day guided cycling tour. Pedal your way from the Roman city of Split to the Medieval city of Dubrovnik, taking in ancient sites, medieval towns, and fishing villages as you island-hop through Hvar and Korcula- two of the Adriatic's most iconic islands. Heading along quiet coastal roads, past vineyards, olive groves and sandy beaches, you’ll also enjoy opportunities to immerse yourself in Balkan culture and traditional Dalmatian cuisine.

days.title: Kastel Kambelovac
optional: Visit medieval harbour town of Trogir
Visit Saint Lawrence Cathedral in Trogir
days.start_point: Biskupa Frane Franića 1, 21214, Kaštel Kambelovac, Croatia (Hotel Baletna Skola, Hotel Reception, 19:00)
days.description: You'll arrive in Kastel Kambelovac, a seaside town about 10km south of Split, and check into your seafront hotel overlooking the bay. Your tour leader will meet you at 7pm for a welcome meeting if your timing works out. The rest of the day is open for whatever you feel like doing. Walk through the medieval streets of nearby Trogir and check out Saint Lawrence Cathedral if you're interested in history, or just head to the beach at your hotel's restaurant and relax after traveling.

days.title: Split - Hvar Island - Jelsa
included: Bike ride loop around Marjan Hill
Guided tour of Split starting from waterfront
Ferry to Hvar Island (Stari Grad to Jelsa)
Afternoon cycle ride from Stari Grad to Jelsa through vineyards and olive groves
optional: Wine tasting at Caric winery in Vrboska village
days.description: After breakfast, you'll drive about 20 minutes to Split and cycle around Marjan Hill in a loop. Then a guided tour takes you through the historic centre, covering the Roman Palace of Diocletian, its cellars, Temple of Jupiter, and Split Cathedral. You'll get free time for lunch before heading to the port. From there, a two-hour ferry ride brings you to Hvar Island. Once you arrive in Stari Grad, you'll cycle through vineyards and olive groves to the harbour town of Jelsa, where you're staying for the next two nights.

days.title: Hvar Island
included: Bike ride to highest point of Hvar Island
Explore historic town of Hvar on foot
optional: Cycle back to Jelsa via alternative route through Malo Grablje and Veliko Grablje villages
days.description: This is a full day on Hvar with your bike. You'll start with a long climb to the island's highest point, passing through lavender fields and getting views across the whole area. The descent takes you through Brusje village down to the town of Hvar, where you'll grab lunch and have time to wander the old streets or swim. In the afternoon, you can drive back to Jelsa or cycle back via a different route through Malo Grablje and Veliko Grablje if you want more time on the bike.

days.title: Hvar to Korcula to Lumbarda
included: Explore historic streets of Korcula town on foot
Cycling along the coast to Racisce (approximately 12 kilometres)
Cycling back to Lumbarda via Korcula (approximately 31 kilometres total for the day with 380 metres ascent and descent)
optional: Sample local cuisine at a Dalmatian-style 'Konoba' restaurant in Korcula
Wine tasting at a local winery specializing in Grk wine (8 Euros)
days.description: You'll drive to Hvar first, then board a catamaran heading to Korcula, the historic island with roots in Venetian architecture. Spend the morning walking through the old town's narrow streets and taking in the harbor views. After lunch, you'll get on a bike for a roughly 31 kilometre coastal ride toward Racisce, stopping partway for coffee and a breather. The route loops back through Korcula and continues to Lumbarda where you'll stay for two nights. There's time to unwind on the sandy beaches in the late afternoon, and if wine interests you, there's an optional tasting of the local Grk variety, which only grows in this region.

days.title: Korcula Island
included: Full day cycling tour of Korcula
Cycle through vineyards and villages back to Lumbarda
optional: Ride in support vehicle for 16km climb to Cara
days.description: Full cycling day around rural Korcula. You'll climb 16 kilometres to Cara, one of the island's oldest towns, or ride in the support vehicle if that suits you better. After that, you descend to Zavalatica, a coastal village where you can swim and have lunch with incredible Adriatic views. On clear days you might see Italy's Monte Gargano across the water. The route continues through vineyards and past Pupnat village before cycling back to Lumbarda.

days.title: Korcula - Peljesac Peninsula - Dubrovnik
included: Cycle from Postup along coast through vineyards
days.description: After breakfast, you'll drive to Korcula harbour and cross to the Peljesac Peninsula. Starting from Postup, you'll cycle along the coast through Plavac Mali vineyards and reach the bay of Zuljana, which has good swimming. Then it's a drive to Dubrovnik with a lunch stop in Ston. You'll stay in Lapad Bay, a lively area with restaurants and a public beach, though Dubrovnik Old Town is just 20 minutes away by bus. There's an optional visit to Mount Srd and the Imperial Fort war museum if you're interested.

days.title: Cavtat to Konavle Valley to Dubrovnik
included: Scenic morning cycle ride from Cavtat through Konavle Valley (approximately 35 kilometres with 390 metres ascent)
Ride through olive groves with panoramic valley views
Drink break in village on the banks of the Ljuta River
Cycle back through Konavle Valley to Cavtat
Free afternoon to explore medieval old town of Dubrovnik
optional: Walk around the circumference of Dubrovnik city walls (15 Euros)
Cable car ride in Dubrovnik (15 Euros)
Visit monasteries and museums in Dubrovnik
days.description: Starting from Cavtat, you'll cycle through the morning on gradually climbing tarmac roads that open up to panoramic views across the Konavle Valley and olive groves. A drink stop happens in a village near the Ljuta River to cool off before heading back down through the valley. You'll arrive in Cavtat for lunch and have some time to eat. After that, you drive to Dubrovnik where the afternoon is free to roam. The medieval old town is compact and walkable, the city walls offer views out to the Adriatic, and there are monasteries and museums scattered throughout if you want to go deeper into local history and art.

days.title: Dubrovnik
days.description: The tour ends this morning, and you're free to leave whenever it suits your schedule. If your flight is later in the day, the hotel has luggage storage available.

name: Cycle Provence

attributes.name: Bicycle
attributes.tip: Pedal through scenic landscapes on two wheels

attributes.name: Group Tour
attributes.tip: Join a group and forge lifelong friendships

intro: Ride through the heart of Provence, indulging in France's rural charms and culinary delights. Our eight-day cycling trip traverses hilltop villages, sprawling vineyards and historic towns. Explore Roman relics, walk in the footsteps of Van Gogh and visit picturesque chateaux, all whilst cycling through some of the region's most photogenic landscapes.

days.title: Marseille to Avignon
optional: Arrive earlier and take shuttle bus to Vitrolles then train to Avignon
Self-arrange parking if driving to the trip start
days.start_point: Aéroport Marseille-Provence (MRS), Route de l'Aéroport, Marignane, Bouches-du-Rhône 13700, France (Arrivals, 11:30 - 12:00)
days.description: Your tour begins at Marseille Airport with a 4pm group transfer by taxi to Avignon. If you land earlier, the airport shuttle to Vitrolles and a train connection work well as an alternative. Once there, you'll get oriented with your tour leader and then walk around the medieval city, checking out the imposing ramparts, Papal Palaces, and the historic Pont d'Avignon.

days.title: Avignon
included: Circular cycle ride along the Rhone River
Return to Avignon via Via Rhona cycling trail
days.description: After four nights in Avignon, you'll cycle to Pernes-les-Fontaines on an easier riding day. Stop for lunch in L'Isle-sur-la-Sorgue, which has plenty of antique shops and good restaurants. Then continue on the Via Venaissia cycling route toward Pernes-les-Fontaines, a medieval village with a ruined castle, city walls, and a cycle museum dedicated to Paul de Vivie, who invented the two-speed derailleur. The ride comes to about 40 kilometres with roughly 220 metres of elevation gain.

days.title: Avignon to St Rémy-de-Provence
included: Pass Abbey of St Martin de Frigolet
Cycle back to Avignon through fruit orchards
optional: Visit St Paul de Massane (psychiatric hospital where Van Gogh stayed) - €5.00
landmarks: Abbey of St Martin de Frigolet
days.description: You have the day to yourself in Avignon. Spend time on your own schedule, or try an optional challenge ride. Options include touring the Papal Palaces or browsing art at the Calvet Museum and Lamber Collection, wandering through covered markets to see local vendors, or tackling a more demanding 68-kilometre bike route out to the impressive Pont du Gard aqueduct.

days.title: Avignon
optional: Challenging cycling route to Pont du Gard (68 kilometres/42 miles with 498 metres/1,634 feet ascent)
days.description: You can relax and explore Pernes-les-Fontaines at your own pace, or tackle an optional ride to Gordes, which earned the title of most beautiful village in France in 2024. The cycle takes you through a scenic canyon with climbing that opens into sweeping views over the Luberon barrier. Once there, walk the narrow lanes, see St Firmin's church, and climb up to the Renaissance château. On the return, there's a stop at Fontaine de Vaucluse. The ride covers 61 kilometres with 600 metres of ascent. If you prefer, transport to Gordes can be arranged for roughly 80 euros per vehicle.

days.title: Avignon to Pernes-les-Fontaines
days.description: On your final day, you'll cycle through Provencal villages and vineyards at the base of Mont Ventoux, heading toward Mormoiron and a vineyard. At Chateau Pesquie, you'll get a guided tour followed by wine tasting, then have a picnic lunch on the terrace with plane trees for shade. By early afternoon, cycle back to Pernes-les-Fontaines and catch any sights you missed. The tour wraps up with a traditional Provencal farewell dinner at your hotel. This last ride covers approximately 41 kilometres with 320 metres of ascent.

days.title: Pernes-les-Fontaines
optional: Challenging cycling route to Gordes (61 kilometres/37.9 miles with 600 metres/1,969 feet ascent)
Visit St Firmin's church in Gordes
Ice cream on the return journey
Alternative transport to Gordes - approximately €80 per vehicle
days.description: After leaving Avignon, you'll head south through Barbentane, passing the Abbey of St Martin de Frigolet along the way. You should roll into St Rémy-de-Provence around lunchtime, where there's time to check out the historic town with its pre-Roman shrine, Roman artifacts, and ties to Nostradamus and Vincent Van Gogh. Optional stops include the ancient Glanum ruins and St Paul de Massane where Van Gogh was treated. The route cycles back through fruit orchards to Avignon, covering approximately 58 kilometres with 260 metres of ascent.

days.title: Pernes-les-Fontaines
included: Cycle through Provencal villages and vineyards
Guided vineyard tour at Chateau Pesquie
Traditional Provencal farewell dinner at hotel
days.meals: Lunch (Picnic lunch on the château terrace in the shade of plane trees), Dinner (Traditional Provencal dinner at hotel)
days.description: You'll cycle across the Rhone River on a circular loop with a coffee break partway through. As you pedal toward Chateauneuf du Pape, the vineyards come into view, and you'll climb up into the village itself. From there, follow the scenic Via Rhona cycling trail back to Avignon. This ride covers about 45 kilometres with roughly 160 metres of elevation gain.

days.title: Pernes-les-Fontaines to Marseille
days.description: After breakfast, you'll head out from Pernes and drive to Marseille Airport. The journey takes about an hour and 15 minutes, and you should arrive around 9am with time to spare for your flight.

name: Jordan Discovery

attributes.name: Ancient Wonders
attributes.tip: Walk among ruins, temples, and timeless landmarks

attributes.name: Group Tour
attributes.tip: Join a group and forge lifelong friendships

attributes.name: Fully Guided
attributes.tip: An experienced guide will be with you for the entire tour

attributes.name: Medium Intensity
attributes.tip: Travelers should be comfortable with somewhat-demanding activities

intro: From the unreal beauty of rock-carved Petra to the lunar landscapes of Wadi Rum, Jordan is steeped in bucket-list gems. Journey through the ancient monuments of Amman and beyond, uncover the tombs and temples of the fabled rose-red city, and sleep on the dunes of the desert, all while getting a taste of Jordanian life, both today and long ago.

days.title: Amman
optional: Explore the bustling souks of downtown Amman
days.start_point: Amman, Jordan (Toledo Hotel, Hotel reception, 19:00)
days.description: You'll arrive in Amman, one of the world's oldest inhabited cities, and head to your hotel to get settled. If you're coming through Queen Alia International Airport, an airport transfer takes about 30 minutes and can be arranged for you. Since most flights come in late, your tour leader will meet you at the hotel the next morning for a welcome briefing to kick things off.

days.title: Amman - Jerash - Amman
included: Guided tour of ancient Jerash including colonnaded streets, hilltop temples, chariot-racing stadium, and ancient theatre
Visit to Amman Citadel (Jabal al-Qal'a) with panoramic city views
Visit to traditional café in downtown Amman
days.description: After breakfast and the welcome meeting, you'll head north to Jerash to see some of the best-preserved Roman ruins around. Walk through the colonnaded streets, check out the chariot-racing stadium, and try calling out in the ancient theatre to hear your voice echo back. Lunch comes next, then you'll return to Amman to climb up to the Citadel for views across the city. From there, wander through the downtown souk with all its spice vendors and activity, finishing off the afternoon at a traditional café.

days.title: Amman - Madaba - Mount Nebo - Kerak - Petra
included: Visit to Madaba to see Byzantine-era mosaics including the 6th-century map of Jerusalem and the Holy Land
Stop at Mount Nebo with views over the Dead Sea, Bethlehem, and Jerusalem
Exploration of Kerak Crusader fortress with its stone-vaulted halls and passageways
days.description: This is a long travel day heading south toward Petra. You'll stop in Madaba to see the famous 6th-century mosaic map of the Holy Land, then continue to Mount Nebo for views over the Dead Sea and the Holy Land beyond. After that, you'll explore the Kerak Crusader fortress before arriving in Petra. Your hotel is within walking distance of the visitor centre, so you can drop off your bags and stretch your legs.

days.title: Petra
included: Guided tour of Petra highlights including the Siq, the Treasury, tombs, and temples
optional: Petra by Night experience - candlelit Siq trail with Treasury illuminated under stars and Bedouin welcome speech
days.description: Spend the full day exploring Petra with a guide who'll take you through the main sights like the Treasury and the Siq canyon. Later in the afternoon, you'll have time on your own to wander around and see different sections at your own pace. Notice how the pink sandstone changes color as the sun moves across the sky throughout the day, creating a different look each hour.

days.title: Petra
included: Bedouin cookery demonstration and traditional Jordanian dinner at family-run restaurant
optional: Climb to the High Place of Sacrifice
days.meals: Dinner (Bedouin cookery demonstration with traditional Jordanian meal including sweet dessert)
days.description: Today is completely free to explore Petra however you like. You might climb to the High Place of Sacrifice for views over Wadi Araba and the Negev Desert, trek up to the Monastery which is Petra's largest monument, or take time to relax at a local hammam. This evening, gather for a Bedouin cookery demonstration at a family restaurant where the chef prepares traditional Jordanian food including a sweet dessert, then you'll all eat together.

days.title: Petra to Wadi Rum
included: 4WD adventure through Wadi Rum with guided history stops
Traditional Zarb dinner (BBQ cooked under desert sand) with vegetarian options available
Overnight stay in traditional Bedouin tent
optional: Upgrade to private tent (subject to availability)
days.meals: Dinner (Traditional Zarb (BBQ of chicken or goat meat with vegetarian options) served with mezze, cooked under desert sand)
days.description: You'll leave Petra and head into the desert dunes of Wadi Rum. After reaching the visitor centre by coach, you'll switch to 4WD vehicles for a three-hour drive through the desert with stops to learn about the region's history. Watch the sunset turn the dunes red and orange, then arrive at camp for Bedouin hospitality. Dinner is a traditional Zarb cooked under the sand (chicken or goat, with vegetarian options), and you'll sleep in traditional Bedouin tents with shared communal areas.

days.title: Wadi Rum to Aqaba
optional: Snorkelling trip on the Red Sea
days.description: Head to Aqaba on the Red Sea coast where you can relax and do water activities. Aqaba is a resort town where locals come to unwind. This afternoon try snorkeling around the preserved coral reefs, cool off in the rooftop pool, walk through the souk, or pick a restaurant or bar along the water.

days.title: Aqaba to Dead Sea to Amman
included: Swim and float in the Dead Sea
Mud application experience at the Dead Sea
Access to pool and bar facilities at Dead Sea
days.description: Early departure for the four-hour drive to the Dead Sea, the lowest point on earth. You'll float effortlessly in the salt-rich water (33% salt content), cover yourself in the famous mud, then relax by the pool or grab a drink at the bar before showering off. Later you'll drive back to Amman, arriving in the late afternoon with time to pick up last-minute souvenirs at the souk before a celebratory Jordanian wine toast at a downtown restaurant marking the end of your trip.

attributes.name: Hiking & Trekking
attributes.tip: Conquer epic trails and breathtaking landscapes

attributes.name: Group Tour
attributes.tip: Join a group and forge lifelong friendships

intro: Traverse the Picos de Europa on this week-long walking holiday. Explore the stunning national park, heading out on daily walks through the unspoilt and wild landscapes of the western, central and eastern massifs. Get a real taste for life in rural northern Spain, staying in the small village of Sotres, refuelling with homemade Asturian food and even meeting with the makers of the famous Cabrales blue cheese.

days.title: Bilbao to Sotres
included: Transfer from Bilbao Airport to Sotres
days.start_point: 33459 Santiago del Monte, Asturias, Spain (Asturias Airport, Arrivals Hall, 10:30)
days.description: You'll land at Bilbao Airport by 1pm, and your tour leader meets you in arrivals around 2pm. From there, the group heads to Sotres, a high mountain village tucked in Asturias. The drive takes you through some nice scenery before you reach Hotel Rural Casa Cipriano, a family-run place right in the village center where you'll stay all week. Once you settle in, there's time to check out the hotel's restaurant and bar, or grab a drink at the local shop. If you're tired from traveling, you can just rest and get ready for the week ahead.

days.title: Sotres - Eastern Massif Walk
included: Guided walk from Jito de Escarandi to Caseton de Andara Refuge and Valdediezma forest
Transfer to and from Jito de Escarandi
days.description: Take a short bus ride to La Caballar and walk down through Camba Forest, passing old shepherd's huts with views of the central massif. Continue to Tielve and visit Queseria Pena Main for a traditional Cabrales blue cheese tasting and tour of their storage caves. The walk back to the hotel follows the old traditional path.

days.title: Sotres - Naranjo de Bulnes Trek
included: Guided walk to Vega de Urriello Refuge at the base of Naranjo de Bulnes
Transfer to and from Invernales de Cabao and Pandebano
days.description: Drive to Invernales de Cabao and walk up switchbacks until you reach Pandebano, where the famous Naranjo de Bulnes mountain rises from the landscape. The path continues to the base of this iconic rust-coloured peak where there's a refuge. You'll have time to watch climbers scaling its sheer face before heading back.

days.title: Sotres - Cares Gorge Trek
included: Guided walk through Garganta del Cares gorge to Cain
Transfer to and from Puente Poncebos
days.description: Start with a short drive to Jito de Escarandi and hike down through Valdediezma beech forest following old shepherds' paths to Tresviso where you'll have lunch. From there you'll continue down to Urdon, then take the bus to Potes, a medieval town known for its bridges and position along the riverside.

days.title: Sotres - Tresviso to Potes
included: Guided walk through Valdediezma beech forest to Tresviso
days.description: Head to Santo Toribio de Liebana Monastery on your way to Fuente Dé, then take a cable car up 1,000 metres to reach rugged plateaux. Walk down through alpine meadows in the Aliva glacial valley, passing the abandoned Las Manforas mines where you'll stop for a picnic lunch before returning to Sotres.

days.title: Potes - Fuente De Cable Car and Aliva Valley Walk
included: Visit to Santo Toribio de Liebana Monastery
Guided walk down Aliva Valley to Sotres
days.meals: Breakfast, Lunch (Picnic lunch in Aliva Valley), Dinner
days.description: After driving down to Puente Poncebos, you'll walk through the Garganta del Cares, a dramatic gorge that drops over 1,000 metres. The path cuts into cliffs using tunnels and bridges as you traverse what's considered one of northern Spain's highlights. A bus takes you back to Sotres by evening.

days.title: Sotres - La Caballar to Tielve and Cabrales Cheese Tasting
included: Guided walk from La Caballar to Camba Forest
Visit to Queseria Pena Main Cabrales cheese production
days.description: This morning you'll start your first walk in the eastern massif of Picos. Transfer to Jito de Escarandi and trek toward Caseton de Andara Refuge, walking through the Valdediezma forest with views down to Majada Jazuca Valley and out toward the Cantabrian coast. By evening you're back at Sotres for the night.

included: Airport transfer from Sotres to Bilbao Airport
days.description: After breakfast you'll depart the mountains and drive to Bilbao Airport, aiming to arrive by 11:30am. This is where your tour ends.

qa.question: Approximately how many hours of walking per day and total for the tour?
qa.answer: This is listed as moderate. There are some significant ascent and descent on days like day 4 where we descent for approximatively 1150 metres/3773 feet. The paths are generally well pathed at times rocky. Fit hikers will find the walks a satisfying day out, while less-fit hikers will find them challenging but manageable. This trip is appropriate for seasoned and first-time hikers who enjoy walking, have good level of fitness and balance. It is not suitable for those with recurring hip or knee problems or those unstable on their feet. As the trip is centre based there is the option to decide to have a rest day during the week if you wish. Days 2-6 are approximately 5-6.5 hours of walking a day but broken with stops, etc.

attributes.name: Ancient Wonders
attributes.tip: Walk among ruins, temples, and timeless landmarks

attributes.name: Group Tour
attributes.tip: Join a group and forge lifelong friendships

intro: Experience the Scottish Highlands on a tour from Edinburgh, as you travel through iconic landscapes, explore the Isle of Skye, and uncover both natural wonders and historic landmarks. The journey takes you from the awe-inspiring peaks of Glen Coe to the serene west coast, with every new sight more breathtaking than the last. Along the way, you’ll enjoy Scotland’s top whisky, visit impressive castles and cross Glenfinnan Viaduct by train. From start to finish, every part of this trip reveals a little more of Scotland’s quintessential charm.

days.title: Edinburgh to Oban
included: See views of the Wallace Monument and Stirling Castle
Visit Killin village and its waterfall
days.start_point: 60 High Street, Edinburgh, EH1 1TB, United Kingdom (60 High Street, The Royal Mile, Edinburgh, EH1 1TB)
days.description: Leave Edinburgh early and head to the Kelpies, those striking horse sculptures that make for great photos. From there you'll travel north past Stirling to see the Wallace Monument towering over the landscape, then check out Stirling Castle itself. The route takes you through Callander before you really enter the Highlands proper. Stop in Killin to see the waterfall that the village is known for, then drive through Glen Coe, which offers some incredible scenery. You'll end up in the fishing town of Oban for your first night, settling in by evening.

days.title: Oban to Isle of Skye
included: Train journey on the West Highland Line
Ferry crossing to the Isle of Skye
optional: Trip on the World-famous Jacobite Steam Train (Reserve at time of booking; Summer itinerary, mid-April to mid-October)
days.description: Start early and head north toward Fort William. Once there, you'll board the West Highland Line train for a scenic journey. The route crosses the Glenfinnan Viaduct, that famous railway bridge from the Harry Potter films, and you get sweeping views of the Highlands and Loch Shiel throughout the ride. The train brings you to Mallaig, where you'll take a ferry across to the Isle of Skye. Drive to Portree after arriving and check into your accommodation for the night.

days.title: Isle of Skye to Inverness
optional: Armadale Castle and Gardens & Museum of the Isles (Pay locally; Summer itinerary, mid-April to mid-October)
days.description: Spend your day exploring the Isle of Skye, which has dramatic mountains, beautiful coastline, and plenty of local folklore and history woven throughout. Later you'll head back to the mainland and make your way to Eilean Donan Castle, which photographs really well from almost any angle. From there, wind through the Great Glen and visit Dundreggan Rewilding Centre to learn about Scotland's ancient Caledonian Forest and conservation efforts. Continue on to Inverness, where you'll stay for two nights.

days.title: Inverness
optional: Loch Ness Cruise (Pay locally; Summer itinerary, mid-April to mid-October)
days.description: This day includes an optional cruise on Loch Ness if you want to try your luck spotting 'Nessie.' Head north to Beauly next, a quiet town with the ruins of Beauly Priory, a 1230 site that was used in Outlander filming. After lunch, you'll visit Clava Cairns with its chambered cairns and standing stones, places that feel quite mysterious and ancient. Then walk through Culloden Battlefield, where the last battle on British soil took place and which also inspired scenes for Outlander. You'll stay another night in Inverness.

days.title: Inverness to Edinburgh
days.description: Leave Inverness and stop at the Highland Folk Museum to get a sense of how people lived in the Scottish Highlands centuries ago. Continue on to a local whisky distillery for a tour and to try some drams. For your last proper stop, you'll reach Dunkeld, a quaint village where you can walk around and explore the area along the River Tay and see the cathedral there. Then it's the drive back to Edinburgh, arriving in the evening to wrap up your trip.

attributes.name: City & Culture
attributes.tip: Immerse yourself in rich history and local traditions

attributes.name: Private Tour
attributes.tip: Travel exclusively with your friends and family

intro:
This trip is a classic of our country, it includes highlights of Patagonia and Iguazú, along with a visit to the city of Buenos Aires, where you can admire local life and tour its main neighborhoods.

You will have the opportunity to delve into the nature of every corner of our country. Will visit the famous Iguazú Falls taking a trip through the five senses inside the jungle; We will get to know Patagonia visiting the small town of Calafate, cradle of the Perito Moreno Glacier, having the possibility of being in contact with glacial ice and we will also visit the End of the World, to discover there the city  "Ushuaia" on the shores of the Beagle Channel, previous step to Antarctica.

During this trip you will share with other travelers during each excursion/tour mentioned in the description of the program.

days.title: Buenos Aires
days.start_point: Buenos Aires, Argentina (International Airport)
days.description: Your driver meets you at Buenos Aires airport and takes you to your hotel. Check-in happens at 2:00 PM, so you'll have the rest of the afternoon and evening to settle in. Wander around your hotel area or grab dinner nearby to get acclimated to the city.

days.title: Buenos Aires
included: Morning city tour of Buenos Aires including Obelisk, squares (Mayo, San Martín, Alvear), avenues (Corrientes, De Mayo, 9 de Julio), neighborhoods (La Boca, San Telmo, Palermo, Recoleta, Puerto Madero), parks (Lezama, Tres de Febrero), and football stadium
days.description: Start early for a guided tour through Buenos Aires. You'll see the Obelisk, walk through historic squares like Mayo and San Martín, and drive down famous avenues including 9 de Julio and Corrientes. The tour covers neighborhoods such as La Boca, San Telmo, Palermo, Recoleta, and Puerto Madero, plus stops at Lezama and Tres de Febrero parks. You'll also visit a football stadium and check out the commercial areas. Afternoon is yours to explore independently.

days.title: Buenos Aires to Iguassu Falls
included: Visit Iguassu Falls (Brazilian side) - Igua\u00e7u National Park with self-guided walkway circuit (1,200 meters)
days.description: Early morning pickup gets you to the domestic airport for your flight to Iguassu. After landing, transfer to your hotel and rest a bit. In the afternoon, head to Iguassu Falls on the Brazilian side. Walk the UNESCO-listed circuit (about 1,200 meters with 130 steps) through Iguaçu National Park to see over 200 waterfalls from different angles. You'll handle this section on your own with included transfers.

days.title: Iguassu Falls
included: Guided landscape observation walk through Iguassu Falls geological formations with three different routes and observation points
days.description: Early pickup for a guided nature walk through the Iguassu Falls area with National Park guides. You'll explore three different routes with observation points showing the geological formations of the falls. Wildlife around you includes birds, butterflies, mammals, and jungle plants. The pace stays relaxed so you can really take in the sounds, colors, smells, and views of the area.

days.title: Iguassu Falls to Ushuaia
days.description: After breakfast, transfer to the airport for your flight to Ushuaia (connecting through Buenos Aires or Cordoba). Once you arrive, transfer takes you to your hotel. The rest of the day is open, so settle in and rest from traveling.

days.title: Ushuaia
included: Tierra del Fuego National Park tour including Ensenada Bay, panoramic viewpoints, Acigami Glacier Lake, Lapataia Bay, and short Fuegian forest walk
optional: End of the World train ticket (approximately 60 minutes)
landmarks: End of the World Train Station
days.description: Morning pickup around 8:30 AM from your hotel takes you to Tierra del Fuego National Park. You can either take an optional 60-minute train ride through the park at End of the World station or take a short walk through the forest instead. Visit the last post office in America, then check out viewpoints like Acigami Glacier Lake and Lapataia Bay while looking for local wildlife and plants.

name: Bali Bucket List Boutique 10 Day Tour

attributes.name: Group Tour
attributes.tip: Join a group and forge lifelong friendships

attributes.name: Fully Guided
attributes.tip: An experienced guide will be with you for the entire tour

attributes.name: Medium Intensity
attributes.tip: Travelers should be comfortable with somewhat-demanding activities

intro:
Bali Bucket List would like to introduce its Boutique tour; for the intrepid traveler looking for action with all the styles of an exclusive vacation. The Boutique Tour is aimed at the 30+ traveler who wants to share all the adventures Bali has to offer but with a little more comfort than the original tour. The tour is perfectly suited to couples or friends looking to enjoy the finer things in life whilst absorbing the incredible culture that Bali has to offer. The tour is action-packed, offering money-can’t-buy experiences, all from the comfort of luxury resorts.

So if you are looking for the perfect honeymoon, holiday, or introduction to the finer hospitality Bali has to offer. Come and tick it off with us, in style.

days.title: Seminyak
days.description: You'll arrive in Bali and head straight to your hotel in Seminyak with a transfer arranged. The rest of the day is yours to settle in and shake off travel fatigue. Grab a beer by the pool, book a massage, wander through boutique shops, or just relax. By evening, head to the beach and catch the sunset before dinner.

days.title: Seminyak to Ubud
days.meals: Lunch (Lunch overlooking the Tegallalang rice terraces)
days.description: Travel to Ubud this morning and stop for lunch with views out over the Tegallalang rice terraces. After eating, you'll have a chance at the rope swings for photos, then walk down to Tegenungan waterfall where you can cool off in the water. Later, check out the local markets to pick up souvenirs and don't skip the haggling part of the experience.

days.title: Ubud
days.description: After breakfast, head to the Monkey Forest where you'll need to keep an eye on your things. In the afternoon, join a traditional Balinese cooking class with local chefs who'll teach you how to prepare a meal from scratch. You'll then eat what you've made as a group, which makes for a much better lunch than usual.

days.title: Ubud
included: Climb Mt Batur (optional early morning activity)
days.description: Early risers can hike Mount Batur and see the sunrise from the top with tea or coffee. If that's not your thing, sleep in and explore Ubud at your own pace. The hikers get back mid-morning so everyone can spend the rest of the day together doing whatever interests you.

days.title: Ubud to Gili Air
included: Island hopping to the Gili Islands
Fast ferry transfer to Gili Air
days.description: Leave Ubud behind and take a fast ferry to the Gili Islands, landing at your resort on Gili Air. Drop your bags, order a cocktail, and settle into the island vibe for the next few days.

days.title: Gili Air
included: Private boat tour of the 3 Gili Islands
days.description: A private boat takes you around all three Gili Islands with stops at the best snorkeling spots where you'll see turtles and tropical fish. You'll have lunch on the island, then rent a bicycle to pedal around and find that famous swing for photos. Stop by the beach for a fresh coconut and soak in the afternoon.

days.title: Gili Air to Nusa Lembongan
days.description: Spend the morning in Gili Air having a lazy brunch or another bike ride if you prefer. Around lunchtime, a boat will take you to Nusa Lembongan. You'll arrive in time to catch the sunset from Devil's Tear viewpoint, which is worth the trip on its own.

days.title: Nusa Lembongan
days.meals: Breakfast, Dinner (Dinner at a local restaurant serving western meals and classic Indonesian cuisine)
days.description: Start with snorkeling and Manta Rays right after breakfast. The rest of your day is flexible, and your guide can help set up optional activities like SUP, surf lessons, or a massage if you want them. Dinner happens after sunset at a restaurant that serves both western and Indonesian food, and your guide will help sort out travel plans if you're heading somewhere next.

days.title: Nusa Lembongan to Nusa Penida
days.description: Your last full day starts with a visit to the Mangroves, then a boat heads to Nusa Penida for photos at Kelingking Beach and Billabong Beach. After lunch, you'll relax at Crystal Bay before heading back to Nusa Lembongan for one final sunset with the group. End the evening with a group dinner and drinks while looking through the week's photos together.

days.title: Departure
days.description: Time to say goodbye to everyone and head your separate ways. You'll take one last group photo before departing, and then it's back to reality.
