name: Japan Adventure 13 Day

attributes.name: City & Culture
attributes.tip: Immerse yourself in rich history and local traditions

attributes.name: Group Tour
attributes.tip: Join a group and forge lifelong friendships

attributes.name: Fully Guided
attributes.tip: An experienced guide will be with you for the entire tour

intro:
From the neon lights of buzzing Tokyo to ancient temples on snowy mountain tops, Japan is a feast for the senses and INTRO is the most amazing way to experience it! You’ll walk the streets of one of the world’s busiest and most futuristic cities, watch monkeys bathe in hot springs, roll your own sushi, visit ancient shrines and castles, get taught to wield a sword by a Samurai master, stay overnight with monks in a 1000 year old Buddhist temple, experience incredible and unique accommodation and much more! With an awesome group leader from the moment you arrive at the hotel, an instant group of friends and help with all your onward travel. Get ready for the trip of a lifetime!

+ Our tours are all 100% Carbon Neutral!

days.title: Tokyo
days.description: You'll arrive in Tokyo and head straight to your hostel to check in. After settling in, take some time to shake off the flight and relax before connecting with the group later on.

days.title: Tokyo
included: Nightlife and Karaoke Bars in Shinjuku
days.description: Start at Senso-ji Temple, Tokyo's oldest Buddhist temple, then move on to Meiji Shrine. From there, you'll walk through the colorful streets of Harajuku and catch the crossing at Shibuya. By evening, head to Shinjuku to try some of Japan's quirky restaurants and tiny bars.

days.title: Tokyo
days.description: Begin the morning learning how to roll sushi from a sushi master. You'll have some free time to explore Tokyo on your own, then head to Akihabara, known for its arcades, maid cafes, photo booths, and game centers.

days.title: Tokyo to Nagano
days.description: Take the bullet train to Nagano (travels at around 200 mph). In the afternoon, learn origami from a local instructor. Later, relax in an onsen fed by volcanic springs, then settle into a traditional ryokan with tatami mats and futon bedding for the night.

days.title: Nagano
days.description: Learn to roll soba noodles this morning. Head into the mountains to see the region's famous snow monkeys in their natural habitat, either playing in trees or soaking in hot springs. After that, explore the lakes and forests of Shiga Kogen National Park.

days.title: Nagano to Hakone
days.description: Board the bullet train headed for Hakone, a town known throughout Japan for its views of Mount Fuji (weather permitting).

days.title: Hakone to Osaka
days.description: Spend the morning in Hakone traveling by pirate ship and cable car with views of Mount Fuji on clear days. Later, take the train to Osaka for BBQ dinner and a night out with karaoke.

days.title: Osaka
days.description: The morning is yours to relax or shop around Osaka. Visit Osaka Castle, built over 400 years ago, to learn about Japanese history and samurai warriors. Finish at Dotonbori, a canal region with some of the best food in the country.

days.title: Osaka to Koyasan
days.description: Head back to the mountains and stay overnight in a 1000-year-old Buddhist temple in Koyasan. The monks will teach you meditation and serve you their traditional cuisine. Later in the evening, take a walk through Japan's largest cemetery.

days.title: Koyasan to Kyoto
included: Night tour of Kyoto's Geisha district
days.description: Wake early to watch Buddhist monks perform their morning prayer service and fire ceremony. The monks will serve you traditional breakfast afterward. Then travel to Kyoto, Japan's ancient capital. Tonight, take a tour of Gion to learn about geishas.

days.title: Kyoto
days.description: Visit the Bamboo Forest of Arashiyama, great for photos with towering bamboo all around. Head to the Golden Pavilion next. The evening is free, so you might grab sushi, find a bar, or try bowling or arcade games with others in the group.

days.title: Kyoto
days.meals: Breakfast, Dinner (Last dinner and drinks to celebrate)
days.description: Walk through the winding trails of Fushimi-Inari, an iconic shrine with countless torii gates leading up the ancient mountain. In the afternoon, learn sword techniques from a samurai master. Tonight, have your final dinner and drinks to celebrate the trip.

days.title: Kyoto
days.description: Your 13-day journey ends today. Check out and head home, or decide to stay longer in Kyoto or continue exploring other parts of Japan on your own.

attributes.tip: Join a group and forge lifelong friendships

intro:
An unforgettable journey through culture, nature, and coastal bliss


Discover the heart and soul of Sri Lanka with our 14-Day All-in-One Classic Tour, a carefully crafted itinerary that brings together the island’s most iconic destinations, rich heritage, and stunning natural beauty. Perfect for first-time visitors or those seeking a well-rounded adventure, this tour offers the best of Sri Lanka in one seamless journey.

days.title: Negombo
optional: Visit Dutch Canal (Hamilton Canal) on foot or by boat
days.start_point: Colombo, Sri Lanka (Air port)
days.description: You'll arrive at Colombo International Airport where your guide meets you for the drive to Negombo, a fishing town that's conveniently close to the airport. Take some time to walk around the Dutch Canal, a historical waterway built during the colonial period that runs between the coast and Negombo Lagoon. It's a nice way to ease into your trip and get a feel for the area.

days.title: Anuradhapura
included: Visit UNESCO World Heritage Site of Anuradhapura
days.description: After breakfast you'll drive roughly 4 hours to Anuradhapura, one of Sri Lanka's ancient capitals and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The day involves walking through well-preserved ruins including dagobas, monastic buildings, and royal ponds that tell the story of this important Cultural Triangle location. Back at your hotel you can relax, and if you're interested, there's an option for an Ayurvedic herbal massage to ease any travel fatigue.

days.title: Upgrade Available
days.description: Following breakfast, you'll head to Polonnaruwa, Sri Lanka's second most ancient kingdom and another UNESCO World Heritage Site. You'll see the historic ruins, then stop at a local village to get a sense of how people live and what daily life is like there. In the afternoon you'll go on a safari at Minneriya National Park where you can see hundreds of elephants in their natural surroundings. Then it's back to your hotel in Sigiriya to settle in for the evening.

days.title: Sigiriya - Dambulla - Matale - Kandy
included: Visit to spice & herbs garden with foot massage
optional: Explore Sigiriya (Lion's Rock) including wall paintings, Mirror Wall, and summit climb
days.description: After breakfast you'll visit the Botanical Garden in Kandy, then head toward the tea region of Nuwara Eliya. On the way you'll stop at a Ramboda waterfall tea factory to see how tea is made and try freshly brewed varieties. Once in Nuwara Eliya, known as Little England, you'll notice the colonial-era architecture including the Queen's Cottage, Grand Hotel, Hill Club, and Town Post Office. The cool climate and quiet atmosphere here feel quite different from the rest of the island.

days.title: Kandy - Nuwara Eliya
included: Tea factory and tea field tour
optional: Explore Nuwara Eliya town and colonial landmarks
days.description: You'll take a scenic train from Nanu Oya to Ella in the afternoon, heading through tea plantations, misty mountains, and small villages along the way. This train route is popular for good reason. Your guide handles your luggage and meets you at Ella station. Once there you'll check out some waterfalls, the Nine Arch Bridge, and can hike up Little Adam's Peak for panoramic views. By evening you can head into Ella's town center where there are plenty of bars and restaurants to choose from.

days.title: Nuwara Eliya
optional: High Tea experience at Grand Hotel Nuwara Eliya
days.description: After breakfast you'll head to Horton Plains National Park to walk through the landscapes with misty grasslands and cloud forests. The big draw is World's End, one of Sri Lanka's most well-known viewpoints. Later, if you want to experience some colonial history firsthand, you can have High Tea at the Grand Hotel Nuwara Eliya, which gives you a chance to relax and soak in the atmosphere of this historic hotel.

days.title: Nuwara Eliya - Ella (via scenic train)
included: 2nd or 3rd class scenic train tickets to Ella (seat reservations subject to availability)
days.description: After breakfast you'll leave Ella for Yala and prepare for an evening safari at Yala National Park where you might spot leopards, bears, and different bird species. Following your safari you'll have a BBQ dinner in the peaceful surroundings. You'll stay the night at Tissa Lake View Hotel, which offers a romantic and charming atmosphere.

days.title: Ella - Yala National Park
optional: Explore Tissamaharama Ancient City and Temple
days.description: You'll have breakfast and then head to Mirissa, which is known for whale watching and has nice beaches. You'll spend two days here relaxing on the coastline, which has a laid-back vibe. There are plenty of beachfront restaurants and cafes nearby serving fresh seafood with ocean views.

days.title: Upgrade Available
days.description: After breakfast you'll travel to Bentota by way of Galle. Along the route you'll stop to see the stilt fishermen of Weligama performing their traditional fishing methods. In Galle you'll check out the Old Portuguese Fort, which was later rebuilt and expanded by the Dutch, and it's a well-preserved historical site. Once in Bentota you'll do a Madu River safari through lush mangroves with different wildlife, then relax on the beaches for two days, enjoying the calm coastal setting.

days.title: Bentota - Colombo Airport
optional: Colombo city tour en route to airport

reviews.reply:
Hi Emely Fehr's
Thank you for taking the time to share your feedback. We are genuinely sorry to hear that your experience did not meet your expectations.

We would, however, like to clarify a few points for future travelers.

Regarding the group tour, due to an unusually high number of cancellations caused by the conflict in the Middle East, you were the only traveler confirmed on your departure date. We informed you in advance because we believe in being transparent with our guests. We did **not** ask you to cancel your booking. Instead, we offered the option of upgrading to a private tour with a supplement, as operating a group tour for a single traveler is not financially sustainable. After you contacted TourRadar, we honored your original booking and provided you with a **private tour at no additional charge**, even though you had booked a small group tour. We did this to ensure your holiday could continue as planned.

Regarding the additional costs, these were **clearly stated before your booking and again before your arrival**. The tour description, quotation, and confirmation all specify that **entrance fees and activity fees are not included** in the tour price. The "What's Included" and "What's Not Included" sections clearly explain this. We also provided a detailed list of entrance fees in advance and offered you the option of prepaying them before arrival for your convenience. Therefore, these costs were never hidden or added unexpectedly during your trip.

We would also like to note that during your tour, you did not inform us of any concerns regarding your guide, hotels, or itinerary. Had you contacted our operations team while you were traveling, we would have done our very best to address any issues immediately and find suitable solutions. Receiving this feedback more than a month after the tour had concluded meant that we no longer had the opportunity to resolve your concerns during your holiday.

Similarly, the inclusions regarding accommodation and meals were exactly as advertised. The itinerary clearly states that the tour includes **3- and 4-star hotels, daily breakfast, and three dinners**. These services were provided exactly as described. Your tour price was approximately **€100 per day**, covering accommodation, breakfast, private transportation, and a dedicated driver-guide for **14 days**—despite the tour operating as a private tour instead of the shared group tour you had originally booked.

We also note your comments regarding your guide and accommodations. We appreciate this feedback and will review it internally with our operations team and hotel partners. Guest feedback is important to us, and we continuously work to improve our services.

We respect that every traveler has different expectations, but we also believe it is important that reviews accurately reflect what was booked and what was included. We are disappointed that several aspects of your review criticize items that were clearly disclosed before your trip and provided exactly as advertised.

We sincerely thank you for visiting Sri Lanka and wish you all the best in your future travels.

Nadeeka
Mango Vacations

intro: Embark on a whirlwind adventure through the heart of Jordan, where history, culture, and the warmth of its people come together to create an unforgettable journey. This short tour will immerse you in the soul of the land, making you feel like a part of its timeless story. Imagine stargazing under the endless skies of Wadi Rum, where the Milky Way stretches out in breathtaking clarity, and floating effortlessly in the serene waters of the Dead Sea, the lowest point on Earth. Whether you're discovering Jordan for the first time or seeking an authentic Middle Eastern experience, this journey promises memories that will last a lifetime. Don't just visit—become part of the magic.

days.title: Amman
days.start_point: مطار الملكة علياء الدولي, Queen Alia Airport Rd, ال جيزا, Amman, Jordan (QAI, 00:00 - 00:00)
days.description: You'll land at Queen Alia Airport and get transferred to Amman International Hotel to check in. After settling into your room, there's a welcome dinner at the hotel restaurant, so you can meet other travelers and get oriented before your first full day exploring the country.

days.title: Amman - Jerash - Petra
optional: Witness Roman chariot races and gladiator performances at Jerash (subject to schedule)
Attend Petra Night Show ($42 USD, available Monday, Wednesday, Thursday)
days.meals: Breakfast (Breakfast at Amman International Hotel at 8:00 AM), Dinner
days.description: Breakfast happens at the hotel, then you'll head to Amman Citadel to take in views across the whole city. From there, it's a scenic drive through Amman's neighborhoods before heading north to Jerash, where you'll walk through one of the world's best-preserved Roman cities with its massive colonnaded streets, temples, and theaters still standing. Later, you'll drive about 3 hours south to Petra and check in for the night. If you're up for it, there's an optional evening visit to Petra's Night Show, where the Treasury gets lit up by candlelight, which is really something special.

days.title: Petra - Wadi Rum
included: Guided tour of Petra including the Siq canyon
2-hour Sunset Jeep Tour in Wadi Rum
optional: Horseback riding through the Siq (alternative to walking)
days.meals: Breakfast (Breakfast at H Luxury Hotel at 7:00 AM), Lunch (Lunch at Al Qantara Restaurant in Petra), Dinner (Barbecue Dinner Party at Wadi Rum Oasis Luxury Camp)
days.description: After an early breakfast, you'll have a guide walk you through Petra from 6:30 AM until lunch time at 12:30 PM. You'll go through the Siq canyon and see the iconic Treasury, which was carved into red sandstone cliffs over 2,000 years ago. There's time for lunch at a local restaurant, and then you'll spend 2 hours on a sunset jeep tour through Wadi Rum desert with its colorful rock formations and otherworldly landscape. You'll finish the day at Wadi Rum Oasis Luxury Camp with dinner and an overnight stay out in the desert.

days.title: Wadi Rum - Madaba - Mount Nebo - Dead Sea - Amman
included: Explore Madaba and Greek Orthodox Church of St. George
landmarks: Greek Orthodox Church of St. George
days.meals: Breakfast (Breakfast at Wadi Rum Oasis Luxury Camp), Lunch (Lunch at Dead Sea resort with spectacular sea views), Dinner (Farewell dinner at Amman International Hotel)
days.description: The desert camp serves breakfast early, then it's a 4-hour drive to Mount Nebo where you can see across to the Jordan Valley, Jerusalem hills, and the Dead Sea stretching out below. Next stop is Madaba, where you'll check out the famous 6th-century mosaic map of the Holy Land inside the Greek Orthodox Church of St. George. Around 2 p.m., you head to the Dead Sea to float in the mineral-rich water, grab lunch with sea views, and try out natural mud treatments. Later you'll head back to Amman and have a farewell dinner at your hotel.

days.title: Amman - Departure
days.description: You'll have your final breakfast at Amman International Hotel, then get transferred to Queen Alia Airport for your departure flight, wrapping up your trip through Jordan.

attributes.name: Ancient Wonders

intro: Explore a seven day adventure, along the Nile River with our expertly guided tours in Egypt. Dive into the essence of marvels as you explore the landmarks, including the breathtaking Giza Pyramids, The Egyptian Museum and the city of Cairo immersing yourself in the diverse tapestry of Egyptian heritage. Embark on a cruise along the Nile from Aswan to Luxor enjoying views and discovering enchanting attractions, like the renowned Valley of the Kings the grand Karnak Temples, the peaceful Philae Temple and the impressive Abu Simbel Temple alongside many other historical gems waiting to be explored.

days.title: Arrival in Cairo
days.start_point: Cairo International Airport (CAI), Airport Rd, Al Shorouk, Al Qahirah 11, Egypt (Cairo International Airport ( CAI ), 01:00 - 23:55)
days.description: Landing at Cairo International Airport, your representative will be waiting to take you straight to your hotel for check-in. This gives you time to settle in and rest up before your activities begin.

days.title: Cairo
included: Visit to the Great Pyramids of Giza (Cheops, Chefren, Mykerinus)
days.description: This morning you'll head to the Great Pyramids of Giza to see the pyramids of Cheops, Chefren, and Mykerinus along with the Sphinx and Valley Temple. After that, the Grand Egyptian Museum is on your agenda where you can walk through 5,000 years of Ancient Egyptian history, including the Statue of King Ramses II and various pieces of royal regalia.

days.title: Cairo to Aswan
days.description: You'll fly to Aswan and then visit Philae Temple, which was built for the goddess Isis. Boarding your Nile cruise ship happens around lunch time, so you'll have your meal while the ship starts moving upriver. If interested, there's an optional visit to a Nubian Village where you can see colorful houses and camels. You'll spend the night on the cruise ship in Aswan.

days.title: Aswan to Edfu
included: Egyptian Night Party on Nile Cruise ship
optional: Early morning tour to Great Temples of Abu Simbel
days.meals: Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner (Egyptian Night Party with traditional music and entertainment)
days.description: An early morning optional tour takes you to Abu Simbel's temples, which Ramses II had built and then relocated in 1968. From there, sailing for about 5 hours brings you to Kom Ombo where a temple honoring both the falcon-headed god Horus and the Crocodile God Sobek waits. By evening, there's an Egyptian Night Party on the ship with traditional Galabeya gowns, 60's, 70's, and Arabian music. Overnight is in Edfu.

days.title: Edfu to Luxor
days.description: Starting with breakfast, you'll visit the Temple of Edfu, which is quite well-preserved and dates to the Greco-Roman era, honoring Horus. Then the ship continues to Luxor where you can see the temples of Luxor and Karnak, both dedicated to the god Amun Ra, plus the recently opened path of sphinxes. There are temple shows at night if you want to catch one. You'll stay overnight in Luxor.

days.title: Luxor West Bank to Cairo
included: Cross Nile River to West Bank
Visit to Valley of the Kings
days.description: Early disembarkation has you crossing the Nile River to Luxor's West Bank. The Temple of Hatshepsut, built by Egypt's notable female Pharaoh, is your first stop. Next comes the Valley of the Kings where you can enter royal tombs and see some of the 64 tombs with their various complexities and ongoing archaeological work. You'll also pass by the Colossus of Memnon. Later, a transfer takes you to Luxor International Airport for an evening flight back to Cairo, with an overnight stay at your Cairo hotel.

days.title: Departure from Cairo
days.description: After breakfast, your transfer to Cairo International Airport is arranged so you can depart hassle-free. If you're interested in extending to Holy Mount Sinai, that's something you can inquire about before leaving.

intro:
Alpaca Expeditions offers the best itinerary option.

This trek is the first alternative for many hikers after the Inca Trail, as the regular route is often crowded and noisy. For this reason, we have carefully designed this itinerary with unique places to spend the night, ensuring that your trip becomes truly unforgettable.


By booking this option, you will stay in our glass cabins overlooking the Humantay Glacier and enjoy a unique experience under the stars in our Glass Domes. Then you will experience our famous Hobbit Houses —which include a jacuzzi— on the third night, and afterward enjoy a quiet night in a hotel in Aguas Calientes before your visit to Machu Picchu.


On the last day, you will visit Machu Picchu early in the morning, where you will have time to take photos and enjoy a guided tour. You will have an unparalleled experience accompanied by the best guides, professional chefs, friendly porters, high-quality equipment, and unique campsites.


AVAILABILITY:


We require a minimum of 02 travelers to start the trek any day of the year, from March to December.

If you are a solo traveler, please check availability with our sales team: info@alpacaexpeditions.com


Last-minute bookings do not guarantee access to Circuit 2.

If there is no availability for Circuit 2, Circuit 3 will be offered as an alternative, which will have an additional cost.


HIGHLIGHTS


• Glass cabins with beautiful views of the Humantay Glacier

• Early-morning visit to Humantay Lake

• Stunning views of Salkantay Mountain

• A magical night under the starry sky in our Glass Domes

• Hobbit House + jacuzzi + hot shower

• Visit to a coffee farm

• Hotel accommodation in Aguas Calientes

• Small groups, guaranteed experience

• Professional and friendly staff


THE JOURNEY IS THE DESTINATION!

days.title: Cusco to Soraypampa
included: Guided hike from Challacancha to Soraypampa (1.5 hours uphill)
days.meals: Breakfast (Breakfast at a local restaurant in Mollepata), Lunch (Freshly prepared lunch at Soraypampa), Dinner (Dinner following Peruvian cooking class)
days.description: Your pickup happens early, around 4:00-4:30 AM from your hotel, then you'll drive through Anta and Limatambo toward Mollepata with valley and Andes views along the way. After breakfast in Mollepata, you'll head to Challacancha where the trek begins. The hike up to Soraypampa at Glass Cabañas takes about 1.5 hours and stays gradual. Following lunch, you'll tackle the afternoon hike to Humantay Lagoon at 5,960m, which starts easy but gets steep as you near the turquoise waters and glacier. Back at camp by 4:00 PM, you'll join a Peruvian cooking class and have dinner under the stars.

days.title: Soraypampa to Wayracmachay
included: Guided hike to Salkantay Pampa (2 hours uphill)
Guided hike to Soyrococha (approximately 1 hour steep climb)
Guided hike to Salkantay Pass (approximately 1 hour)
Guided descent to Wayracmachay (2.5 hours downhill)
days.meals: Breakfast (Hot breakfast at 5:30 AM at Glass Cabañas), Lunch (Freshly prepared lunch at Soyrococha), Dinner (Dinner at Wayracmachay camp)
days.description: This is the hardest day of your trek. Hot breakfast starts at 5:30 AM at Glass Cabañas, then you'll hike toward Salkantay Pass with moderate uphill for 2 hours to Salkantay Pampa at 4,100m where you'll see glacier views. Next comes a steep zigzag climb for about an hour to Soyrococha beneath Salkantay peak, where lunch is ready. After refilling water bottles, you'll continue roughly an hour to Salkantay Pass at 4,630m, the trek's highest point, where you'll honor Pachamama and take in snow-capped peaks. The descent takes 2.5 hours through a green valley down to Wayracmachay camp at 3,800m at Glass Domes, finishing with dinner and rest under stars.

days.title: Wayracmachay to Loreta
included: Guided hike from Wayracmachay to Rayanpata (approximately 2 hours downhill)
Guided hike to Colpapampa (approximately 2 hours downhill)
Guided jungle hike to Loreta (approximately 4 hours)
days.meals: Breakfast (Breakfast at Wayracmachay camp), Lunch (Jungle-inspired lunch at Colpapampa), Dinner (Dinner at Hobbit House, Loreta)
days.description: You'll transition from high Andes to lush high jungle with warm breezes and tropical vegetation. Tea gets delivered to your room before breakfast, then you'll pack snacks and fill water bottles. The mostly downhill trail takes about 2 hours to Rayanpata where the jungle starts with warm air and tropical scents. After a short hydration break, it's 2 more hours to Colpapampa at 2,950m for jungle-inspired lunch. Then approximately 4 more hours along narrow jungle paths past waterfalls, orchids, and coffee fields until you reach Loreta and the unique Hobbit House with hot showers, soft bedding, and magical forest surroundings.

days.title: Loreta to Aguas Calientes
included: Guided hike along Inca Trail from Lucmabamba to Llactapata (approximately 4 hours uphill)
Guided tour of Llactapata archaeological site
Guided descent to Hidroelectrica (1.5 hours downhill)
Guided walk along railway tracks through Machu Picchu canyon (3 hours)
days.meals: Breakfast (Breakfast at Hobbit House, Loreta), Lunch (Freshly prepared lunch at Hidroelectrica)
days.description: You'll follow original Inca paths with views of Machu Picchu in the distance. Breakfast happens at the Hobbit House under a lush canopy, then a 30-minute drive takes you to Lucmabamba to start your hike. The well-preserved Inca Trail goes uphill for about 4 hours through forests of coffee, bananas, and avocados with ancient stonework visible. You'll reach Llactapata at 2,700m, an archaeological site where your guide gives a short tour and you catch panoramic views of Machu Picchu. Next is a 1.5 hour descent to Hidroelectrica for your final trek meal with the trekking crew. From there, walk 3 hours along railway tracks through Machu Picchu canyon spotting orchids, butterflies, and possibly Andean cock-of-the-rock or spectacled bears. You'll arrive in Aguas Calientes for check-in, a hot shower, and rest.

days.title: Aguas Calientes to Machu Picchu to Cusco
included: Guided tour of Machu Picchu citadel with Circuit 2 route (when booked)
Guided tour of upper citadel for classic views
optional: Huayna Picchu hike (2 hours; $75 per person; must be booked minimum 1 month in advance)
Explore, shop, or dine in Aguas Calientes during free time
Upgrade to Vistadome train ($75 per person)
days.description: After an early breakfast in Aguas Calientes, you'll board one of the first buses to Machu Picchu with your guide handling entry (bring ticket and passport). The tour starts at the upper citadel for the classic postcard view, then explores highlights including Inca architecture, history, spirituality, and engineering. If you've booked Huayna Picchu, there's an optional 2-hour hike afterward for views from above. You'll return by bus to Aguas Calientes with free time to explore, shop, or have lunch on your own. The afternoon train departs at 2:55 PM to Ollantaytambo, so arrive 30 minutes early. Your private driver transfers you to your Cusco hotel, arriving around 7:30-8:00 PM.

Option 2: Keep only Circuit 1A, which is currently the available option for your date. This circuit focuses on the panoramic experience and the most iconic views of Machu Picchu.

qa.question: What is the temperature range for the Sancantay treck the last week in September? How many people are generally in a group? What is the typical age range and physical abilities for those on this track?
qa.answer: What is the temperature range for the Salkantay Trek during the last week of September? According to climate records and meteorological studies of the area, the last week of September is considered one of the best periods for trekking, as it falls within the dry season. However, because the route crosses different altitude levels, temperatures can vary considerably. At Soraypampa (approx. 3,800 m / 12,467 ft), during the night and early morning, temperatures can drop approximately between -5°C and 5°C. During the day, with sunlight, temperatures are usually around 10°C to 20°C. In lower areas along the route, such as the cloud forest region, temperatures can be warmer, approximately between 15°C and 25°C. We recommend bringing appropriate clothing for changing conditions, including thermal layers, a warm jacket, a rain jacket, and cold-weather accessories. How many people are generally...

At the moment, Circuit 2 is completely sold out until the month of November, so we cannot guarantee its availability for your travel date. We will be happy to review the available options and offer you the best alternative according to the current availability for your visit day.

intro: This Tour in 10 days, covers the following sites: Amamn, Jerash, Ajloun, Madaba, Mount Nebo, Wadi Al Mujib, Dana, Petra, Dead Sea, Wadi Rum, Aqaba, Little Petra and others.

days.title: Arrival in Amman
days.start_point: مطار الملكة علياء الدولي, Queen Alia Airport Rd, ال جيزا, Amman, Jordan (مطار الملكة علياء الدولي, Queen Alia Airport Rd, ال جيزا, Amman, Jordan)
days.description: You'll arrive at Queen Alia Airport where the visa on arrival process is handled for you. From there, it's a transfer to your hotel in Amman for your first night to settle in.

days.title: Jerash - Ajloun
included: Amman city tour including Citadel and Roman Theatre
Jerash guided tour including colonnaded street and amphitheater
days.description: After breakfast, start with a city tour of Amman, checking out the Citadel and the Roman Theatre. Head north to Jerash to walk through the colonnaded streets and see the amphitheater of this well-preserved Greco-Roman city. Later you'll pass through Dibeen Forest on your way to Ajloun Castle, which sits on a hilltop with views across the Jordan Valley. Get back to Amman by evening.

days.title: Mount Nebo - Wadi Mujib - Dead Sea
included: Mount Nebo and Byzantine Church visit
days.description: Following breakfast, travel to Madaba to see St. George's Church and the ancient mosaic map of the Holy Land inside. Next, head to Mount Nebo for views over the Jordan Valley and its Byzantine Church. In the afternoon, explore Wadi Mujib Reserve where you can hike through the scenery. Finish the day swimming in the Dead Sea's warm salty waters before heading to your hotel.

days.title: Dana Reserve
days.description: After breakfast, you'll head south on the Kings Highway, an ancient trading route with centuries of history running through it. Stop at Karak Castle to see its Byzantine heritage. From there, continue to Dana Reserve where you can walk through Dana Village and experience landscapes that shift from wooded highlands to sand dunes.

days.title: Dana Reserve to Petra
days.description: Spend the morning hiking through Dana's varied scenery. Later, depart for Petra and travel to your overnight accommodation there. The drive gives you time to appreciate the desert landscape you'll be exploring.

days.title: Petra Full Day
included: Petra guided tour (3 hours) including Treasury, city center, Royal Tomb, Theatre, High Place of Sacrifice, and Roman soldier tombs
optional: Petra Back Door route - 2-hour hike starting from Little Petra through surrounding mountains to the Monastery (surcharge $180 USD for 1-6 people)
days.description: Explore the UNESCO World Heritage site of Petra, the ancient Nabatean city carved into desert rock over 2,000 years ago. You can choose between two guided tour options: the traditional route through the Siq Canyon to the Treasury and other major sites, or the more adventurous back door route that starts from Little Petra with a 2-hour hike.

days.title: Little Petra - Wadi Rum
days.description: Following breakfast, revisit Petra and explore Little Petra in Beida, the ancient trading suburb with its classical temple and 350-meter Cold Canyon entrance. In the afternoon, travel to Wadi Rum to explore Jordan's largest desert landscape by jeep or camel. Watch the sunset with local Bedouin while having tea, then enjoy a traditional dinner under the stars at your Bedouin camp.

days.title: Wadi Rum to Aqaba
days.description: After breakfast, explore Wadi Rum's desert landscape by 4x4 jeep for 4 hours, taking in the dramatic rock formations and desert scenery. Later, transfer to Aqaba, Jordan's only port city, and check into your hotel for the night.

days.title: Return to Amman
days.description: You have a free day to explore Aqaba at your own pace. Whether you want to walk along the waterfront, try some local restaurants, or relax by the sea, the time is yours. In the afternoon, transfer back to Amman for your final night.

days.title: Departure from Amman
days.description: Head to Queen Alia International Airport for your departure. Your tour comes to an end.

intro: Embark on an exhilarating Amazonian journey, commencing in the bustling Manaus and stretching into the heart of the jungle. Tranquil waters, vibrant wildlife, and traditional village bonds complement adventurous piranha fishing and thrilling cayman spotting. With expert jungle guidance, discover the forest's secrets and embrace traditional lifestyles, ensuring an unforgettable escape.

days.title: Manaus to Amazon Jungle
included: Speedboat transfer across the Meeting of the Waters
Scenic van drive through rainforest to Paraná do Mamori
Caiman safari by canoe with up-close wildlife encounter
days.meals: Lunch (Amazonian lunch at the lodge), Dinner (Dinner at the lodge)
days.start_point: Rua Manaus, Mathias Velho, Canoas - Rio Grande do Sul, 92340, Brazil (Airport, Bus Station, or Hotel Pick-up.)
days.description: Your adventure kicks off early with a speedboat ride across the Meeting of the Waters to Careiro village, then you'll head into the rainforest by van toward Paraná do Mamori. By mid-morning you're settling in at the jungle lodge. After eating lunch, you'll paddle out for piranha fishing and keep an eye out for pink river dolphins in the water. Once evening rolls around, your guide takes you on a canoe safari to spot caimans, and if you're interested they'll catch and handle some of the smaller ones so you can get photos.

days.title: Amazon Jungle
included: Ecological jungle trek with guide instruction on medicinal plants and survival techniques
days.meals: Breakfast, Lunch (Amazonian lunch at the lodge)
days.description: Get up early to catch the sunrise while birdwatching, looking for tropical birds across the forest canopy. You'll grab breakfast once you're back, then spend the morning on an ecological trek where your guide teaches you about medicinal plants, survival techniques, and the wildlife like monkeys and sloths you'll encounter. After lunch at the lodge, you head out for an overnight jungle camp experience. Your guide will show you spear fishing and other survival skills while you search for nocturnal animals under the stars.

days.title: Amazon Jungle
included: Canoe paddle through flooded forests and creeks
Wildlife and plant observation with guide commentary
Visit to caboclo family riverside home
days.meals: Breakfast (Jungle-prepared breakfast), Lunch (Amazonian lunch at the lodge)
days.description: Start with breakfast prepared jungle-style, then take a canoe through the flooded forests and narrow creeks, watching wildlife and learning how the Amazon's ecosystem works. Back at the lodge for lunch, and then you'll visit a local caboclo family's home by the river to watch them make manioc flour and see how they live. You stay overnight with the family so you can get a real sense of their daily life and traditions along the river.

days.title: Amazon Jungle
included: Wildlife spotting: monkeys, birds, river dolphins
Night canoe ride through narrow channels
days.description: You're camping in different spots deep in the rainforest that your guides have picked out. During the day you'll trek through untouched forest looking for monkeys, birds, and river dolphins while picking up survival skills from your guide. As it gets dark, you try spear fishing to catch your own dinner, then paddle through narrow channels spotting animals that come out at night. You can either sleep under the stars in the forest or with a local Amazon family, depending on what you prefer.

days.title: Amazon Jungle to Manaus
included: Return journey from jungle camp to lodge
Return speedboat and van transfer to Manaus Downtown Area
days.meals: Breakfast, Lunch (Last Amazonian lunch at the lodge)
days.description: Your last morning in the jungle you wake up surrounded by rainforest sounds and wildlife, have breakfast, then begin heading back to the lodge, getting there around 11:30. You'll have one more lunch with everyone at the lodge, then at 1 PM start the boat and van journey back to Manaus. As you travel, the dense rainforest slowly gives way to more developed areas, and you'll roll into Manaus by around 5 PM.

attributes.tip: Immerse yourself in rich history and local traditions

attributes.tip: An experienced guide will be with you for the entire tour

intro:
We leave Edinburgh in the morning and head north towards the stunning Kelpies. We pass Stirling and take in views of the towering Wallace Monument and its' stunning Castle. Listen to stories about the insane events which have taken place in this area throughout history. Enter into the wild Scottish Highlands, passing the medieval stronghold of Doune Castle; featured in Outlander and Game of Thrones.   

Our next stop is eerie Glen Coe; one of Scotland’s most iconic and dramatic landscapes. Hear the harrowing tale of the 1692 massacre of Clan MacDonald, as you soak up the epic scenery. Tonight, we’ll stay in the bustling fishing town of Oban; enjoy fresh seafood and dance the night away at a traditional Scottish ceilidh – the best way to bond with your new tour buddies. (Overnight: Oban)

days.title: Edinburgh to Oban
included: View Stirling Castle and Wallace Monument
days.start_point: 60 High Street, Edinburgh, EH1 1TB, United Kingdom (60 High Street, The Royal Mile, Edinburgh, EH1 1TB)
days.description: You'll head north from Edinburgh to see the Kelpies sculpture, then pass by Stirling Castle and the Wallace Monument on your way into the Highlands. Doune Castle comes up next - you might recognize it from Outlander and Game of Thrones. The landscape gets more dramatic as you push toward Glen Coe, and you'll end the day in Oban, a fishing town where dinner features fresh seafood followed by a traditional Scottish ceilidh.

days.title: Oban to Isle of Skye
included: Local pub evening on Isle of Skye
days.description: This morning takes you north past Fort William where Ben Nevis, the UK's tallest mountain, sits on the horizon. You'll pass the Glenfinnan Viaduct - that's the Harry Potter bridge - with its striking Highland views behind it. From there, the route leads to the Isle of Skye where you'll spend the night. Later, head to a local pub to try some local ale, whisky, and get a feel for Scottish hospitality.

days.title: Isle of Skye to Inverness
days.description: The entire day focuses on exploring the Isle of Skye and its otherworldly landscape - waterfalls, ancient mountains, and a dramatic coastline. You'll learn about Viking history, ancient monarchs, and local legends while you're there. After that, you head back to the mainland, stopping at Eilean Donan Castle for photos before visiting Dundreggan Rewilding Centre to learn about Scotland's ancient Caledonian Forest. The drive along the Great Glen takes you to Inverness for the night.

days.title: Inverness
optional: Hunt for Nessie on a Loch Ness cruise (reserve at time of booking)
days.description: Start with an easy walk along Loch Ness shores, keeping an eye out for Nessie. Then drive through the North West Highlands to reach Beauly, a quiet town with a historic Priory you might know from Outlander season two. Next comes Clava Cairns, a mysterious prehistoric burial site with standing stones, followed by Culloden Battlefield where you'll hear about Bonnie Prince Charlie and the 1746 Jacobite Rising. Return to Inverness after that for the night.

days.title: Inverness to Edinburgh
days.description: This morning you'll visit the Highland Folk Museum to see how people lived in the Highlands centuries ago, then stop at a local whisky distillery for a tasting session. Later, drive to the village of Dunkeld for a walk through its streets and along the River Tay, where you can visit the historic cathedral. You'll head back to Edinburgh by early evening.

reviews.reply:
Dear Emily,

Thank you for taking the time to share your feedback about your recent Highland Fling Tour with our fantastic Driver-Guide, Liz.

Haggis Adventures and our sister brand, Highland Explorer Tours, operate this itinerary jointly, and I'm sorry that this arrangement was not made clearer prior to departure.

Haggis Adventures is typically aimed at travellers seeking a more budget-conscious travel experience, with included shared hostel accommodation and a demographic that tends to attract younger travellers. Highland Explorer Tours, meanwhile, caters to a broader range of guests, generally aged 5 to 99+, and offers private B&B accommodation at a higher price point.

As a result, the age range of travellers on this particular 5-day tour can vary significantly from departure to departure. We therefore regret that the third-party advertising you viewed did not accurately reflect your personal experience of the group dynamics during your tour.

I am delighted to hear your positive comments about Liz. She will be thrilled to receive your feedback. We always strive to provide an engaging, informative, and entertaining guided experience, and it's wonderful to know that she helped make your journey memorable.

Thank you again for sharing your thoughts. We truly value your feedback and hope you'll look back fondly on your wee Scottish adventure!
Kind regards,
Amy

Dear Niels, many thanks for taking the time to share your feedback following your recent tour experience!
We are delighted to hear that you enjoyed many elements of the tour including the company of our expert driver guide, hostel accommodation and distillery visit. We are pleased that you appreciated the schedule of the itinerary and found that activities and timings were clearly communicated.

We regret that certain aspects of the tour fell below expectations and would like to directly address your comments to provide some more information about our tour product.
With regards to the age range of passengers for this tour, the Highland Fling tour is one of our multi-day tours shared between Haggis Adventures passengers and passengers travelling with our sister brand Highland Explorer Tours Ltd. Feedback from past passengers prompted our company to offer the same 5-day tour itinerary to passengers from both brands to increase the diversity and age range of our passengers. Since making this change to merge passengers on select tours, we have received positive feedback from our travellers who enjoy sharing travel experiences with a more diverse group. We will ensure that all third party booking partners are clearly marketing the age range of passengers for each tour to ensure expectations are managed prior to departure.
We welcome your feedback regarding the number of museum stops alongside time spent at The Old Man of Storr and Eilean Donan Castle.
During the peak summer months, coach bay parking at both locations is extremely limited and therefore our driver guides will decide each day of the tour whether it is possible to include an extended stop at each location or whether it will be necessary to include a shorter scenic photo stop. We regret that longer could not be allocated during the schedule to these featured stops during your travel dates. Every effort will be made to maximise the time spent at the highlight locations and where possible additional bonus stops will be offered to showcase even more of bonnie Scotland where timings/ availability allows.

We will certainly forward your feedback directly to our product development team to ensure the continued development and improvement of our tour collection.

We hope that you will treasure memories of your tour and hope to welcome you back for another adventure in the future!

Kind regards,
Amy- Haggis Adventures

attributes.tip: Seek thrilling adventures that keep you moving

intro: Just think; lush green jungles, volcanic hot springs, breathtaking waterfalls, a diverse range of wildlife, and more adventure activities then you can count. Costa Rica not only boasts the title of the world’s most diverse eco-system but also has gained a reputation as one of the adventurous capitals of the world! Starting in San Jose you’ll meet your new travel buddies before heading to experience life of locals in the rural village of Coope San Juan. Explore the volcanic hot springs in La Fortuna, and get up close and personal to wildlife on a night safari in Monteverde. Witness breathtaking views ziplining through the canopy of the cloud forest, and unwind in a sunset yoga class in Santa Teresa. An incredible experience of what Costa Rica has to offer!

days.title: Arrival
days.description: You'll land in San Jose and get settled into your accommodation, which gives you time to shake off any travel fatigue and get oriented. This evening brings a welcome dinner with your group, followed by drinks around the city so you can start getting to know everyone and feel out the vibe of the country.

days.title: Coop San Juan
included: Bike Ride through rural Costa Rica
days.description: A scenic 3.5-hour minibus ride takes you into the countryside toward Coop San Juan, a rural village where you'll stay with a local family. Your hosts will teach you how they cook traditional meals, and you'll have time to walk around the village and look for wildlife. As evening comes, there's time for games and conversation before gathering around a bonfire.

days.title: La Fortuna
days.description: The minibus heads toward La Fortuna, where Arenal Volcano dominates the landscape. After checking in, you'll hike around the volcano's base to take in the views, then soak in natural hot springs to relax your muscles. Dinner with the group happens later in the evening.

days.title: La Fortuna
optional: Various adventure activities in La Fortuna (details available from Tru Leader)
days.description: This day is yours to shape. Your tour leader can suggest activities depending on whether you want to chill or get your adrenaline going, and there's plenty to choose from around La Fortuna. You'll have time to freshen up back at your hotel before rejoining the group for dinner and drinks.

days.title: La Fortuna to Monteverde
days.description: You'll travel through jungle mountains and cross a scenic lake with views of Arenal Volcano in the distance, heading toward Monteverde. Once you've settled in, a nocturnal safari takes you out into the forest where you can spot sloths, armadillos, tree frogs, and various bird species as darkness falls.

days.title: Monteverde
days.description: Today is all about ziplining through Monteverde's cloud forest canopy. This region is known for having some of the longest and most thrilling zipline courses, and you'll experience the rush of flying through the forest at heights that give you a completely different perspective on the landscape.

days.title: Monteverde to Santa Teresa
included: Beach time for sunset and cocktails
days.description: A minibus ride and ferry crossing bring you to Santa Teresa, a lively beach town popular with surfers and travelers looking for that laid-back coastal vibe. After dropping your bags at accommodation, you'll head straight to the beach for cocktails and watch the sun set over the Pacific.

days.title: Santa Teresa
optional: Surfing lessons at local surf schools
days.description: The beach is calling, and you can spend the day however suits you. Some people lounge in the sand while others take advantage of optional surfing lessons at local schools. Late afternoon brings a sunset yoga class if you want to stretch out and find some calm before things pick up again.

days.title: Santa Teresa to Montezuma
days.description: You'll travel to Montezuma, another beach town with a more bohemian feel, and grab lunch right by the water. A hike to one of Costa Rica's iconic waterfalls lets you search for howler monkeys and other wildlife along the way. After exploring Montezuma's artisan shops and laid-back atmosphere, you'll head back to Santa Teresa for a farewell dinner with the group.

days.title: Santa Teresa
days.description: It's time to check out and say goodbye to your group. The morning is free for you to wander Santa Teresa one last time or just relax at your place. Your tour leader is available to help arrange transport back to San Jose or to wherever you're heading next.

intro: If you are looking for a truly fun & unique adventure, our 11 day Yucatán Experience is just what you need! Touch down in Cancún to get ready to explore the crystal Carribean sea via an island boat trip, before chilling out on the pristine, white sandy beaches. Dive into the culture at the ancient Mayan site of Chichen Itza and cool off in cenotes - natural freshwater pools made from collapsed limestone. Check out the magnificent 7 colour lagoon, take on a tequila tasting session and test your salsa dancing skills. The perfect trip for island & beach lovers looking to immerse yourself in the culture & fun of Yucantán Mexico. Join us for the complete Yucatán fiesta!

days.title: Cancun
days.description: You'll arrive in Cancun and have time to settle into your accommodation. This afternoon, check out the local shopping scene at Market 28, Plaza Las Americas, and Puerto Cancun if you want to browse Mexican clothing boutiques and accessories. Later, join your group for a welcome dinner by the pool or on the beach with drinks and beers to meet everyone on the trip.

days.title: Isla Holbox
optional: Swimming and exploring tropical marine life
Beach bar visits with live music
days.description: Take a ferry out to Isla Holbox, a car-free island with pristine beaches and no vehicles at all. You'll have the day to relax and explore, checking out the tropical marine life and lounging in sea hammocks. The funky beach bars have live music if you want to get out, or you can just chill and gear up for the Yucatan adventure ahead.

days.title: Isla Holbox
days.description: After a morning to relax, you'll board a boat to explore three different spots: Bird Island with its unique bird species, Eye of the Water cenote featuring that bright turquoise freshwater pool surrounded by mangroves, and Passion Island known for its pink flamingos. By evening, grab beers on the boat and watch the sunset, and if you're lucky, you might catch bioluminescence glowing in the ocean after dark.

days.title: Isla Holbox to Merida
days.description: You'll leave Holbox early and head to Chichen Itza, one of the seven wonders. A guided tour walks you through the ancient Mayan ruins and explains the civilization. After that, stop at Cenote Yokdzonot for a swim in the turquoise water. By early evening, you'll travel to Merida and get an orientation walk around the city to see what's there.

days.title: Merida
days.description: Cycle between three cenotes with a lunch break somewhere along the route. You'll swim and hang out at each location. Back in Merida, take a few hours to rest, then it's time for a Mexican feast with tacos and burritos. The evening includes a tequila and mezcal tasting, followed by salsa dancing at bars with live music.

days.title: Merida to Bacalar
optional: Kayaking or paddleboarding at Bacalar Lagoon
days.description: Leave Merida by minibus and head to Bacalar, arriving in the early afternoon. From there, go to Bacalar Lagoon with its incredibly clear blue water. Spend your time lounging on the sand, kayaking or paddleboarding to explore, or just taking a dip to cool off. When evening comes, relax by the water and watch the sunset with optional beers.

days.title: Bacalar
days.description: Check out the famous 7 Color Lagoon with its distinct shades of turquoise, blue, and deep indigo created by the clear waters and white sandy bottom. You'll stop at several spots throughout the day for swimming, photos, and lunch. The color variations throughout the lagoon are pretty special.

days.title: Bacalar to Tulum
days.description: Travel by minibus to Tulum, a trendy beachside town. Spend your afternoon exploring around town or relaxing on the white sandy beaches. Later in the evening, meet up with your group for dinner and drinks somewhere in town.

days.title: Tulum
optional: Tulum archaeological site visit (trips before November 2025)
days.description: What you do depends on your departure date. If your trip is before November 2025, you'll visit the Tulum archaeological site in the Riviera Maya with ancient Mayan ruins overlooking blue ocean and white sandy beaches, then swim and grab cocktails at beach lounges. Trips from November 2025 onward take it easier this morning to recharge, then head to the beach for swimming and cocktails at beach lounges with that same ocean backdrop.

days.title: Tulum to Playa del Carmen
days.description: Travel to Playa del Carmen, a popular beachside resort town. Spend your time shopping for souvenirs or picking up personal treats, or just relax on the beach to keep that summer glow going. Your group will gather for a farewell dinner and drinks in this lively town to wrap up the trip.

days.title: Playa del Carmen
days.description: Check out and depart. The trip ends here, and assistance is available if you need help arranging onward travel or getting home. Take time to think back on all the memories and friendships you made throughout your Mexico adventure.

intro:
Amazing Thailand in 9 Days offers a captivating journey through the diverse landscapes and rich culture of Thailand. This meticulously designed tour blends the excitement of urban exploration with moments of serene relaxation. Discover the grandeur of Bangkok's royal palaces and sacred temples, followed by an immersion into the artistic heritage of Chiang Rai. Venture into the lush landscapes of Doi Inthanon National Park, exploring its hidden waterfalls and Thailand's highest peak. Finally, unwind on the golden shores of Phuket, where pristine beaches provide the perfect escape. From the vibrant energy of Bangkok to the tranquil beauty of the north and the tropical allure of the south, this 9-day adventure presents a comprehensive and unforgettable experience of Thailand's most treasured destinations.

Top it all, by choosing this tour you will contribute to the local community. From each trip booked on Tour Radar, we donate $20 to our foundation which helps to maintain the projects we run for developing a safe and green environment for children and our environmental protection initiatives. you could find more details and reports on our social media.

days.title: Bangkok
optional: Explore the streets of Bangkok to discover historic charm, architectural marvels, and local products
days.start_point: Suvarnabhumi Airport (BKK) ท่าอากาศยานสุวรรณภูมิ, 999 Moo 1 Debaratana Rd, Bang Phli, Samut Prakan 10540, Thailand (Suvarnabhumi International Airport)
days.description: Your private driver meets you at the airport and takes you to your hotel in Bangkok. After checking in, the afternoon and evening are yours to wander around the historic streets, check out the architectural landmarks, and browse the local markets at whatever pace works for you before heading back to rest.

days.title: Bangkok
included: Visit Royal Grand Palace and Emerald Buddha (Wat Phra Kaew)
Visit Reclining Buddha image at Wat Pho (oldest and largest temple, more than 200 years old)
days.description: After a final breakfast in Bangkok, your private driver takes you to the airport for the flight to Chiang Mai. Once you land, another driver meets you and transfers you to your hotel. You'll have the rest of the day free to relax and get settled in.

days.title: Bangkok to Chiang Mai
days.description: Your guide picks you up from the hotel for a temple tour starting at the Royal Grand Palace and Emerald Buddha. From there you'll head to Wat Pho to see the Reclining Buddha, one of the city's oldest and largest temples. The final stop is Wat Benchamabopit, known as the Marble Temple for its striking combination of Italian marble and traditional Thai architectural details.

days.title: Chiang Mai - Chiang Rai
included: Visit Maekhachan Hot Springs (natural geothermal site)
Visit Blue Temple (Wat Rong Suea Ten)
days.meals: Breakfast, Lunch (Delightful lunch (time and location to be confirmed on tour))
days.description: You'll depart early around 7:00 AM for a full-day group tour through northern Thailand. The itinerary includes a stop at Maekhachan Hot Springs, then the White Temple with its white and mirrored mosaics, followed by the Blue Temple known for its deep blue color. After lunch you'll explore the Black House Museum to see Lanna-style architecture and local art. You'll get back to Chiang Mai around 5:00 PM.

days.title: Chiang Mai - Doi Inthanon National Park
included: Visit Doi Inthanon National Park (highest peak of Thailand)
View the summit and walk nature trails
Visit Nophamaytanidol Chedi and Phra Mahatat Nopaphon Bhumisiri pagodas
Walk through jungle to hidden waterfall
Pass through farmland with coffee plantation, flowers farm, and rice terraces
Visit Pagagayaw Karen hill tribe village and taste locally ground coffee
days.description: An early pickup between 7:00 and 7:30 AM takes you to Doi Inthanon National Park, Thailand's highest peak. You'll enjoy views from the summit and walk nature trails to spot birds and wildflowers, then visit two pagodas built to honor the King and Queen. After lunch you'll hike about 2 hours through jungle to find a hidden waterfall, pass through coffee plantations and rice terraces, visit a Karen hill tribe village, and see the 70-meter Vachirathern waterfall before returning around 6:30 PM.

days.title: Chiang Mai to Phuket
optional: Half-day Elephant Sanctuary Tour (USD 85 per person): Learn about elephants, change into traditional Karen clothing, feed and interact with elephants, participate in mud spa, walk with and bathe elephants in river, eat traditional meal
days.description: You can choose to join an optional half-day group tour to the Elephant Jungle Sanctuary (USD 85 per person) where you'll change into traditional Karen clothing, feed and interact with elephants, enjoy a mud spa, bathe them in the river, and have a traditional meal, then take a late evening flight. Otherwise your driver will pick you up for the transfer to Chiang Mai airport and the flight to Phuket, where you'll be picked up again for transfer to your hotel.

days.title: Phuket
optional: Relax at the beach, sunbathe, swim, or try snorkeling
Visit Hanuman World Phuket for zipline activities
Enjoy seafood dinner at a local restaurant
days.description: You have a completely free day in Phuket. The island has beaches, tropical rainforests, and limestone cliffs. You might relax on the beach with a cold drink and swim, try snorkeling, check out the Cape Panwa aquarium to see marine life, or do jungle ziplines at Hanuman World Phuket. In the evening you could have seafood dinner, browse a night market, or grab drinks on Bangla Road.

days.title: Phuket
optional: Optional Phi Phi Maya Bay, Pileh Cove, and Bamboo Island Speedboat Tour (USD 75 per person): Visit Bamboo Island for swimming and snorkeling, enjoy beachside lunch on Phi Phi Don Island, swim in Pileh Lagoon, visit Maya Bay and Monkey Beach, see Viking Cave
days.description: Your day is free to relax or explore Phuket however you want. If interested, you can join an optional group speedboat tour to the Phi Phi Islands (USD 75 per person) departing at 7:30 AM with breakfast snacks and drinks at the marina. The tour visits Bamboo Island for swimming and snorkeling, includes lunch at a beachside restaurant on Phi Phi Don, visits Pileh Lagoon and Maya Bay and Monkey Beach, sees Viking Cave, and returns by around 5:15 PM.

days.title: Phuket
optional: Visit local markets to buy souvenirs
days.description: You'll have breakfast and check out from your hotel. There's time to visit local markets to pick up souvenirs before your private driver takes you to the airport for your departure flight home.

intro:
Welcome to Southern Africa – A Wildlife Paradise

­ 

Southern Africa is home to one of the richest wildlife communities on Earth, offering unforgettable encounters with diverse animal and bird species. This 8-day cross-border safari experience takes you through three magnificent countries—Zambia, Botswana, and Zimbabwe—promising adventure, culture, and breathtaking natural beauty.

­ 

Why This Safari is Perfect for You

­ 

Start in Zambia – The Real Africa

­ 

Your journey begins in Zambia, a country celebrated for its friendly people, abundant wildlife, vibrant culture, and rich history. With the recent introduction of visa-free entry for many international travelers, Zambia stands out as one of Africa’s most accessible and welcoming holiday destinations.

­ 

Zambia is also home to one of the Seven Natural Wonders of the World—the mighty Victoria Falls—and offers some of the most pristine landscapes on the continent.

­ 

A Truly Authentic Three-Country Experience

­ 

This itinerary is designed to deliver exceptional wildlife viewing, cultural immersion, and soft adventure activities. You will explore:

­ 

Mosi-oa-Tunya National Park (Zambia)

­ 

Chobe National Park (Botswana)

­ 

Zambezi National Park (Zimbabwe)

­ 

Each park offers unique landscapes and an abundance of wildlife, including elephants, rhinos, big cats, diverse birdlife, and more.

­ 

Tour Kick-Off and Journey

­ 

Your safari commences in Lusaka, the capital of Zambia. After meeting your trip leader at StayEasy Lusaka Hotel (GPS: S15° 24' 10'' / E28° 17' 7''), you will travel south with an overnight stop in Choma, before proceeding to Livingstone—the tourism capital of Zambia. From here, you will venture across borders into Botswana and Zimbabwe for the ultimate wildlife experience.

­ 

Tour End Options

­ 

Standard End Point: Livingstone, Zambia

Includes a complimentary transfer to Harry Mwaanga Nkumbula International Airport and covered accommodation for the final night.

­ 

Alternative End Point: Victoria Falls, Zimbabwe

A transfer back to Zimbabwe can be arranged if your outbound flight is from Victoria Falls International Airport (final night’s accommodation in Zimbabwe not included).

­ 

Highlights of Each Destination

1. Zambia – “The Real Africa”

­ 

Home of the Victoria Falls and the iconic Mosi-oa-Tunya National Park

­ 

Rare opportunity to see white rhinos

­ 

Rich cultural and historical experiences, including museums and heritage sites

­ 

Peaceful, welcoming, and deeply authentic

­ 

2. Botswana – Africa’s 2019 Best Eco-Tourism Destination

­ 

Experience a full-day safari to Chobe National Park, world-famous for:

­ 

Africa’s largest elephant population

­ 

High densities of predators including lions, leopards, and painted dogs

­ 

Exceptional river-based and land-based game viewing

­ 

3. Zimbabwe – A World of Wonders

­ 

Discover:

­ 

Zambezi National Park, known for its scenic river views and abundant elephants

­ 

Additional spectacular viewpoints of Victoria Falls from the Zimbabwean side

­ 

Soft Adventure Activities Included

­ 

Overland travel from Lusaka

­ 

Visits to Munali Pass and Samu Lya Moomba Heritage Sites

­ 

Tours of Choma and Livingstone Museums

­ 

Guided nature walk and rhino tracking

­ 

Victoria Falls tour (Zambia and Zimbabwe)

­ 

Chobe National Park day trip (Botswana)

­ 

Zambezi National Park game drive (Zimbabwe)

­ 

Quality, Safety & Flexibility

­ 

This itinerary has been updated according to:

­ 

WHO health and hygiene protocols

­ 

Sustainable travel guidelines from UN Climate Change (COP27)

­ 

All departure dates are 100% guaranteed, with no minimum number of travelers required. You may join a group, request a private tour, or choose a solo travel arrangement based on your preference.

­ 

Sustainable Tourism & Social Responsibility

­ 

We proudly support local communities by partnering with locally owned lodges, restaurants, and service providers. Our theme is:

“Take photos and leave your footprints only.”

­ 

Health & Safety – Malaria Advisory

­ 

Zambia, Botswana, and Zimbabwe are malaria-risk countries. Travelers should:

­ 

Take recommended malaria prophylaxis

­ 

Use mosquito repellents and bed nets

­ 

Seek medical advice from a travel clinic before departure

­ 

Visa Information

­ 

As of 1 October 2022, Zambia offers visa-free entry to nationals from:

­ 

USA, UK, EU countries

­ 

Canada, Australia, New Zealand

­ 

China, Japan, South Korea

­ 

Gulf States

…and others.

Travelers from countries outside this list should consult their local embassy or travel agent for visa requirements.

­ 

Our Goal

­ 

To offer you a peaceful, rejuvenating, and adventure-filled holiday—combining wildlife, culture, nature, and unforgettable experiences across Southern Africa.

­ 

If you’d like, I can also help convert this into a full itinerary document or format it into a brochure-style presentation.

days.title: Lusaka to Choma
included: View Kafue River and Kafue Road Bridge
Visit Munali Pass National Monument heritage site
Stop at roadside lay-bye station for fresh fruit (bananas and apples)
Tour Samu Lya Moomba national heritage site in Monze
Visit Family Safari private animal sanctuary in Monze
days.meals: Lunch (Sumptuous lunch at Indian Classic Food Restaurant or other good restaurant in Monze), Dinner (Delicious dinner at lodge or good restaurant in Choma)
days.start_point: 10, Luneta, Lusaka, Lusaka, Zambia (The pick up point in Lusaka at StayEasy Hotel at Levy Mall , 06:30)
days.description: Your safari kicks off at 6:30am from StayEasy Lusaka Hotel, heading south through Zambia's interior. Along the way you'll cross the Kafue River and Bridge, then stop at Munali Hills Pass Monument to take in some history. The route passes through Mazabuka's sugar plantations before reaching Samu Lya Moomba heritage site near Monze. Lunch is included partway through, and you'll arrive in Choma with time to check in and have dinner.

days.title: Choma to Livingstone
included: Visit and tour Choma Museum and Craft Centre
View Kalundu Mound Iron-Age archaeological site
optional: Visit former Colonial Administrators Residence in Kalomo
Visit site of first Standard Chartered Bank of North-Western Rhodesia in Kalomo
days.description: After breakfast in Choma, you'll check out and visit the Choma Museum and Craft Centre to get a sense of local culture. From there it's on to Kalomo to see Kalundu Mound, an important historic site. The drive to Livingstone takes up most of the afternoon, and you should be settled at your lodge by late afternoon. Dinner's not included this evening, so plan where you'd like to eat.

days.title: Livingstone to Chobe National Park, Botswana (Day Trip)
included: Game drive in Chobe National Park in open safari vehicle with qualified guide
Buffet lunch at Chobe Safari Lodge Restaurant on Chobe River shores
Chobe River boat cruise on speedboat with guide
days.meals: Lunch (Delicious buffet lunch at Chobe Safari Lodge Restaurant on Chobe River shores)
days.description: An early pickup gets you to the Kazungula border crossing where you'll enter Botswana. Head into Chobe National Park for a morning game drive, one of Africa's best spots for wildlife viewing. You'll have lunch at Chobe Safari Lodge right on the river, then take an afternoon boat cruise to see elephants, hippos, and crocodiles in their natural habitat. The drive back to Livingstone happens by evening.

days.title: Livingstone
days.description: Start with breakfast before heading to Victoria Falls for a morning tour of one of the Seven Natural Wonders. You'll see the massive sheet of falling water and the misty rainbows it creates. Back in Livingstone, stop by the Livingstone Museum to explore the city's history. The afternoon gives you time to rest at your lodge, then later you'll visit Mukuni Village on Livingstone's outskirts for a guided tour. Lunch and dinner are self-pay.

days.title: Livingstone
included: Morning game drive in Mosi-oa-Tunya National Park for approximately 2 hours in open 4x4 safari vehicle with qualified guide
Rhino walk safari in Mosi-oa-Tunya National Park
Visit Old Drift Crossing Point and Cemetery historic site within Mosi-oa-Tunya National Park
Sunset cruise on Zambezi River on medium-sized boat with snacks and refreshments
days.meals: Breakfast (Sumptuous breakfast before morning game drive)
days.description: Start with breakfast before heading into Mosi-oa-Tunya National Park for a morning in an open 4x4 vehicle. You'll do a game drive and rhino walk, spotting elephants, buffalo, and white rhinos. Next you'll visit the Old Drift Crossing Point before leaving the park around noon. After touring the National Art Gallery, you have free time for lunch. Later in the afternoon, transfer to the Zambezi River for a sunset cruise with snacks and beverages included.

days.title: Livingstone to Zambezi National Park, Zimbabwe (Day Trip)
included: View Victoria Falls from Zimbabwean side with access to 16 viewpoints in rainforest
Afternoon game drive in Zambezi National Park in Zimbabwe
optional: Lunch at Look Out Cafe (advance reservation required; self-pay)
Lunch at Malonga Village Restaurant (self-pay alternative)
days.meals: Breakfast (Breakfast in Livingstone before traveling to border)
days.description: Following breakfast in Livingstone, you'll travel to the Zimbabwe border and walk across the historic Victoria Falls Bridge. On the Zimbabwe side, explore Victoria Falls with access to 16 viewpoints set within the rainforest. Walk through Victoria Falls town, then head into Zambezi National Park for an afternoon game drive. You'll return to Livingstone by evening. Dinner is on your own, though nightlife options are available if you're interested.

days.title: Livingstone
optional: Devil's Pool swimming experience at Victoria Falls (self-pay; subject to seasonal water levels)
Angel's Pool swimming experience on Zambezi River (self-pay; alternative to Devil's Pool if water levels high)
Microlight and Ultralight flights over Victoria Falls (self-pay)
Spa and wellness activities at Livingstone Rudson Blu Hotel (self-pay)
Relaxation at Livingstone Rudson Blu Hotel sun yard
days.description: This day is yours to structure as you'd like. If relaxation appeals to you, spend time at Livingstone Rudson Blu Hotel's sun yard with optional access to spa and wellness services. For those wanting action, there are plenty of activities on the Zambezi River and around Victoria Falls to choose from. Just arrange any activities in advance with the tour operator. All meals are at your own cost.

days.title: Livingstone to Lusaka
days.description: Wake up early and pack everything. You'll have your last special breakfast before transfer to Livingstone International Airport by 10:30 am to catch your flight home. This wraps up your 8-day safari across Zambia, Botswana, and Zimbabwe.

reviews.body: We didn’t get the same itinerary so wasn't sure what was happening each day and then what was...
reviews.reply:
Dear Jan,
Thank you so much for taking the time to share your experience with us. First and foremost, we sincerely appreciate you choosing to travel with Lochinvar Safaris. We’re truly sorry to hear that parts of your safari did not meet your expectations, and we deeply regret any frustration you may have experienced during your journey.

We understand how important it is to have clear communication, especially when it comes to itinerary details and daily planning. It’s disappointing to hear that you felt out of the loop at times, and we acknowledge how unsettling that can be—particularly when it affects what you bring along for the day. We'll be taking this feedback seriously to ensure better consistency and clarity moving forward.

Regarding the seating arrangement and the vehicle used, please be assured that we followed legal and safety guidelines as per the manufacturer's specifications. That said, your comfort is equally important to us, and we’re sorry to hear you felt cramped. This is certainly something we’ll consider when assigning vehicles for future group sizes.

When it comes to accommodation, we do our best to balance quality and logistics, and we truly regret that some locations didn’t meet your expectations. We're glad our team acted promptly to move you to a different hotel upon learning of the issues—though we understand that the challenges with electricity and water were far from ideal. These challenges, while unfortunately outside our control, are nonetheless frustrating, and we appreciate your patience.

We’d also like to extend our thanks for acknowledging the efforts of the tour guides. While we stand by the professionalism and training of our guide Fines—who is one of our most experienced and respected team members—we understand that difficult circumstances can sometimes impact even the best-planned tours. Your feedback will help us identify areas where we can continue to improve support for our guides in the field.

Jan, we truly value all feedback—positive and constructive—as it helps us grow and refine the experience for every guest. Your thoughts have already prompted internal discussions, and we are committed to learning from them.

Thank you again for traveling with us, and we hope we’ll have the opportunity to provide you with a smoother, more enjoyable experience in the future.

Warmest regards,
Mark - (On behalf of the Lochinvar Safaris Team)

qa.question: I am 73 years old healthy and my doctor says it is not good for me to get a Yellow fever shot but doctor can give me a yellow fever exemption letter. So will the countries accept me with a Yellow fever exemption letter for me to go on this tour? Do you have any other suggestions/requirments to go on this tour?
qa.answer: For this tour, none of the three countries included in the itinerary require a Yellow Fever Vaccination Certificate. As such, there is no Yellow Fever vaccination requirement stated anywhere in our tour itinerary. You should not need to provide a Yellow Fever Certificate or an exemption letter for this particular tour. However, we always recommend carrying your doctor's exemption letter with you when traveling, as it may be useful should any questions arise during your journey or transit.

intro: Uncover the most famous India destinations  starting with the visit of Delhi where you'll uncover the most significant monuments then continue to the Agra to make your journey memorable with an visit of Taj Mahal. then you'll continue to Jaipur enroute an visit to Fatehpur Sikri. Jaipur where you can enjoy  Elephant / Jeep ride in Jaipur and visit to the massive forts & palaces. Ending your tour in the energetic capital of Delhi.

days.title: New Delhi
days.start_point: New Delhi, Delhi, India (Airport, Railway Station, Hotel)
days.description: You'll land at New Delhi airport where someone from the tour company meets you and takes you to your hotel. The afternoon and evening are free, so you can rest up after your flight and get settled into your room.

days.title: New Delhi
included: Full day guided tour of New Delhi
Cycle rickshaw ride at Chandni Chowk spice market
days.meals: Breakfast, Lunch (Lunch at Delhi local city restaurant)
days.description: Following breakfast, you're on a full day guided tour covering both New Delhi and Old Delhi. Start with Qutub Minar, then move to Lotus Temple, Humayun's Tomb, and pass by Rashtrapati Bhavan and India Gate. After lunch, head into Old Delhi to see Raj Ghat, Jama Masjid, and Red Fort. The day wraps up with a short rickshaw ride through Chandni Chowk, where you'll see the crowded spice market and clothing shops.

days.title: New Delhi to Agra
included: Visit Agra Fort (Moti Masjid, Octagonal Tower, Jahangir Palace, Diwan-I-Aam, Diwan-I-Khas)
days.description: After breakfast, you drive to Agra (220 kms, about 3.5 hours), stopping along the way to visit Sikandra Fort. Once you reach Agra and check in, you'll have time to rest. Later in the afternoon, your guide takes you to Agra Fort with its various palaces and structures, then Itmad-ud-Daulah's Tomb and Jama Masjid.

days.title: Agra - Fatehpur Sikri - Jaipur
included: Battery car ride at Fatehpur Sikri
days.description: Very early, before breakfast, you head out to watch the sun rise over the Taj Mahal and explore Mehtab Bagh. Back at your hotel, you'll have breakfast and check out, then drive toward Jaipur (238 kms, around 5 hours). On the way, you stop at Fatehpur Sikri, a red-stone city built in 1571 that's been abandoned. There you'll see the Tomb of Salim Chisti, Buland Darwaza, Diwane e Khas, and Panch Mahal. You reach Jaipur by evening and check into your hotel.

days.title: Jaipur
included: Full day guided tour of Jaipur
Elephant or Jeep ride at Amber Fort
days.description: After breakfast, you spend the full day on a guided tour of Jaipur. Start at Amber Fort and choose between an elephant or jeep ride to get around, then continue to City Palace and Jantar Mantar. You'll drive past Jal Mahal, Hawa Mahal (Palace of Winds), and Birla Temple. Once the sightseeing ends, the rest of the day is yours to shop or relax back at your hotel.

days.title: Jaipur to New Delhi
days.description: You have breakfast and check out, then drive back to New Delhi (275 kms, approximately 5.5 hours). Along the way, you stop at the Rail Museum in Rewari for tea and coffee snacks. After you reach New Delhi and check in, the evening is free for you to relax and settle in.

days.title: New Delhi
days.description: Following breakfast and checkout, you're transferred to New Delhi airport for your flight home.
